text: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Abu Sabit, from hanan Bin Sudeyr, from Ibn Abu Yafour, from Is’haq who said, ‘A slave of Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws died. Heasws said: ‘Look around, can you find an inheritor for him?’ So it was said to himasws, ‘There are two daughters for him at Al-Yamama, both slaves’. So heasws bought them both from the wealth of the deceased, then handed over to them the remainder of the wealth’. Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Sabit - similar to it.

citation.arabic_text: مَاتَ مَوْلًى لِعَلِيِّ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ انْظُرُوا هَلْ تَجِدُونَ لَهُ وَارِثاً فَقِيلَ لَهُ ابْنَتَانِ بِالْيَمَامَةِ مَمْلُوكَتَانِ فَاشْتَرَاهُمَا مِنْ مَالِ الْمَيِّتِ ثُمَّ دَفَعَ إِلَيْهِمَا بَقِيَّةَ الْمَالِ . عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ أَبِي ثَابِتٍ مِثْلَهُ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a house which fell upon a people who had gathered (and they all died). So it was not known which one of them died first’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They would inherit from each other’. I said, ‘But Abu Haneefa has included something in it’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And what has he included?’ I said, ‘Two men, brother, one of them was my slave and the other was a slave of another man. For one of them was a hundred thousand Dirham, and the other one, there was nothing for him. They both sailed in the ship, so they drowned. So it was not know which of the two died first. The wealth is for the inheritors of the one who had nothing for him, and nothing will be for the inheritors of the one who had the wealth’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He (Abu Haneefa) has heard it (the answer), and it is like this’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ بَيْتٍ وَقَعَ عَلَى قَوْمٍ مُجْتَمِعِينَ فَلَا يُدْرَى أَيُّهُمْ مَاتَ قَبْلُ قَالَ فَقَالَ يُوَرَّثُ بَعْضُهُمْ مِنْ بَعْضٍ قُلْتُ فَإِنَّ أَبَا حَنِيفَةَ أَدْخَلَ فِيهَا شَيْئاً قَالَ وَ مَا أَدْخَلَ قُلْتُ رَجُلَيْنِ أَخَوَيْنِ أَحَدُهُمَا مَوْلَايَ وَ الْآخَرُ مَوْلًى لِرَجُلٍ لِأَحَدِهِمَا مِائَةُ أَلْفِ دِرْهَمٍ وَ الْآخَرُ لَيْسَ لَهُ شَيْ‏ءٌ رَكِبَا فِي السَّفِينَةِ فَغَرِقَا فَلَمْ يُدْرَ أَيُّهُمَا مَاتَ أَوَّلًا كَانَ الْمَالُ لِوَرَثَةِ الَّذِي لَيْسَ لَهُ شَيْ‏ءٌ وَ لَمْ يَكُنْ لِوَرَثَةِ الَّذِي لَهُ الْمَالُ شَيْ‏ءٌ قَالَ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) لَقَدْ سَمِعَهَا وَ هُوَ هَكَذَا.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjan, and Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, (The narrator says) ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, (about the case of) a man and a woman, upon whom the house had collapsed, so they both died’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The man would inherit from the woman, and the woman would inherit from the man’. I said, ‘But Abu Haneefa has included something upon them with regards to this’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And which thing has he included upon them?’ I said, ‘Two men, brothers, non-Arabs, not having any inheritor except their two masters. One of them had a hundred thousand Dirhams, well known, and the other there was nothing for him. They both sailed in a ship, so it drowned. So the one hundred Dirhams were extracted. What should be done with it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It should be handed over to the master of the one who had nothing’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> do not deny what he has included in it as true, and it is like this’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Hand over the wealth to the master of the one who had nothing, and there would not be anything for the man who had wealth, to be inherited by the other master. So there is nothing for his inheritors’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged at Al-Yemen regarding one people upon whom a house of theirs had collapsed. So there remained two young children, one of them being a slave, the other a free one. So he<sup>asws</sup> drew lots between the two of them, so the lot came upon one of the two, so he<sup>asws</sup> made the wealth to be for him, and emancipated (liberated) the other one’.

citation.arabic_text: قَضَى أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) بِالْيَمَنِ فِي قَوْمٍ انْهَدَمَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ دَارٌ لَهُمْ فَبَقِيَ مِنْهُمْ صَبِيَّانِ أَحَدُهُمَا مَمْلُوكٌ وَ الْآخَرُ حُرٌّ فَأَسْهَمَ بَيْنَهُمَا فَخَرَجَ السَّهْمُ عَلَى أَحَدِهِمَا فَجَعَلَ الْمَالَ لَهُ وَ أَعْتَقَ الْآخَرَ .

text: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> regard the mam, a house collapsed upon him and his wife. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The woman would inherit from the man, and the man would inherit from the woman. Its meaning is, they would inherit each other from the origins of their wealth, they would not be inheriting anything from what they would have (already) inherited from each other’.

citation.arabic_text: الرَّجُلِ يَسْقُطُ عَلَيْهِ وَ عَلَى امْرَأَتِهِ بَيْتٌ قَالَ تُوَرَّثُ الْمَرْأَةُ مِنَ الرَّجُلِ وَ الرَّجُلُ مِنَ الْمَرْأَةِ مَعْنَاهُ يُوَرَّثُ بَعْضُهُمْ مِنْ بَعْضٍ مِنْ صُلْبِ أَمْوَالِهِمْ لَا يَرِثُونَ مِمَّا يُورَثُ بَعْضُهُمْ مِنْ بَعْضٍ شَيْئاً .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, raising it, said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding a man and a woman who both died together in the plague. They both died upon one bed, and the hand and the leg of the man were found upon the woman. So he<sup>asws</sup> made the inheritance to be for the man and said: ‘He died after her’.

citation.arabic_text: رَجُلٍ وَ امْرَأَةٍ مَاتَا جَمِيعاً فِي الطَّاعُونِ مَاتَا عَلَى فِرَاشٍ وَاحِدٍ وَ يَدُ الرَّجُلِ وَ رِجْلُهُ عَلَى الْمَرْأَةِ فَجَعَلَ الْمِيرَاثَ لِلرَّجُلِ وَ قَالَ إِنَّهُ مَاتَ بَعْدَهَا .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, raising it, said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding a man and a woman who both died together in the plague. They both died upon one bed, and the hand and the leg of the man were found upon the woman. So he<sup>asws</sup> made the inheritance to be for the man and said: ‘He died after her’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (3/205)

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Al Mukhtar who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to Abu Haneefa: ‘O Abu Haneefa! What are you saying regard a house which fell upon a group of people, and there remained two children from them, one of the free and the other one a slave of his companion, but the free is not recognised from the slave?’ So Abu Haneefa said, ‘Half of this should be liberated, and half of this, and the wealth be distributed between the two of them’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not like that, but a lot be drawn between the two of them, so the one who is hit by the lot, so he would be free, and this one be liberated, so he is made to be a master of his’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) لِأَبِي حَنِيفَةَ يَا أَبَا حَنِيفَةَ مَا تَقُولُ فِي بَيْتٍ سَقَطَ عَلَى قَوْمٍ وَ بَقِيَ مِنْهُمْ صَبِيَّانِ أَحَدُهُمَا حُرٌّ وَ الْآخَرُ مَمْلُوكٌ لِصَاحِبِهِ فَلَمْ يُعْرَفِ الْحُرُّ مِنَ الْمَمْلُوكِ فَقَالَ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ يُعْتَقُ نِصْفُ هَذَا وَ يُعْتَقُ نِصْفُ هَذَا وَ يُقْسَمُ الْمَالُ بَيْنَهُمَا فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) لَيْسَ كَذَلِكَ وَ لَكِنَّهُ يُقْرَعُ بَيْنَهُمَا فَمَنْ أَصَابَتْهُ الْقُرْعَةُ فَهُوَ حُرٌّ وَ يُعْتَقُ هَذَا فَيُجْعَلُ مَوْلًى لَهُ .

What are you saying regard a house which fell upon a group of people, and there remained two children from them, one of the free and the other one a slave of his companion, but the free is not recognised from the slave?’ So Abu Haneefa said, ‘Half of this should be liberated, and half of this, and the wealth be distributed between the two of them’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not like that, but a lot be drawn between the two of them, so the one who is hit by the lot, so he would be free, and this one be liberated, so he is made to be a master of his’.

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Dawood Bin Al Husayn, from Abu Al Abbas, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Is there anything for the brothers from the mother from the wergild?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.

citation.arabic_text: عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ الْحُصَيْنِ عَنْ أَبِي الْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ سَأَلْتُهُ هَلْ لِلْإِخْوَةِ مِنَ الْأُمِّ مِنَ الدِّيَةِ شَيْ‏ءٌ قَالَ لَا .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Dawood Bin Al Husayn, from Abu Al Abbas, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Is there anything for the brothers from the mother from the wergild?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Sawwar, from Al Hassan who said, ‘When Ali<sup>asws</sup> defeated Talha and Al-Zubeyr, the people faced their defeat, so they passed by a pregnant woman upon the road. So she panicked from them, and gave birth to what was in her belly, alive. So it (child) became restless until it died. Then its mother died from after it. So Ali<sup>asws</sup> and his companions passed by her and she and her child were lying upon the road. So he<sup>asws</sup> told them about her matter, so they said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘But rather, she was pregnant, so she panicked when she saw the fighting and the defeat’. So he<sup>asws</sup> asked them, ‘Which of the two died before its companion?’ So it was said, ‘Her son died before her’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So he<sup>asws</sup> called her husband, father of the dead boy, so made him to inherit from his son, two-thirds of the wergild (blood money compensation), and her mother to inherit a third of the wergild. Then made the husband to inherit from his dead wife, half of the one-third wergild which she had inherited from her son, and made the relatives of the dead woman, the remainder (of the one-third wergild). Then made the husband to inherit as well from the wergild of the dead woman, half of the wergild, and it was two thousand and five hundred Dirhams, and made the relatives of the dead woman to inherit half of the wergild, and it was two thousand and five hundred Dirhams, and that is because there did not happen to be for her any child other than that which had been miscarried with when she panicked. He (the narrator) said, ‘And he<sup>asws</sup> paid all of that from the Public Treasury of Al-Basra’.

citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ عَلِيّاً ( عليه السلام ) لَمَّا هَزَمَ طَلْحَةَ وَ الزُّبَيْرَ أَقْبَلَ النَّاسُ مُنْهَزِمِينَ فَمَرُّوا بِامْرَأَةٍ حَامِلٍ عَلَى الطَّرِيقِ فَفَزِعَتْ مِنْهُمْ فَطَرَحَتْ مَا فِي بَطْنِهَا حَيّاً فَاضْطَرَبَ حَتَّى مَاتَ ثُمَّ مَاتَتْ أُمُّهُ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ فَمَرَّ بِهَا عَلِيٌّ ( عليه السلام ) وَ أَصْحَابُهُ وَ هِيَ مَطْرُوحَةٌ وَ وَلَدُهَا عَلَى الطَّرِيقِ فَسَأَلَهُمْ عَنْ أَمْرِهَا فَقَالُوا لَهُ إِنَّهَا كَانَتْ حُبْلَى فَفَزِعَتْ حِينَ رَأَتِ الْقِتَالَ وَ الْهَزِيمَةَ قَالَ فَسَأَلَهُمْ أَيُّهُمَا مَاتَ قَبْلَ صَاحِبِهِ فَقِيلَ إِنَّ ابْنَهَا مَاتَ قَبْلَهَا قَالَ فَدَعَا بِزَوْجِهَا أَبِي الْغُلَامِ الْمَيِّتِ فَوَرَّثَهُ مِنِ ابْنِهِ ثُلُثَيِ الدِّيَةِ وَ وَرَّثَ أُمَّهُ ثُلُثَ الدِّيَةِ ثُمَّ وَرَّثَ الزَّوْجَ مِنِ امْرَأَتِهِ الْمَيِّتَةِ نِصْفَ ثُلُثِ الدِّيَةِ الَّذِي وَرِثَتْهُ مِنِ ابْنِهَا وَ وَرَّثَ قَرَابَةَ الْمَرْأَةِ الْمَيِّتَةِ الْبَاقِيَ ثُمَّ وَرَّثَ الزَّوْجَ أَيْضاً مِنْ دِيَةِ امْرَأَتِهِ الْمَيِّتَةِ نِصْفَ الدِّيَةِ وَ هُوَ أَلْفَانِ وَ خَمْسُمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ وَ وَرَّثَ قَرَابَةَ الْمَرْأَةِ الْمَيِّتَةِ نِصْفَ الدِّيَةِ وَ هُوَ أَلْفَانِ وَ خَمْسُمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ وَ ذَلِكَ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهَا وَلَدٌ غَيْرُ الَّذِي رَمَتْ بِهِ حِينَ فَزِعَتْ قَالَ وَ أَدَّى ذَلِكَ كُلَّهُ مِنْ بَيْتِ مَالِ الْبَصْرَةِ .

text: Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Suleyman Bin Khalid, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged with regards to a wergild of the murdered that the inheritors would inherit the inheritance upon the the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and their (legislated) shares, if there does not happen to be a debt upon the murdered, except for the brothers and the sisters from the mother, so they would not be inheriting anything from his wergild’.

citation.arabic_text: قَضَى أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) فِي دِيَةِ الْمَقْتُولِ أَنَّهُ يَرِثُهَا الْوَرَثَةُ عَلَى كِتَابِ اللَّهِ وَ سِهَامِهِمْ إِذَا لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَى الْمَقْتُولِ دَيْنٌ إِلَّا الْإِخْوَةَ وَ الْأَخَوَاتِ مِنَ الْأُمِّ فَإِنَّهُمْ لَا يَرِثُونَ مِنْ دِيَتِهِ شَيْئاً .

text: Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged that the wergild, the inheritors would inherit it except for the brothers and the sisters from the mother’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The wergild, the inheritors would inherit it upon the Obligated inheritances except the brothers from the mother, so they would not be inheriting anything from the wergild’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ الدِّيَةُ يَرِثُهَا الْوَرَثَةُ عَلَى فَرَائِضِ الْمَوَارِيثِ إِلَّا الْإِخْوَةَ مِنَ الْأُمِّ فَإِنَّهُمْ لَا يَرِثُونَ مِنَ الدِّيَةِ شَيْئاً .

text: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from Abdullah Bin Jabala and Ali Bin Rabat, from Abdullah Bin Bukeyr, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The brothers from the mother do not inherit anything from the wergild’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا يَرِثُ الْإِخْوَةُ مِنَ الْأُمِّ مِنَ الدِّيَةِ شَيْئاً .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (3/207)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Noman, from Yahys Al Azraq who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who was murdered and left debts, and there was not wealth for him. So his guardians took the wergild. Is it upon them to pay off his debts?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’. I said, ‘And if he had not left anything?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. But rather, they took the wergild, therefore it is upon them that they pay off his debts’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُقْتَلُ وَ يَتْرُكُ دَيْناً وَ لَيْسَ لَهُ مَالٌ فَيَأْخُذُ أَوْلِيَاؤُهُ الدِّيَةَ أَ عَلَيْهِمْ أَنْ يَقْضُوا دَيْنَهُ قَالَ نَعَمْ قُلْتُ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَتْرُكْ شَيْئاً قَالَ نَعَمْ إِنَّمَا أَخَذُوا دِيَتَهُ فَعَلَيْهِمْ أَنْ يَقْضُوا دَيْنَهُ .

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Dawood Bin Al Husayn, from Abu Al Abbas, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Is there anything for the brothers from the mother from the wergild?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdullah Bin Abu Yafour who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Is there anything for the woman from the wergild of her husband, and is there anything for the man from the wergild of his wife?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, so long as one of the two has not killed the other’.

citation.arabic_text: الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُعَلَّى بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ قَالَ قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) هَلْ لِلْمَرْأَةِ مِنْ دِيَةِ زَوْجِهَا وَ هَلْ لِلرَّجُلِ مِنْ دِيَةِ امْرَأَتِهِ شَيْ‏ءٌ قَالَ نَعَمْ مَا لَمْ يَقْتُلْ أَحَدُهُمَا الْآخَرَ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdullah Bin Abu Yafour who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Is there anything for the woman from the wergild of her husband, and is there anything for the man from the wergild of his wife?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, so long as one of the two has not killed the other’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘When the man kills his father, he would be killed due to it, and if his father kills him he (father) would not be killed due to it, and he would not inherit him’.

citation.arabic_text: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ الْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ إِذَا قَتَلَ الرَّجُلُ أَبَاهُ قُتِلَ بِهِ وَ إِنْ قَتَلَهُ أَبُوهُ لَمْ يُقْتَلْ بِهِ وَ لَمْ يَرِثْهُ
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘When the man kills his father, he would be killed due to it, and if his father kills him he (father) would not be killed due to it, and he would not inherit him’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The two men would not inherit when one of them has killed his companion’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا يَتَوَارَثُ رَجُلَانِ قَتَلَ أَحَدُهُمَا صَاحِبَهُ .

text: Ahmad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who killed his mother, would he inherit her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> heard my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Whichever man with relationship kills his relative, would not inherit from him (the one who has been killed)’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ رَجُلٍ قَتَلَ أُمَّهُ أَ يَرِثُهَا قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبِي ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ أَيُّمَا رَجُلٍ ذُو رَحِمٍ قَتَلَ قَرِيبَهُ لَمْ يَرِثْهُ .
citation.translation: Ahmad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who killed his mother, would he inherit her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> heard my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Whichever man with relationship kills his relative, would not inherit from him (the one who has been killed)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مجهول - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (23/208)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Hadeed, altogether from Jameel Bin Darraj, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘The man would not inherit when he kills his child, or his parent, but the inheritance would happen to be for the inheritors of the killer’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا يَرِثُ الرَّجُلُ إِذَا قَتَلَ وَلَدَهُ أَوْ وَالِدَهُ وَ لَكِنْ يَكُونُ الْمِيرَاثُ لِوَرَثَةِ الْقَاتِلِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Hadeed, altogether from Jameel Bin Darraj, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘The man would not inherit when he kills his child, or his parent, but the inheritance would happen to be for the inheritors of the killer’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن كالصحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (3/208)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubeyda, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws regarding a man who killed his mother. Heasws said: ‘He would not inherit her, and he would be killed humiliatingly due to it, and Iasws do not think that his being killed due to it is an expiation (kaffara) for his sin’.

citation.arabic_text: رَجُلٍ قَتَلَ أُمَّهُ قَالَ لَا يَرِثُهَا وَ يُقْتَلُ بِهَا صَاغِراً وَ لَا أَظُنُّ قَتْلَهُ بِهَا كَفَّارَةً لِذَنْبِهِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubeyda, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws regarding a man who killed his mother. Heasws said: ‘He would not inherit her, and he would be killed humiliatingly due to it, and Iasws do not think that his being killed due to it is an expiation (kaffara) for his sin’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (23/208)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad and Abdullah, two sons of Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘There is no inheritance for the killer’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لَا مِيرَاثَ لِلْقَاتِلِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad and Abdullah, two sons of Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘There is no inheritance for the killer’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (23/208)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubeyda who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about a woman who drank medicine and she was pregnant, and her husband did not know of that. So her child miscarried. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If there were bones for him (the child), and the flesh had grown upon him, the wergild is upon her to submit it to its father. However, if she miscarried a clot or lump (unformed), so upon her would be forty Dinars, or a slave to be paid to its father’. I said, ‘Would she not inherit the wergild of her child along with its father?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, because she killed it, so she would not inherit’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ امْرَأَةٍ شَرِبَتْ دَوَاءً وَ هِيَ حَامِلٌ وَ لَمْ يَعْلَمْ بِذَلِكَ زَوْجُهَا فَأَلْقَتْ وَلَدَهَا قَالَ فَقَالَ إِنْ كَانَ لَهُ عَظْمٌ وَ قَدْ نَبَتَ عَلَيْهِ اللَّحْمُ عَلَيْهَا دِيَةٌ تُسَلِّمُهَا لِأَبِيهِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ حِينَ طَرَحَتْهُ عَلَقَةً أَوْ مُضْغَةً فَإِنَّ عَلَيْهَا أَرْبَعِينَ دِينَاراً أَوْ غُرَّةً تُؤَدِّيهَا إِلَى أَبِيهِ قُلْتُ لَهُ فَهِيَ لَا تَرِثُ وَلَدَهَا مِنْ دِيَتِهِ مَعَ أَبِيهِ قَالَ لَا لِأَنَّهَا قَتَلَتْهُ فَلَا تَرِثُهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubeyda who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about a woman who drank medicine and she was pregnant, and her husband did not know of that. So her child miscarried. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If there were bones for him (the child), and the flesh had grown upon him, the wergild is upon her to submit it to its father. However, if she miscarried a clot or lump (unformed), so upon her would be forty Dinars, or a slave to be paid to its father’. I said, ‘Would she not inherit the wergild of her child along with its father?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, because she killed it, so she would not inherit’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (3/209)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Fuzayl Bin Yasaar, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The man would not be killed if he were to kill his child, but the child would be killed if he were to kill his parent and he would not inherit his father if he kills him, even though it may be in error’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا يُقْتَلُ الرَّجُلُ بِوَلَدِهِ إِذَا قَتَلَهُ وَ يُقْتَلُ الْوَلَدُ بِوَالِدِهِ إِذَا قَتَلَ وَالِدَهُ وَ لَا يَرِثُ الرَّجُلُ أَبَاهُ إِذَا قَتَلَهُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ خَطَأً .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Fuzayl Bin Yasaar, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The man would not be killed if he were to kill his child, but the child would be killed if he were to kill his parent and he would not inherit his father if he kills him, even though it may be in error’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (23/209)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The woman would inherit from the wergild of her husband, and he would inherit from her wergild, so long as one of the two has not killed his partner’.

citation.arabic_text: الْمَرْأَةُ تَرِثُ مِنْ دِيَةِ زَوْجِهَا وَ يَرِثُ مِنْ دِيَتِهَا مَا لَمْ يَقْتُلْ أَحَدُهُمَا صَاحِبَهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The woman would inherit from the wergild of her husband, and he would inherit from her wergild, so long as one of the two has not killed his partner’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (3/209)

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdullah Bin Abu Yafour who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Is there anything for the woman from the wergild of her husband, and is there anything for the man from the wergild of his wife?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, so long as one of the two has not killed the other’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) هَلْ لِلْمَرْأَةِ مِنْ دِيَةِ زَوْجِهَا وَ هَلْ لِلرَّجُلِ مِنْ دِيَةِ امْرَأَتِهِ شَيْ‏ءٌ قَالَ نَعَمْ مَا لَمْ يَقْتُلْ أَحَدُهُمَا الْآخَرَ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdullah Bin Abu Yafour who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Is there anything for the woman from the wergild of her husband, and is there anything for the man from the wergild of his wife?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, so long as one of the two has not killed the other’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (3/209)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘When the man kills his father, he would be killed due to it, and if his father kills him he (father) would not be killed due to it, and he would not inherit him’.

citation.arabic_text: إِذَا قَتَلَ الرَّجُلُ أَبَاهُ قُتِلَ بِهِ وَ إِنْ قَتَلَهُ أَبُوهُ لَمْ يُقْتَلْ بِهِ وَ لَمْ يَرِثْهُ
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘When the man kills his father, he would be killed due to it, and if his father kills him he (father) would not be killed due to it, and he would not inherit him’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (23/210)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel and Hisham, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said regarding what the people are reporting from the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> having said: ‘The people of the two Religions do not inherit (each other)’, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘We inherit them and they do not inherit us, because Al-Islam did not increase in his favour except for the harshness’.

citation.arabic_text: فِيمَا رَوَى النَّاسُ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أَنَّهُ قَالَ لَا يَتَوَارَثُ أَهْلُ مِلَّتَيْنِ فَقَالَ نَرِثُهُمْ وَ لَا يَرِثُونَّا لِأَنَّ الْإِسْلَامَ لَمْ يَزِدْهُ فِي حَقِّهِ إِلَّا شِدَّةً .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel and Hisham, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said regarding what the people are reporting from the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> having said: ‘The people of the two Religions do not inherit (each other)’, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘We inherit them and they do not inherit us, because Al-Islam did not increase in his favour except for the harshness’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (23/212)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays who said, ‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Neither the Jew nor the Christian would inherit the Muslim, but the Muslim would inherit the Jew and the Christian’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ لَا يَرِثُ الْيَهُودِيُّ وَ لَا النَّصْرَانِيُّ الْمُسْلِمَ وَ يَرِثُ الْمُسْلِمُ الْيَهُودِيَّ وَ النَّصْرَانِيَّ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays who said, ‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Neither the Jew nor the Christian would inherit the Muslim, but the Muslim would inherit the Jew and the Christian’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (3/212)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Zurara, from Sama’at who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the Muslim man, would he inherit the Polytheist?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, but the Polytheist would not inherit the Muslim’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الرَّجُلِ الْمُسْلِمِ هَلْ يَرِثُ الْمُشْرِكَ قَالَ نَعَمْ وَ لَا يَرِثُ الْمُشْرِكُ الْمُسْلِمَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Zurara, from Sama’at who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the Muslim man, would he inherit the Polytheist?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, but the Polytheist would not inherit the Muslim’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (23/213)

text: From him, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Abdullah Bin Ayn who said, ‘I said to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! The Christian died and for him was a Muslim son, would he inherit him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic did not Increase with Al-Islam except for honour, so we inherit them, but they do not inherit us’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ النَّصْرَانِيُّ يَمُوتُ وَ لَهُ ابْنٌ مُسْلِمٌ أَ يَرِثُهُ قَالَ فَقَالَ نَعَمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ لَمْ يَزِدْهُ بِالْإِسْلَامِ إِلَّا عِزّاً فَنَحْنُ نَرِثُهُمْ وَ لَا يَرِثُونَّا .
citation.translation: From him, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Abdullah Bin Ayn who said, ‘I said to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! The Christian died and for him was a Muslim son, would he inherit him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic did not Increase with Al-Islam except for honour, so we inherit them, but they do not inherit us’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف على المشهور - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (23/213)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al Hassan Bin Salih, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The Muslim blocks the infidel and inherits him, but the infidel does not block the Believer and does not inherit him’.

citation.arabic_text: الْمُسْلِمُ يَحْجُبُ الْكَافِرَ وَ يَرِثُهُ وَ الْكَافِرُ لَا يَحْجُبُ الْمُؤْمِنَ وَ لَا يَرِثُهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al Hassan Bin Salih, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The Muslim blocks the infidel and inherits him, but the infidel does not block the Believer and does not inherit him’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: ضعيف - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (23/213)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallaad who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘The Muslim inherits his ‘Zimmi’ wife (Jew or a Christian under the protection of Islam), but she does not inherit him’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ الْمُسْلِمُ يَرِثُ امْرَأَتَهُ الذِّمِّيَّةَ وَ لَا تَرِثُهُ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (3/213)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, altogether from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Malik Bin Ayn, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a Christian who died and for him was a son of his Muslim brother, and a son of a Muslim sister, and for the Christian were children and a Christian wife. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> see that you should give the son of his brother two-thirds of what is left (as legacy), and give the son of his sister a third of what is left, if there does not happen to be young children for him. So if there were small children for him, so it would be upon the two inheritors that they should spent upon the small children from what they both had inherited from their father, until they mature’. It was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘How should the two of them be spending?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The inheritor of the two thirds of the inheritance should take out two thirds of the expenses, and the inheritor of the one-third of the inheritance should take out a one-third of the expenses about them’. It was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, so if the children become Muslim and they are still young?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Hand over to the Imam<sup>asws</sup> whatever their father had left until they grow up. So if they remain upon Al-Islam, the Imam<sup>asws</sup> hands over their inheritance to them, but if they do not remain upon Al-Islam when they mature, the Imam<sup>asws</sup> hands over their inheritance to the son of his brother, and the son of his sister, the two Muslim. To the son of the brother two-thirds would be handed over, and to the son of the sister, a one-third of whatever was left (as legacy)’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ نَصْرَانِيٍّ مَاتَ وَ لَهُ ابْنُ أَخٍ مُسْلِمٌ وَ ابْنُ أُخْتٍ مُسْلِمٌ وَ لِلنَّصْرَانِيِّ أَوْلَادٌ وَ زَوْجَةٌ نَصَارَى قَالَ فَقَالَ أَرَى أَنْ يُعْطَى ابْنُ أَخِيهِ الْمُسْلِمُ ثُلُثَيْ مَا تَرَكَ وَ يُعْطَى ابْنُ أُخْتِهِ ثُلُثَ مَا تَرَكَ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ وُلْدٌ صِغَارٌ فَإِنْ كَانَ لَهُ وُلْدٌ صِغَارٌ فَإِنَّ عَلَى الْوَارِثَيْنِ أَنْ يُنْفِقَا عَلَى الصِّغَارِ مِمَّا وَرِثَا مِنْ أَبِيهِمْ حَتَّى يُدْرِكُوا قِيلَ لَهُ كَيْفَ يُنْفِقَانِ قَالَ فَقَالَ يُخْرِجُ وَارِثُ الثُّلُثَيْنِ ثُلُثَيِ النَّفَقَةِ وَ يُخْرِجُ وَارِثُ الثُّلُثِ ثُلُثَ النَّفَقَةِ فَإِنْ أَدْرَكُوا قَطَعَا النَّفَقَةَ عَنْهُمْ قِيلَ لَهُ فَإِنْ أَسْلَمَ الْأَوْلَادُ وَ هُمْ صِغَارٌ قَالَ فَقَالَ يُدْفَعُ مَا تَرَكَ أَبُوهُمْ إِلَى الْإِمَامِ حَتَّى يُدْرِكُوا فَإِنْ بَقُوا عَلَى الْإِسْلَامِ دَفَعَ الْإِمَامُ مِيرَاثَهُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَبْقَوْا عَلَى الْإِسْلَامِ إِذَا أَدْرَكُوا دَفَعَ الْإِمَامُ مِيرَاثَهُ إِلَى ابْنِ أَخِيهِ وَ ابْنِ أُخْتِهِ الْمُسْلِمَيْنِ يَدْفَعُ إِلَى ابْنِ أَخِيهِ ثُلُثَيْ مَا تَرَكَ وَ يَدْفَعُ إِلَى ابْنِ أُخْتِهِ ثُلُثَ مَا تَرَكَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, altogether from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Malik Bin Ayn, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a Christian who died and for him was a son of his Muslim brother, and a son of a Muslim sister, and for the Christian were children and a Christian wife. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> see that you should give the son of his brother two-thirds of what is left (as legacy), and give the son of his sister a third of what is left, if there does not happen to be young children for him. So if there were small children for him, so it would be upon the two inheritors that they should spent upon the small children from what they both had inherited from their father, until they mature’. It was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘How should the two of them be spending?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The inheritor of the two thirds of the inheritance should take out two thirds of the expenses, and the inheritor of the one-third of the inheritance should take out a one-third of the expenses about them’. It was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, so if the children become Muslim and they are still young?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Hand over to the Imam<sup>asws</sup> whatever their father had left until they grow up. So if they remain upon Al-Islam, the Imam<sup>asws</sup> hands over their inheritance to them, but if they do not remain upon Al-Islam when they mature, the Imam<sup>asws</sup> hands over their inheritance to the son of his brother, and the son of his sister, the two Muslim. To the son of the brother two-thirds would be handed over, and to the son of the sister, a one-third of whatever was left (as legacy)’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (3/213)

text: Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a Muslim man who died and for him was a Christian mother, and for him was a Muslim wife and a Muslim child. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the mother becomes a Muslim before the distribution of his inheritance, give her the one-sixth’. I said, ‘So if there did not happen to be a wife for him nor a child, nor any inheritor for him from the Muslims, with a legislated share in the Book (Quran), and his mother is a Christian, and for him are Christian relatives, from the ones who dont have for them a legislated share in the Book had they been Muslims. For whom would the inheritance be?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the mother becomes a Muslim, then the entirety of the inheritance is for her, and if his mother does not become a Muslim, and some of his relatives become Muslim, from the ones who have a legislated share in the Book, so the inheritance would be for him. And if no one from his relatives becomes Muslim, so his inheritance is for the Imam<sup>asws</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ مُسْلِمٍ مَاتَ وَ لَهُ أُمٌّ نَصْرَانِيَّةٌ وَ لَهُ زَوْجَةٌ وَ وُلْدٌ مُسْلِمُونَ قَالَ فَقَالَ إِنْ أَسْلَمَتْ أُمُّهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُقْسَمَ مِيرَاثُهُ أُعْطِيَتِ السُّدُسَ قُلْتُ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ امْرَأَةٌ وَ لَا وُلْدٌ وَ لَا وَارِثٌ لَهُ سَهْمٌ فِي الْكِتَابِ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَ أُمُّهُ نَصْرَانِيَّةٌ وَ لَهُ قَرَابَةٌ نَصَارَى مِمَّنْ لَهُ سَهْمٌ فِي الْكِتَابِ لَوْ كَانُوا مُسْلِمِينَ لِمَنْ يَكُونُ مِيرَاثُهُ قَالَ إِنْ أَسْلَمَتْ أُمُّهُ فَإِنَّ جَمِيعَ مِيرَاثِهِ لَهَا وَ إِنْ لَمْ تُسْلِمْ أُمُّهُ وَ أَسْلَمَ بَعْضُ قَرَابَتِهِ مِمَّنْ لَهُ سَهْمٌ فِي الْكِتَابِ فَإِنَّ مِيرَاثَهُ لَهُ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يُسْلِمْ مِنْ قَرَابَتِهِ أَحَدٌ فَإِنَّ مِيرَاثَهُ لِلْإِمَامِ .

For whom would the inheritance be?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the mother becomes a Muslim, then the entirety of the inheritance is for her, and if his mother does not become a Muslim, and some of his relatives become Muslim, from the ones who have a legislated share in the Book, so the inheritance would be for him. text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who becomes a Muslim upon an inheritance before the distribution, so for him is his inheritance, and if he becomes a Muslim after the distribution, so there is no inheritance for him’.

citation.arabic_text: مَنْ أَسْلَمَ عَلَى مِيرَاثٍ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُقْسَمَ فَلَهُ مِيرَاثُهُ وَ إِنْ أَسْلَمَ بَعْدَ مَا قُسِمَ فَلَا مِيرَاثَ لَهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who becomes a Muslim upon an inheritance before the distribution, so for him is his inheritance, and if he becomes a Muslim after the distribution, so there is no inheritance for him’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (23/216)

text: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Aban Al Ahmar, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘The one who becomes a Muslim upon an inheritance before the distribution of the inheritance, so it is for him; but the one who becomes a Muslim after the distribution, so there is no inheritance for him; and the one who is emancipated (liberated) upon an inheritance before the distribution of the inheritance, so it is for him; and the one who is emancipated (liberated) after the distribution, so there is no inheritance for him’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said regarding the woman: ‘If she becomes a Muslim before the distribution of the inheritance, so for her is the inheritance’.

citation.arabic_text: مَنْ أَسْلَمَ عَلَى مِيرَاثٍ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُقْسَمَ الْمِيرَاثُ فَهُوَ لَهُ وَ مَنْ أَسْلَمَ بَعْدَ مَا قُسِمَ فَلَا مِيرَاثَ لَهُ وَ مَنْ أُعْتِقَ عَلَى مِيرَاثٍ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُقْسَمَ الْمَوَارِيثُ فَهُوَ لَهُ وَ مَنْ أُعْتِقَ بَعْدَ مَا قُسِمَ فَلَا مِيرَاثَ لَهُ وَ قَالَ فِي الْمَرْأَةِ إِذَا أَسْلَمَتْ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُقْسَمَ الْمِيرَاثُ فَلَهَا الْمِيرَاثُ .
citation.translation: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Aban Al Ahmar, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘The one who becomes a Muslim upon an inheritance before the distribution of the inheritance, so it is for him; but the one who becomes a Muslim after the distribution, so there is no inheritance for him; and the one who is emancipated (liberated) upon an inheritance before the distribution of the inheritance, so it is for him; and the one who is emancipated (liberated) after the distribution, so there is no inheritance for him’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said regarding the woman: ‘If she becomes a Muslim before the distribution of the inheritance, so for her is the inheritance’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن أو موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (3/216)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibb Raib, from Abu Hamza, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said that Ali<sup>asws</sup> had judged regarding the inheritances regarding the one who realised Al-Islam, from the wealth of the Polytheists which had been left undistributed before Al-Islam. He<sup>asws</sup> made for the women and the men, their shares, upon the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic and the Sunnah of His<sup>azwj</sup> Prophet<sup>saww</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ عَلِيّاً ( عليه السلام ) كَانَ يَقْضِي فِي الْمَوَارِيثِ فِيمَا أَدْرَكَ الْإِسْلَامَ مِنْ مَالِ مُشْرِكٍ تَرَكَهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ قُسِمَ قَبْلَ الْإِسْلَامِ أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَجْعَلُ لِلنِّسَاءِ وَ الرِّجَالِ حُظُوظَهُمْ مِنْهُ عَلَى كِتَابِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ وَ سُنَّةِ نَبِيِّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) .

He<sup>asws</sup> made for the women and the men, their shares, upon the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic and the Sunnah of His<sup>azwj</sup> Prophet<sup>saww</sup>’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (3/216)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasi Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding the inheritances what Al-Islam acquired from the wealth of the Polytheists which had not been distributed, so for the women were their fortunes from it’.

citation.arabic_text: قَضَى أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) فِي الْمَوَارِيثِ مَا أَدْرَكَ الْإِسْلَامَ مِنْ مَالِ مُشْرِكٍ لَمْ يُقْسَمْ فَإِنَّ لِلنِّسَاءِ حُظُوظَهُنَّ مِنْهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasi Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding the inheritances what Al-Islam acquired from the wealth of the Polytheists which had not been distributed, so for the women were their fortunes from it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (23/217)

text: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Al Taymi, from his brother Ahmad Bin Al Hassan, from his father, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Rabat, raising it, said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If a Zimmy man (Jew or a Christian under the protection) becomes a Muslim while his father is alive, and for his father are children other than him, then the father dies, the Muslim would inherit the entirety of his wealth, and his (other) children and his wife would not inherit anything along with the Muslim’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) لَوْ أَنَّ رَجُلًا ذِمِّيّاً أَسْلَمَ وَ أَبُوهُ حَيٌّ وَ لِأَبِيهِ وَلَدٌ غَيْرُهُ ثُمَّ مَاتَ الْأَبُ وَرِثَهُ الْمُسْلِمُ جَمِيعَ مَالِهِ وَ لَمْ يَرِثْهُ وَلَدُهُ وَ لَا امْرَأَتُهُ مَعَ الْمُسْلِمِ شَيْئاً .
citation.translation: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Al Taymi, from his brother Ahmad Bin Al Hassan, from his father, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Rabat, raising it, said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If a Zimmy man (Jew or a Christian under the protection) becomes a Muslim while his father is alive, and for his father are children other than him, then the father dies, the Muslim would inherit the entirety of his wealth, and his (other) children and his wife would not inherit anything along with the Muslim’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: مرفوع - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (23/219)

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from someone else, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a Jew or a Christian who dies and for him are Muslim children, and non-Muslim children, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They (Muslims) are above their (other non-Muslim) inheritors’.

citation.arabic_text: يَهُودِيٍّ أَوْ نَصْرَانِيٍّ يَمُوتُ وَ لَهُ أَوْلَادٌ مُسْلِمُونَ وَ أَوْلَادٌ غَيْرُ مُسْلِمِينَ فَقَالَ هُمْ عَلَى مَوَارِيثِهِمْ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from someone else, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a Jew or a Christian who dies and for him are Muslim children, and non-Muslim children, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They (Muslims) are above their (other non-Muslim) inheritors’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: كالحسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (3/219)

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Ibn Bukeyr, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the man dies and leaves his father and he is a slave, or his mother and she is a slave, and the deceased is a free man, his father or his relatives be bought from what is left (the legacy), and they would inherit the remainder of the wealth’.

citation.arabic_text: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنِ ابْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ إِذَا مَاتَ الرَّجُلُ وَ تَرَكَ أَبَاهُ وَ هُوَ مَمْلُوكٌ أَوْ أُمَّهُ وَ هِيَ مَمْلُوكَةٌ وَ الْمَيِّتُ حُرٌّ اشْتُرِيَ مِمَّا تَرَكَ أَبُوهُ أَوْ قَرَابَتُهُ وَ وَرِثَ مَا بَقِيَ مِنَ الْمَالِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Ibn Bukeyr, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the man dies and leaves his father and he is a slave, or his mother and she is a slave, and the deceased is a free man, his father or his relatives be bought from what is left (the legacy), and they would inherit the remainder of the wealth’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man died, and for him was a son who was a slave’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should be bought and emancipated (liberated), then the remainder of what is left to be handed over to him’.

citation.arabic_text: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ قَالَ قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) الرَّجُلُ يَمُوتُ وَ لَهُ ابْنٌ مَمْلُوكٌ قَالَ يُشْتَرَى وَ يُعْتَقُ ثُمَّ يُدْفَعُ إِلَيْهِ مَا بَقِيَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man died, and for him was a son who was a slave’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should be bought and emancipated (liberated), then the remainder of what is left to be handed over to him’.

citation.arabic_text: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ ابْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ كَانَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ فِي الرَّجُلِ الْحُرِّ يَمُوتُ وَ لَهُ أُمٌّ مَمْلُوكَةٌ قَالَ تُشْتَرَى مِنْ مَالِ ابْنِهَا ثُمَّ تُعْتَقُ ثُمَّ يُوَرِّثُهَا .

citation.arabic_text: وَ بِالْإِسْنَادِ عَنْ عَاصِمِ بْنِ حُمَيْدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ قَيْسٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) فِي مُكَاتَبٍ تُوُفِّيَ وَ لَهُ مَالٌ قَالَ يُحْسَبُ مِيرَاثُهُ عَلَى قَدْرِ مَا أُعْتِقَ مِنْهُ لِوَرَثَتِهِ وَ مَا لَمْ يُعْتَقْ مِنْهُ لِأَرْبَابِهِ الَّذِينَ كَاتَبُوهُ مِنْ مَالِهِ .

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Malik Bin Atiyya who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about a contracted man who died and had not paid off his contractual amount, and left wealth and children. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If his master, when he contracted him, had placed a condition upon him that if he was frustrated (from paying it off) a part of his deficit, so he would be returned in the slaver, and he was frustrated from paying the deficit. So whatever something he left, so it would be for his master, and his son would be returned in the slavery if there was a child of his before the contract. And if he was contracted afterwards and there was no such condition placed upon him, so his son is free, and he would pay off on behalf of his father whatever remained upon him from what his father had left. And there is nothing from the inheritance for his sons until he pays off what was upon him. So if his father had not left anything, so there is nothing upon his son’.

citation.arabic_text: عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ وَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مَالِكِ بْنِ عَطِيَّةَ قَالَ سُئِلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ رَجُلٍ مُكَاتَبٍ مَاتَ وَ لَمْ يُؤَدِّ مُكَاتَبَتَهُ وَ تَرَكَ مَالًا وَ وَلَداً قَالَ إِنْ كَانَ سَيِّدُهُ حِينَ كَاتَبَهُ اشْتَرَطَ عَلَيْهِ إِنْ عَجَزَ عَنْ نَجْمٍ مِنْ نُجُومِهِ فَهُوَ رَدٌّ فِي الرِّقِّ وَ كَانَ قَدْ عَجَزَ عَنْ نَجْمٍ فَمَا تَرَكَ مِنْ شَيْ‏ءٍ فَهُوَ لِسَيِّدِهِ وَ ابْنُهُ رَدٌّ فِي الرِّقِّ إِنْ كَانَ لَهُ وَلَدٌ قَبْلَ الْمُكَاتَبَةِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ كَاتَبَهُ بَعْدُ وَ لَمْ يَشْتَرِطْ عَلَيْهِ فَإِنَّ ابْنَهُ حُرٌّ فَيُؤَدِّي عَنْ أَبِيهِ مَا بَقِيَ عَلَيْهِ مِمَّا تَرَكَ أَبُوهُ وَ لَيْسَ لِابْنِهِ شَيْ‏ءٌ مِنَ الْمِيرَاثِ حَتَّى يُؤَدِّيَ مَا عَلَيْهِ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ أَبُوهُ تَرَكَ شَيْئاً فَلَا شَيْ‏ءَ عَلَى ابْنِهِ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby and Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a contracted man who died and had paid off some of his contracted amount, and for him was a son from his slave girl. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If there was a condition upon that if he was frustrated (from paying off his contracted amount), so he would be a slave, his son returns as a slave along with the slave girl, and if there was not such condition upon him, that which remains unpaid from his contract would be paid off by his son, and he would inherit what remains’.

citation.arabic_text: رَجُلٍ مُكَاتَبٍ يَمُوتُ وَ قَدْ أَدَّى بَعْضَ مُكَاتَبَتِهِ وَ لَهُ ابْنٌ مِنْ جَارِيَتِهِ قَالَ إِنْ كَانَ اشْتُرِطَ عَلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ إِنْ عَجَزَ فَهُوَ مَمْلُوكٌ رَجَعَ ابْنُهُ مَمْلُوكاً وَ الْجَارِيَةُ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنِ اشْتُرِطَ عَلَيْهِ ذَلِكَ أَدَّى ابْنُهُ مَا بَقِيَ مِنْ مُكَاتَبَتِهِ وَ وَرِثَ مَا بَقِيَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby and Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a contracted man who died and had paid off some of his contracted amount, and for him was a son from his slave girl. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If there was a condition upon that if he was frustrated (from paying off his contracted amount), so he would be a slave, his son returns as a slave along with the slave girl, and if there was not such condition upon him, that which remains unpaid from his contract would be paid off by his son, and he would inherit what remains’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran and Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, altogether from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> regarding a contracted man, under whom was a free wife, so she bequeathed during her death with a bequest. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The people of the inheritance do not inherit, and her bequest is not allowed for him because he is a contracted slave, yet to be emancipated (liberated), but he would not inherit’. So he<sup>asws</sup> judged that he would inherit by the calculation of whatever he had been emancipated (liberated) from it (his contract)’.

citation.arabic_text: رَجُلٍ مُكَاتَبٍ كَانَتْ تَحْتَهُ امْرَأَةٌ حُرَّةٌ فَأَوْصَتْ عِنْدَ مَوْتِهَا بِوَصِيَّةٍ فَقَالَ أَهْلُ الْمِيرَاثِ لَا يَرِثُ وَ لَا نُجِيزُ وَصِيَّتَهَا لَهُ لِأَنَّهُ مُكَاتَبٌ لَمْ يُعْتَقْ وَ لَا يَرِثُ فَقَضَى أَنَّهُ يَرِثُ بِحِسَابِ مَا أُعْتِقَ مِنْهُ .

text: And by the chain, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> regarding a contracted slave who died and for him was wealth. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘His inheritance would be calculated in accordance of what he had been emancipated (liberated) from it, to be for his inheritors, and whatever he had not been emancipated from it, is for his master who had contracted him, from his wealth’.

citation.arabic_text: مُكَاتَبٍ تُوُفِّيَ وَ لَهُ مَالٌ قَالَ يُحْسَبُ مِيرَاثُهُ عَلَى قَدْرِ مَا أُعْتِقَ مِنْهُ لِوَرَثَتِهِ وَ مَا لَمْ يُعْتَقْ مِنْهُ لِأَرْبَابِهِ الَّذِينَ كَاتَبُوهُ مِنْ مَالِهِ .

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Malik Bin Atiyya who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about a contracted man who died and had not paid off his contractual amount, and left wealth and children. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If his master, when he contracted him, had placed a condition upon him that if he was frustrated (from paying it off) a part of his deficit, so he would be returned in the slaver, and he was frustrated from paying the deficit. So whatever something he left, so it would be for his master, and his son would be returned in the slavery if there was a child of his before the contract. And if he was contracted afterwards and there was no such condition placed upon him, so his son is free, and he would pay off on behalf of his father whatever remained upon him from what his father had left. And there is nothing from the inheritance for his sons until he pays off what was upon him. So if his father had not left anything, so there is nothing upon his son’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ ارْتَدَّ عَنِ الْإِسْلَامِ لِمَنْ يَكُونُ مِيرَاثُهُ قَالَ يُقْسَمُ مِيرَاثُهُ عَلَى وَرَثَتِهِ عَلَى كِتَابِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abu Wallad Al Hanaat, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who reneged (go back on) from Al-Islam, for whom would his inheritance happen to be?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘His inheritance would be distributed over his inheritors upon the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: صحيح - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (3/229)

text: Ibn Mahboub, from Sayf Bin Umeyra, from Abu Bakr Al Hazramy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the Muslim man reneges from Al-Islam, his wife becomes irrevocably divorced from him just as the irrevocably divorced woman. And if he were to be killed, or die before the fulfillment of her waiting period, so she would inherit him during the waiting period, and he would not inherit her if she had died and he had reneged from Al-Islam’.

citation.arabic_text: إِذَا ارْتَدَّ الرَّجُلُ الْمُسْلِمُ عَنِ الْإِسْلَامِ بَانَتْ مِنْهُ امْرَأَتُهُ كَمَا تَبِينُ الْمُطَلَّقَةُ وَ إِنْ قُتِلَ أَوْ مَاتَ قَبْلَ انْقِضَاءِ الْعِدَّةِ فَهِيَ تَرِثُهُ فِي الْعِدَّةِ وَ لَا يَرِثُهَا إِنْ مَاتَتْ وَ هُوَ مُرْتَدٌّ عَنِ الْإِسْلَامِ .
citation.translation: Ibn Mahboub, from Sayf Bin Umeyra, from Abu Bakr Al Hazramy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the Muslim man reneges from Al-Islam, his wife becomes irrevocably divorced from him just as the irrevocably divorced woman. And if he were to be killed, or die before the fulfillment of her waiting period, so she would inherit him during the waiting period, and he would not inherit her if she had died and he had reneged from Al-Islam’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: حسن - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (23/229)

text: Ibn Mahboub, from Al A’la Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the apostate, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who turns away from the Religion of Al-Islam and rejects what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Revealed unto Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>, after his Islam, so there is no repentance for him, and his killing is Obligated, and his wife is irrevocably divorced from him. Therefore, whatever he has left would be distributed upon his (Muslim) children’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الْمُرْتَدِّ فَقَالَ مَنْ رَغِبَ عَنْ دِينِ الْإِسْلَامِ وَ كَفَرَ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) بَعْدَ إِسْلَامِهِ فَلَا تَوْبَةَ لَهُ وَ قَدْ وَجَبَ قَتْلُهُ وَ بَانَتِ امْرَأَتُهُ مِنْهُ فَلْيُقْسَمْ مَا تَرَكَ عَلَى وُلْدِهِ .
citation.translation: Ibn Mahboub, from Al A’la Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the apostate, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who turns away from the Religion of Al-Islam and rejects what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Revealed unto Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>, after his Islam, so there is no repentance for him, and his killing is Obligated, and his wife is irrevocably divorced from him. Therefore, whatever he has left would be distributed upon his (Muslim) children’.

text: Yunus, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘The lost, one should wait with his wealth for four years, then distribute it’.

citation.arabic_text: يُونُسُ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ قَالَ لِي أَبُو الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) الْمَفْقُودُ يُتَرَبَّصُ بِمَالِهِ أَرْبَعَ سِنِينَ ثُمَّ يُقْسَمُ .
citation.translation: Yunus, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘The lost, one should wait with his wealth for four years, then distribute it’.

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Mahziyar who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> the 2<sup>nd</sup> - about a house which belonged to a woman, and had a son and a daughter. The son disappeared in the sea, and the woman died, so she left (behind) her daughter. So her daughter claimed that when she was small, her mother had made this house to be for her, and then she sold parts from it, and there remained a part in the house by the side of a house of a man from our companions and he disliked buying it due to the disappearance of the son, and what made him fear that it might not be Permissible for him to buy it, and there is no new of the son (who had disappeared in the sea). So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘And since how long has he been absent?’ So I said, ‘Since many years’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should wait with it after his absence for ten years, then he should buy it’. So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So if one were to wait with it after his absence of ten years, it is Permissible to buy it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.

citation.arabic_text: عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ قَالَ سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ الثَّانِيَ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ دَارٍ كَانَتْ لِامْرَأَةٍ وَ كَانَ لَهَا ابْنٌ وَ ابْنَةٌ فَغَابَ الِابْنُ بِالْبَحْرِ وَ مَاتَتِ الْمَرْأَةُ فَادَّعَتِ ابْنَتُهَا أَنَّ أُمَّهَا كَانَتْ صَيَّرَتْ هَذِهِ الدَّارَ لَهَا وَ بَاعَتْ أَشْقَاصاً مِنْهَا وَ بَقِيَتْ فِي الدَّارِ قِطْعَةٌ إِلَى جَنْبِ دَارِ رَجُلٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا وَ هُوَ يَكْرَهُ أَنْ يَشْتَرِيَهَا لِغَيْبَةِ الِابْنِ وَ مَا يَتَخَوَّفُ مِنْ أَنْ لَا يَحِلَّ لَهُ شِرَاؤُهَا وَ لَيْسَ يُعْرَفُ لِلِابْنِ خَبَرٌ فَقَالَ لِي وَ مُنْذُ كَمْ غَابَ فَقُلْتُ مُنْذُ سِنِينَ كَثِيرَةٍ فَقَالَ يُنْتَظَرُ بِهِ غَيْبَتُهُ عَشْرَ سِنِينَ ثُمَّ يُشْتَرَى فَقُلْتُ لَهُ فَإِذَا انْتُظِرَ بِهِ غَيْبَتُهُ عَشْرَ سِنِينَ يَحِلُّ شِرَاؤُهَا قَالَ نَعَمْ .

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man for whom were children. So one of the children disappeared and he did not know where he was, and the man died. How should we deal with the inheritance of the disappeared one from his father?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Keep it aside until he comes’. I said, ‘The man is lost and will not be coming’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the inheritors of the man were reliable with his wealth, distribute it between them, so when he comes, they can return it to him’. A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Hammad, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), similar to it’.

citation.arabic_text: أَبُو عَلِيٍّ الْأَشْعَرِيُّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْجَبَّارِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ كَانَ لَهُ وُلْدٌ فَغَابَ بَعْضُ وُلْدِهِ وَ لَمْ يَدْرِ أَيْنَ هُوَ وَ مَاتَ الرَّجُلُ كَيْفَ يُصْنَعُ بِمِيرَاثِ الْغَائِبِ مِنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ يُعْزَلُ حَتَّى يَجِي‏ءَ قُلْتُ فُقِدَ الرَّجُلُ فَلَمْ يَجِئْ فَقَالَ إِنْ كَانَ وَرَثَةُ الرَّجُلِ مِلَاءً بِمَالِهِ اقْتَسَمُوهُ بَيْنَهُمْ فَإِذَا جَاءَ رَدُّوهُ عَلَيْهِ . عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ ( عليه السلام ) مِثْلَهُ .

text: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ibn Rabat and Abdullah Bin Jabalat, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the first, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who had children for him, so one of his children disappeared and he did not know where he was, and the man died. So what should be done with the inheritance of the man, for the absent one from his father?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Keep it aside until he comes’. I said, ‘So upon his wealth is the Zakat?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, until he comes’. So whenever he comes, it should be returned to him’.

citation.arabic_text: حُمَيْدُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَمَاعَةَ عَنِ ابْنِ رِبَاطٍ وَ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ جَبَلَةَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّلِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ كَانَ لَهُ وُلْدٌ فَغَابَ بَعْضُ وُلْدِهِ وَ لَمْ يَدْرِ أَيْنَ هُوَ وَ مَاتَ الرَّجُلُ فَأَيُّ شَيْ‏ءٍ يُصْنَعُ بِمِيرَاثِ الرَّجُلِ الْغَائِبِ مِنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ يُعْزَلُ حَتَّى يَجِي‏ءَ قُلْتُ فَعَلَى مَالِهِ زَكَاةٌ قَالَ لَا حَتَّى يَجِي‏ءَ قُلْتُ فَإِذَا جَاءَ يُزَكِّيهِ قَالَ لَا حَتَّى يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَوْلُ فِي يَدِهِ فَقُلْتُ فُقِدَ الرَّجُلُ فَلَمْ يَجِئْ قَالَ إِنْ كَانَ وَرَثَةُ الرَّجُلِ مِلَاءً بِمَالِهِ اقْتَسَمُوهُ بَيْنَهُمْ فَإِذَا هُوَ جَاءَ رَدُّوهُ عَلَيْهِ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The lost one, the inheritors should withhold his wealth upon doing their best to seek him in the earth, for four years. So if they are not able to locate him, the wealth is distributed between the inheritors. And if there was a child for him, withhold the wealth, and spend upon that very child for four years’.

citation.arabic_text: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ قَالَ ( عليه السلام ) الْمَفْقُودُ يَحْبِسُ مَالَهُ الْوَرَثَةُ عَلَى قَدْرِ مَا يُطْلَبُ فِي الْأَرْضِ أَرْبَعَ سِنِينَ فَإِنْ لَمْ يُقْدَرْ عَلَيْهِ قُسِمَ مَالُهُ بَيْنَ الْوَرَثَةِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ لَهُ وُلْدٌ حُبِسَ الْمَالُ وَ أُنْفِقَ عَلَى وُلْدِهِ تِلْكَ الْأَرْبَعَ سِنِينَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The lost one, the inheritors should withhold his wealth upon doing their best to seek him in the earth, for four years. So if they are not able to locate him, the wealth is distributed between the inheritors. And if there was a child for him, withhold the wealth, and spend upon that very child for four years’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus, from Hisham Bin Salim who said, ‘Khatab Al-Awr asked Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), and I was seated there, so he said, ‘There was an employee with my father who worked for him for the wages. So we lost him, and there remained for him something from his wages, and we do not recognise his inheritors’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So seek him’. He said, ‘We have sought him, but could not find him’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Poor’ – and he<sup>asws</sup> moved his<sup>asws</sup> hands (gestured). He (the narrator) said, ‘So I repeated to him<sup>asws</sup>. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Seek and strive in accordance to your ability, or else it is like your wealth until there comes someone seeking it. So if there befalls with you what befalls (death), so bequeath with it that if someone comes seeking it, then it should be handed over to him’.

text: Yunus, from Abu Sabit and Ibn Awn, from Muawiya Bin Wahab, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who had a right upon a man, so he lost him and he did not know where to seek him, and he did not know whether he was alive or he was dead, and he did not recognise an inheritor for him, nor a clan, nor a city. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Seek him’. He said, If that is prolonged, so I should give in charity with it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Seek him’.

citation.arabic_text: رَجُلٍ كَانَ لَهُ عَلَى رَجُلٍ حَقٌّ فَفَقَدَهُ وَ لَا يَدْرِي أَيْنَ يَطْلُبُهُ وَ لَا يَدْرِي أَ حَيٌّ هُوَ أَمْ مَيِّتٌ وَ لَا يَعْرِفُ لَهُ وَارِثاً وَ لَا نَسَباً وَ لَا بَلَداً قَالَ اطْلُبْ قَالَ إِنَّ ذَلِكَ قَدْ طَالَ فَأَتَصَدَّقُ بِهِ قَالَ اطْلُبْهُ .

text: Yunus, from Nasr Bin Habeeb, the author of Al Khan, who said, ‘I wrote to Abd Salih<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) that there were with me one hundred and forty Dirhams, and I am an owner of a hotel, and its owner (of the money) died, and I do not recognise any inheritor of his. So, your<sup>asws</sup> view in letting me know of its state and what shall I do with it, for I am fed up with it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘You can work in it and take out charity, little by little until it is taken out (completely)’.

citation.arabic_text: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى عَبْدٍ صَالِحٍ ( عليه السلام ) قَدْ وَقَعَتْ عِنْدِي مِائَتَا دِرْهَمٍ وَ أَرْبَعَةُ دَرَاهِمَ وَ أَنَا صَاحِبُ فُنْدُقٍ وَ مَاتَ صَاحِبُهَا وَ لَمْ أَعْرِفْ لَهُ وَرَثَةً فَرَأْيُكَ فِي إِعْلَامِي حَالَهَا وَ مَا أَصْنَعُ بِهَا فَقَدْ ضِقْتُ بِهَا ذَرْعاً فَكَتَبَ اعْمَلْ فِيهَا وَ أَخْرِجْهَا صَدَقَةً قَلِيلًا قَلِيلًا حَتَّى تَخْرُجَ .

text: Yunus, from Al Haysam Abu Rawh author of Al Khan, said, ‘I wrote to Abd Salih<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), ‘I manage hotels, so there lodged with me the man, and he died suddenly. I do not know him, nor do I know his city, nor any inheritor for him. So there remains the wealth with me, how should I deal with it, and for whom is that wealth?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘Leave it upon its state’ (until you find his inheritors).

citation.arabic_text: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى عَبْدٍ صَالِحٍ ( عليه السلام ) أَنِّي أَتَقَبَّلُ الْفَنَادِقَ فَيَنْزِلُ عِنْدِيَ الرَّجُلُ فَيَمُوتُ فَجْأَةً لَا أَعْرِفُهُ وَ لَا أَعْرِفُ بِلَادَهُ وَ لَا وَرَثَتَهُ فَيَبْقَى الْمَالُ عِنْدِي كَيْفَ أَصْنَعُ بِهِ وَ لِمَنْ ذَلِكَ الْمَالُ فَكَتَبَ ( عليه السلام ) اتْرُكْهُ عَلَى حَالِهِ .

text: Yunus, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘The lost, one should wait with his wealth for four years, then distribute it’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لِي أَبُو الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) الْمَفْقُودُ يُتَرَبَّصُ بِمَالِهِ أَرْبَعَ سِنِينَ ثُمَّ يُقْسَمُ .
citation.translation: Yunus, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said, ‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘The lost, one should wait with his wealth for four years, then distribute it’.
citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (3/231)

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Mahziyar who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> the 2<sup>nd</sup> - about a house which belonged to a woman, and had a son and a daughter. The son disappeared in the sea, and the woman died, so she left (behind) her daughter. So her daughter claimed that when she was small, her mother had made this house to be for her, and then she sold parts from it, and there remained a part in the house by the side of a house of a man from our companions and he disliked buying it due to the disappearance of the son, and what made him fear that it might not be Permissible for him to buy it, and there is no new of the son (who had disappeared in the sea). So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘And since how long has he been absent?’ So I said, ‘Since many years’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should wait with it after his absence for ten years, then he should buy it’. So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So if one were to wait with it after his absence of ten years, it is Permissible to buy it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ الثَّانِيَ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ دَارٍ كَانَتْ لِامْرَأَةٍ وَ كَانَ لَهَا ابْنٌ وَ ابْنَةٌ فَغَابَ الِابْنُ بِالْبَحْرِ وَ مَاتَتِ الْمَرْأَةُ فَادَّعَتِ ابْنَتُهَا أَنَّ أُمَّهَا كَانَتْ صَيَّرَتْ هَذِهِ الدَّارَ لَهَا وَ بَاعَتْ أَشْقَاصاً مِنْهَا وَ بَقِيَتْ فِي الدَّارِ قِطْعَةٌ إِلَى جَنْبِ دَارِ رَجُلٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا وَ هُوَ يَكْرَهُ أَنْ يَشْتَرِيَهَا لِغَيْبَةِ الِابْنِ وَ مَا يَتَخَوَّفُ مِنْ أَنْ لَا يَحِلَّ لَهُ شِرَاؤُهَا وَ لَيْسَ يُعْرَفُ لِلِابْنِ خَبَرٌ فَقَالَ لِي وَ مُنْذُ كَمْ غَابَ فَقُلْتُ مُنْذُ سِنِينَ كَثِيرَةٍ فَقَالَ يُنْتَظَرُ بِهِ غَيْبَتُهُ عَشْرَ سِنِينَ ثُمَّ يُشْتَرَى فَقُلْتُ لَهُ فَإِذَا انْتُظِرَ بِهِ غَيْبَتُهُ عَشْرَ سِنِينَ يَحِلُّ شِرَاؤُهَا قَالَ نَعَمْ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Mahziyar who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> the 2<sup>nd</sup> - about a house which belonged to a woman, and had a son and a daughter. The son disappeared in the sea, and the woman died, so she left (behind) her daughter. So her daughter claimed that when she was small, her mother had made this house to be for her, and then she sold parts from it, and there remained a part in the house by the side of a house of a man from our companions and he disliked buying it due to the disappearance of the son, and what made him fear that it might not be Permissible for him to buy it, and there is no new of the son (who had disappeared in the sea). So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘And since how long has he been absent?’ So I said, ‘Since many years’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should wait with it after his absence for ten years, then he should buy it’. So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So if one were to wait with it after his absence of ten years, it is Permissible to buy it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man for whom were children. So one of the children disappeared and he did not know where he was, and the man died. How should we deal with the inheritance of the disappeared one from his father?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Keep it aside until he comes’. I said, ‘The man is lost and will not be coming’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the inheritors of the man were reliable with his wealth, distribute it between them, so when he comes, they can return it to him’. A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Hammad, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), similar to it’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ كَانَ لَهُ وُلْدٌ فَغَابَ بَعْضُ وُلْدِهِ وَ لَمْ يَدْرِ أَيْنَ هُوَ وَ مَاتَ الرَّجُلُ كَيْفَ يُصْنَعُ بِمِيرَاثِ الْغَائِبِ مِنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ يُعْزَلُ حَتَّى يَجِي‏ءَ قُلْتُ فُقِدَ الرَّجُلُ فَلَمْ يَجِئْ فَقَالَ إِنْ كَانَ وَرَثَةُ الرَّجُلِ مِلَاءً بِمَالِهِ اقْتَسَمُوهُ بَيْنَهُمْ فَإِذَا جَاءَ رَدُّوهُ عَلَيْهِ . عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ ( عليه السلام ) مِثْلَهُ .

citation.grade_source: Allamah Baqir al-Majlisi: موثق - Mir‘at al ‘Uqul Fi Sharh Akhbar Al al Rasul (3/232)

text: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ibn Rabat and Abdullah Bin Jabalat, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the first, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who had children for him, so one of his children disappeared and he did not know where he was, and the man died. So what should be done with the inheritance of the man, for the absent one from his father?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Keep it aside until he comes’. I said, ‘So upon his wealth is the Zakat?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, until he comes’. I said, ‘So if he comes, he has to purify it (by paying Zakat)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, until there turns a year with it being in his hands’. So I said, ‘The man is lost and does not come?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the inheritors of the man can be relied upon with his wealth, so distribute it between them. So whenever he comes, it should be returned to him’.
