citation.arabic_text: فَلَمَّا كَانَ مِنْ غَدٍ عَادَ إِلَيْهِ فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِنِّي أَوْقَبْتُ عَلَى غُلَامٍ فَطَهِّرْنِي فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا هَذَا امْضِ إِلَى مَنْزِلِكَ لَعَلَّ مِرَاراً هَاجَ بِكَ حَتَّى فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ ثَلَاثاً بَعْدَ مَرَّتِهِ الْأُولَى فَلَمَّا كَانَ فِي الرَّابِعَةِ قَالَ لَهُ يَا هَذَا إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) حَكَمَ فِي مِثْلِكَ بِثَلَاثَةِ أَحْكَامٍ فَاخْتَرْ أَيَّهُنَّ شِئْتَ قَالَ وَ مَا هُنَّ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ قَالَ ضَرْبَةٌ بِالسَّيْفِ فِي عُنُقِكَ بَالِغَةً مَا بَلَغَتْ أَوْ إِهْدَاءٌ مِنْ جَبَلٍ مَشْدُودَ الْيَدَيْنِ وَ الرِّجْلَيْنِ أَوْ إِحْرَاقٌ بِالنَّارِ فَقَالَ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَيُّهُنَّ أَشَدُّ عَلَيَّ قَالَ الْإِحْرَاقُ بِالنَّارِ قَالَ فَإِنِّي قَدِ اخْتَرْتُهَا يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ قَالَ خُذْ لِذَلِكَ أُهْبَتَكَ فَقَالَ نَعَمْ فَقَالَ فَصَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ جَلَسَ فِي تَشَهُّدِهِ فَقَالَ اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي قَدْ أَتَيْتُ مِنَ الذَّنْبِ مَا قَدْ عَلِمْتَهُ وَ إِنِّي تَخَوَّفْتُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَجِئْتُ إِلَى وَصِيِّ رَسُولِكَ وَ ابْنِ عَمِّ نَبِيِّكَ فَسَأَلْتُهُ أَنْ يُطَهِّرَنِي فَخَيَّرَنِي بَيْنَ ثَلَاثَةِ أَصْنَافٍ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ اللَّهُمَّ فَإِنِّي قَدِ اخْتَرْتُ أَشَدَّهَا اللَّهُمَّ فَإِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ أَنْ تَجْعَلَ ذَلِكَ كَفَّارَةً لِذُنُوبِي وَ أَنْ لَا تُحْرِقَنِي بِنَارِكَ فِي آخِرَتِي ثُمَّ قَامَ وَ هُوَ بَاكٍ حَتَّى جَلَسَ فِي الْحُفْرَةِ الَّتِي حَفَرَهَا لَهُ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) وَ هُوَ يَرَى النَّارَ تَتَأَجَّجُ حَوْلَهُ قَالَ فَبَكَى أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) وَ بَكَى أَصْحَابُهُ جَمِيعاً فَقَالَ لَهُ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) قُمْ يَا هَذَا فَقَدْ أَبْكَيْتَ مَلَائِكَةَ السَّمَاءِ وَ مَلَائِكَةَ الْأَرْضِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ تَابَ عَلَيْكَ فَقُمْ وَ لَا تُعَاوِدَنَّ شَيْئاً مِمَّا قَدْ فَعَلْتَ .
citation.translation: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ ابْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ ابْنِ رِئَابٍ عَنْ مَالِكِ بْنِ عَطِيَّةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) قَالَ بَيْنَا أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) فِي مَلَإٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ إِذْ أَتَاهُ رَجُلٌ فَقَالَ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِنِّي قَدْ أَوْقَبْتُ عَلَى غُلَامٍ فَطَهِّرْنِي فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا هَذَا امْضِ إِلَى مَنْزِلِكَ لَعَلَّ مِرَاراً هَاجَ بِكَ Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Maalik Bin Atiyya, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Whilst Amir Al-Momineenasws was among a group of hisasws companions, when a man came over and said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineenasws! I have gone to a boy, therefore purify me’. So heasws said: ‘O you! Go to your house, perhaps your gall bladder is exciting you’. So when is was the next morning, he returned to himasws and said to himasws, ‘O Amir Al-Momineenasws! I have gone to a boy, therefore purify me’. So heasws said to him: ‘O you! Go to your house, perhaps your gall bladder is exciting you’. He did it three times after the first. So when it was during the fourth, heasws said to him: ‘O you! Rasool-Allahsaww had judged regarding (a case) similar to yours with three judgements, therfore choose which of these you like’. He said, ‘And what are these, O Amir Al-Momineenasws?’ Heasws said: ‘A strike with the sword in your neck, it reaches what it reaches, or throwing you off the mountain with your hands and feet tied up, or burning with the fire’. So he said, ‘O Amir Al-Momineenasws! Which of these is the harshest upon me’. Heasws said: ‘Burning with the fire’. He said, ‘So I have chosen it, O Amir Al-Momineenasws! Heasws said: ‘Are you prepared to take that, Iasws shall call for you’. So he said, ‘Yes’. So heasws said: ‘So he (the sinner) Prayed two cycles, then sat in his Tashahhud, so he said: ‘O Allahazwj! I had committed from the sins which Youazwj Know of, and I feared from that. So I went to the successorasws of Yourazwj Rasoolsaww, and a cousin of Yourazwj Prophetsaww, so I asked himasws that heasws should purify me. Soasws gave me a choice of three types of punishment. O Allahazwj! So I have chosen the harshest of these. O Allahazwj! I ask Youazwj that Youazwj Make that as an expiation of my sin, and that Youazwj do not Burn me with Yourazwj Fire in my Hereafter!’ Then he stood up and he was crying until he sat in the pit which had been dug out for him by Amir Al-Momineenasws, and he was seeing the fire inflaming around him. So Amir Al-Momineenasws wept and his companions wept altogether. So Amir Al-Momineenasws said to him: ‘Arise, O you, for you have made the Angels of the sky and the Angels of the earth to cry, so Allahazwj has Turned towards you (with Mercy). So arise and do not repeat anything from what you have done’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza and Hisham and hafs, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, some women having come over to him, so a woman from them asked himasws about the lesbianism. So heasws said: ‘The Penalty (Hadd) is the Penalty (Hadd) of the adulterer’. So the woman said, ‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic has not Mentioned that in the Quran?’ So heasws said: ‘Yes’. She said, ‘And where is it?’ Heasws said: ‘These are [25:38] the dwellers of the Al-Rass’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Abdul Raham Bin Abu Hashim, from Abu Khadeeja, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘It is not for the two women that they should be sleeping in one quilt, except that there happens to be in between the two of them, a partition. text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Ziyad called us and said that, ‘The commander of the faithful (the caliph Mansour) has written to me that I should ask around about this question’. So I said, ‘And what is it?’ So he said, ‘A man went to a woman so she carried his water (sperm). So she performed the lesbian act with a slave girl, so she (the slave girl) became pregnant’. So I said to him, ‘So did you ask the people of Al-Medina about it’. He said, ‘So he placed the letter to me and therein was, ‘Ask Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> about it. So if he<sup>asws</sup> were to answer you (fine), or else carry it back to me’. So I said to him, ‘The woman would be stoned, and the slave girl would be whipped, and the child would be attached with its father’. citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Ziyad called us and said that, ‘The commander of the faithful (the caliph Mansour) has written to me that I should ask around about this question’. So I said to him, ‘So did you ask the people of Al-Medina about it’. He said, ‘So he placed the letter to me and therein was, ‘Ask Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> about it. So if he<sup>asws</sup> were to answer you (fine), or else carry it back to me’. So I said to him, ‘The woman would be stoned, and the slave girl would be whipped, and the child would be attached with its father’. He said, and I do not know it except that he said, ‘And he (the caliph) is the one who is involved in it’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a woman who deflowered a slave girl by her hand. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon her is her dower, and she would be whipped eighty lashes’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَأْتِي بَهِيمَةً أَوْ شَاةً أَوْ نَاقَةً أَوْ بَقَرَةً قَالَ فَقَالَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُجْلَدَ حَدّاً غَيْرَ الْحَدِّ ثُمَّ يُنْفَى مِنْ بِلَادٍ إِلَى غَيْرِهَا وَ ذَكَرُوا أَنَّ لَحْمَ تِلْكَ الْبَهِيمَةِ مُحَرَّمٌ وَ لَبَنَهَا .

citation.arabic_text: الرَّجُلِ يَأْتِي الْبَهِيمَةَ فَقَالُوا جَمِيعاً إِنْ كَانَتِ الْبَهِيمَةُ لِلْفَاعِلِ ذُبِحَتْ فَإِذَا مَاتَتْ أُحْرِقَتْ بِالنَّارِ وَ لَمْ يُنْتَفَعْ بِهَا وَ ضُرِبَ هُوَ خَمْسَةً وَ عِشْرِينَ سَوْطاً رُبُعَ حَدِّ الزَّانِي وَ إِنْ لَمْ تَكُنِ الْبَهِيمَةُ لَهُ قُوِّمَتْ فَأُخِذَ ثَمَنُهَا مِنْهُ وَ دُفِعَ إِلَى صَاحِبِهَا وَ ذُبِحَتْ وَ أُحْرِقَتْ بِالنَّارِ وَ لَمْ يُنْتَفَعْ بِهَا وَ ضُرِبَ خَمْسَةً وَ عِشْرِينَ سَوْطاً فَقُلْتُ وَ مَا ذَنْبُ الْبَهِيمَةِ فَقَالَ لَا ذَنْبَ لَهَا وَ لَكِنْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَعَلَ هَذَا وَ أَمَرَ بِهِ لِكَيْلَا يَجْتَرِئَ النَّاسُ بِالْبَهَائِمِ وَ يَنْقَطِعَ النَّسْلُ .

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If his mother was alive, present, then she came seeking her right, he would be whipped eighty lashes; and if she was absent, she would be awaited with until she proceeds, so she seeks her right; and if she had died and nothing was known about her except for the goodness, the fabricator, upon him would be eighty lashes’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Amro Bin Usman Al Khazaz, from Al Fazl Bin Ismail Al Hashimy, from his father who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws and Abu Al-Hassanasws about a woman who committed adultery, so she came with a child, and accepted in the presence of an Imam of the Muslims, of her having committed adultery, and that, that child of hers, is from the adultery. So the Penalty (Hadd) was established upon her and that child grew up until he became a man. So a man fabricated against him, would he be whipped, the one who fabricated upon him?’ So heasws said: ‘He would be whipped, and not whipped’. So I said, ‘How can he be whipped and not whipped?’ So heasws said: ‘The one who says to him, ‘O son of the adultery’, would not be whipped, but rather he would be rebuked, and it is less than the Penalty (Hadd); and the one who says to him, ‘O son of the adulteress’, would be whipped the complete Penalty (Hadd)’. citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Amro Bin Usman Al Khazaz, from Al Fazl Bin Ismail Al Hashimy, from his father who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws and Abu Al-Hassanasws about a woman who committed adultery, so she came with a child, and accepted in the presence of an Imam of the Muslims, of her having committed adultery, and that, that child of hers, is from the adultery. So the Penalty (Hadd) was established upon her and that child grew up until he became a man. text: Ibn Mahboub, from Naeem Bin Ibrahim, from Abbad Al Basry, (It has been narrated) from Ja’farasws Bin Muhammadasws having said: ‘When the man slanders the man, so he says, ‘You have done the deed of the people of Lotas, having copulated with the men’. Heasws said: ‘He would be whipped the Penalty (Hadd) of the slanderer, eighty lashes’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:26
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا قَذَفَ الرَّجُلُ الرَّجُلَ فَقَالَ إِنَّكَ لَتَعْمَلُ عَمَلَ قَوْمِ لُوطٍ تَنْكِحُ الرِّجَالَ قَالَ يُجْلَدُ حَدَّ الْقَاذِفِ ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً .
citation.translation: Ibn Mahboub, from Naeem Bin Ibrahim, from Abbad Al Basry, (It has been narrated) from Ja’farasws Bin Muhammadasws having said: ‘When the man slanders the man, so he says, ‘You have done the deed of the people of Lotas, having copulated with the men’. Heasws said: ‘He would be whipped the Penalty (Hadd) of the slanderer, eighty lashes’.

text: Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub and Ibn Bakeyr, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws regarding the man who slanders the man, so he is whipped, and he repeats the slander against him. Heasws said: ‘If he says to him, ‘That which I said to you was true’, he would not be whipped; and if he were to slander with the adultery after having been whipped, so upon him would be the Penalty (Hadd); and if he slanders him before he is whipped, by ten slanders, there would not happen to be upon him, except for one Penalty (Hadd)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:26
citation.arabic_text: الرَّجُلِ يَقْذِفُ الرَّجُلَ فَيُجْلَدُ فَيَعُودُ عَلَيْهِ بِالْقَذْفِ قَالَ إِنْ قَالَ لَهُ إِنَّ الَّذِي قُلْتُ لَكَ حَقٌّ لَمْ يُجْلَدْ وَ إِنْ قَذَفَهُ بِالزِّنَى بَعْدَ مَا جُلِدَ فَعَلَيْهِ الْحَدُّ وَ إِنْ قَذَفَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُجْلَدَ بِعَشْرِ قَذَفَاتٍ لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَيْهِ إِلَّا حَدٌّ وَاحِدٌ .
citation.translation: Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub and Ibn Bakeyr, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws regarding the man who slanders the man, so he is whipped, and he repeats the slander against him. Heasws said: ‘If he says to him, ‘That which I said to you was true’, he would not be whipped; and if he were to slander with the adultery after having been whipped, so upon him would be the Penalty (Hadd); and if he slanders him before he is whipped, by ten slanders, there would not happen to be upon him, except for one Penalty (Hadd)’.

text: Ibn Mahboub, from Abbad Bin Suheyb, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, (the narrator says), ‘I heard himasws saying: ‘Aliasws was saying: ‘When the man says to the man, ‘O passive sodomist!’, and ‘O one copulated with in his backside!’, so upon him is the Penalty (Hadd), a Penalty (Hadd) of the slanderer’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:26
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ كَانَ عَلِيٌّ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ إِذَا قَالَ الرَّجُلُ لِلرَّجُلِ يَا مَعْفُوجَ وَ يَا مَنْكُوحَ فِي دُبُرِهِ فَإِنَّ عَلَيْهِ الْحَدَّ حَدَّ الْقَاذِفِ .
citation.translation: Ibn Mahboub, from Abbad Bin Suheyb, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, (the narrator says), ‘I heard himasws saying: ‘Aliasws was saying: ‘When the man says to the man, ‘O passive sodomist!’, and ‘O one copulated with in his backside!’, so upon him is the Penalty (Hadd), a Penalty (Hadd) of the slanderer’.

text: Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘If they come up to measws with a man who slandered a Muslim servant with the adultery, not being known from him except for the goodness, Iasws would strike him with the Penalty (Hadd), a Penalty (Hadd) of the free (man) except for one lash (less)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:26
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ لَوْ أُتِيتُ بِرَجُلٍ قَدْ قَذَفَ عَبْداً مُسْلِماً بِالزِّنَى لَا نَعْلَمُ مِنْهُ إِلَّا خَيْراً لَضَرَبْتُهُ الْحَدَّ حَدَّ الْحُرِّ إِلَّا سَوْطاً .
citation.translation: Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘If they come up to measws with a man who slandered a Muslim servant with the adultery, not being known from him except for the goodness, Iasws would strike him with the Penalty (Hadd), a Penalty (Hadd) of the free (man) except for one lash (less)’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Hamza Bin Humran, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who emancipated (librated) half of his slave girl, then accused her with the adultery. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> view upon him being fifty lashes, and he should repent to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic for his deed’. I said, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view of her having freed him from his accusation and forgiven him about it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no whipping upon him if she has forgiven him before it (the matter) is raised (before a judge)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:26
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَعْتَقَ نِصْفَ جَارِيَتِهِ ثُمَّ قَذَفَهَا بِالزِّنَى قَالَ فَقَالَ أَرَى عَلَيْهِ خَمْسِينَ جَلْدَةً وَ يَسْتَغْفِرَ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ مِنْ فِعْلِهِ قُلْتُ أَ رَأَيْتَ إِنْ جَعَلَتْهُ فِي حِلٍّ مِنْ قَذْفِهِ إِيَّاهَا وَ عَفَتْ عَنْهُ قَالَ لَا ضَرْبَ عَلَيْهِ إِذَا عَفَتْ عَنْهُ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَرْفَعَهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Hamza Bin Humran, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who emancipated (librated) half of his slave girl, then accused her with the adultery. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> view upon him being fifty lashes, and he should repent to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic for his deed’. I said, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view of her having freed him from his accusation and forgiven him about it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no whipping upon him if she has forgiven him before it (the matter) is raised (before a judge)’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Ibn Mahboub, from one of his companions, Abu Abdullahasws has said: ‘The slanderer of the bastard would be penalised (by the Penalty (Hadd)), and the slanderer of the son of a woman cursed by her husband would be penalised (by the Penalty (Hadd))’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:26
citation.arabic_text: يُحَدُّ قَاذِفُ اللَّقِيطِ وَ يُحَدُّ قَاذِفُ ابْنِ الْمُلَاعَنَةِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Ibn Mahboub, from one of his companions, Abu Abdullahasws has said: ‘The slanderer of the bastard would be penalised (by the Penalty (Hadd)), and the slanderer of the son of a woman cursed by her husband would be penalised (by the Penalty (Hadd))’.

text: From him, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘When an immoral woman is asked, ‘Who has been immoral with you?’, so she says, ‘So and so’, so upon her would be two Penalties – a Penalty (Hadd) for her immorality, and a Penalty (Hadd) for her accusation upon the Muslim man’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:26
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) إِذَا سُئِلَتِ الْفَاجِرَةُ مَنْ فَجَرَ بِكِ فَقَالَتْ فُلَانٌ فَإِنَّ عَلَيْهَا حَدَّيْنِ حَدّاً لِفُجُورِهَا وَ حَدّاً لِفِرْيَتِهَا عَلَى الرَّجُلِ الْمُسْلِمِ .
citation.translation: From him, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘When an immoral woman is asked, ‘Who has been immoral with you?’, so she says, ‘So and so’, so upon her would be two Penalties – a Penalty (Hadd) for her immorality, and a Penalty (Hadd) for her accusation upon the Muslim man’.

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Aban, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said: ‘If a Christian woman, and/or the Jewish woman are under the Muslim man (married to him), so if she is subjected to Penality, and (if) he slanders her son?’ Heasws said: ‘He would be whipped the Penalty (Hadd) because being (legal wife of a) ‘Muslim’ has given her protected’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:26
citation.arabic_text: النَّصْرَانِيَّةُ وَ الْيَهُودِيَّةُ تَكُونُ تَحْتَ الْمُسْلِمِ فَتُجْلَدُ فَيُقْذَفُ ابْنُهَا قَالَ تُضْرَبُ حَدّاً لِأَنَّ الْمُسْلِمَ حَصَّنَهَا .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Aban, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said: ‘If a Christian woman, and/or the Jewish woman are under the Muslim man (married to him), so if she is subjected to Penality, and (if) he slanders her son?’ Heasws said: ‘He would be whipped the Penalty (Hadd) because being (legal wife of a) ‘Muslim’ has given her protected’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah <sup>asws</sup> about the man who slanders the young girl. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would not be whipped except if she happens to have matured or near to it’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:26
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَقْذِفُ الْجَارِيَةَ الصَّغِيرَةَ قَالَ لَا يُجْلَدُ إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونَ قَدْ أَدْرَكَتْ أَوْ قَارَبَتْ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah <sup>asws</sup> about the man who slanders the young girl. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would not be whipped except if she happens to have matured or near to it’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Aasim Bin Jumeyd, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who slanders the young girl. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, until she is an adult’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:26
citation.arabic_text: الرَّجُلِ يَقْذِفُ الصَّبِيَّةَ يُجْلَدُ قَالَ لَا حَتَّى تَبْلُغَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Aasim Bin Jumeyd, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who slanders the young girl. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, until she is an adult’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about a man who fabricated upon a group of people. Heasws said: ‘If they come with it altogether, he would be whipped with one Penalty (Hadd), and if they come to be separately, he would be whipped a Penalty (Hadd) for each one of them’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:27
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ افْتَرَى عَلَى قَوْمٍ جَمَاعَةً قَالَ إِنْ أَتَوْا بِهِ مُجْتَمِعِينَ ضُرِبَ حَدّاً وَاحِداً وَ إِنْ أَتَوْا بِهِ مُتَفَرِّقِينَ ضُرِبَ لِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمْ حَدّاً .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about a man who fabricated upon a group of people. Heasws said: ‘If they come with it altogether, he would be whipped with one Penalty (Hadd), and if they come to be separately, he would be whipped a Penalty (Hadd) for each one of them’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, form Al Hassan Al Ataar who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘A man who slanders a people?’ Heasws said: ‘With one speech?’ I said, ‘Yes’. Heasws said: ‘He would be whipped one Penalty (Hadd). So if he had differentiated between them with regards to the slander, he would be whipped a Penalty (Hadd) for each one of them’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:27
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) رَجُلٌ قَذَفَ قَوْماً قَالَ قَالَ بِكَلِمَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ قُلْتُ نَعَمْ قَالَ يُضْرَبُ حَدّاً وَاحِداً فَإِنْ فَرَّقَ بَيْنَهُمْ فِي الْقَذْفِ ضُرِبَ لِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمْ حَدّاً .

Heasws said: ‘He would be whipped one Penalty (Hadd). So if he had differentiated between them with regards to the slander, he would be whipped a Penalty (Hadd) for each one of them’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad Bin Humran, (The narrator) says, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a man who fabricated upon a group of people. So heasws said: ‘If they come with it altogether, he would be whipped one Penalty (Hadd), and if they come with it seperately, he would be whipped for each man, one Penalty (Hadd)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:27
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ افْتَرَى عَلَى قَوْمٍ جَمَاعَةً قَالَ فَقَالَ إِنْ أَتَوْا بِهِ مُجْتَمِعِينَ ضُرِبَ حَدّاً وَاحِداً وَ إِنْ أَتَوْا بِهِ مُتَفَرِّقِينَ ضُرِبَ لِكُلِّ رَجُلٍ حَدّاً.

text: From him, from Sama’at, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, similar to it’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:27
citation.translation: From him, from Sama’at, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, similar to it’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Naeem Bin Ibrahim, from Abbad Al basry who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about three testimonies upon a man, with the adultery, and they said, ‘We will now be coming with the fourth’. Heasws said: ‘They would be whipped with the Penalty (Hadd) of the slander, eighty lashes, each man among them’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:28
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ ثَلَاثَةٍ شَهِدُوا عَلَى رَجُلٍ بِالزِّنَى وَ قَالُوا الْآنَ نَأْتِي بِالرَّابِعِ قَالَ يُجْلَدُونَ حَدَّ الْقَاذِفِ ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً كُلُّ رَجُلٍ مِنْهُمْ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Naeem Bin Ibrahim, from Abbad Al basry who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about three testimonies upon a man, with the adultery, and they said, ‘We will now be coming with the fourth’. Heasws said: ‘They would be whipped with the Penalty (Hadd) of the slander, eighty lashes, each man among them’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>: ‘Amir Al Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘May I<sup>asws</sup> not be the first of the witnessed upon the adultery, for fear that one of them might withdraw, so I<sup>asws</sup> would be whipped’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:28
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) لَا أَكُونُ أَوَّلَ الشُّهُودِ الْأَرْبَعَةِ عَلَى الزِّنَى أَخْشَى أَنْ يَنْكُلَ بَعْضُهُمْ فَأُجْلَدَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>: ‘Amir Al Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘May I<sup>asws</sup> not be the first of the witnessed upon the adultery, for fear that one of them might withdraw, so I<sup>asws</sup> would be whipped’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Musaddaq Bin Sadaqa, from Ammar Bin Musa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man against whom three testified that he had committed adultery with so and so woman, and the fourth one testified that he does not know who he committed adultery with. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He (the accused) would neither be whipped, nor stoned’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:28
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ شَهِدَ عَلَيْهِ ثَلَاثَةٌ أَنَّهُ زَنَى بِفُلَانَةَ وَ شَهِدَ الرَّابِعُ أَنَّهُ لَا يَدْرِي بِمَنْ زَنَى قَالَ لَا يُجْلَدُ وَ لَا يُرْجَمُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Musaddaq Bin Sadaqa, from Ammar Bin Musa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man against whom three testified that he had committed adultery with so and so woman, and the fourth one testified that he does not know who he committed adultery with. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He (the accused) would neither be whipped, nor stoned’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, from hisasws fatherasws regarding three witnesses upon one man with the adultery. So Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Where is the fourth?’ So they said, ‘He is coming just now’. So Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Apply the Penalty (Hadd) upon them, for there is nothing in the Penalties, waiting for a moment’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:28

citation.arabic_text: مَنْ قَذَفَ امْرَأَتَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ بِهَا جُلِدَ الْحَدَّ وَ هِيَ امْرَأَتُهُ .

citation.translation: From him, form Yunus, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, Abu Abdullahasws has said: ‘When the man accuses his wife, then admits having lied to himself, would be whipped the Penalty (Hadd), and she would be his wife; but if he did not admit lying to himself, there would be cursing and separation between the two of them’.

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Musny Al Hanaat, from Zurara who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws was asked about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [24:6] And (as for) those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except for themselves, heasws said: ‘He is the one who accuses his wife, so when he has accused her, then he accepts that he had lied against her, would be whipped the Penalty (Hadd), and his wife would be returned to him. So if he refuses (to admit having lied) and stands by it, so the testimony of one of these (should be taken) four times, bearing Allah to Witness that he is from the truthful ones [24:7] And the fifth (time) then the Curse of Allah be on him if he is one of the liars. And if she intends to stave off the punishment from herself, and the punishment, it is the stoning, she should testify by four testimonies with Allahazwj that he is from the liars, and during the fifth that the Anger of Allahazwj would be upon her if he was from the truthful ones. And if she does not do it, she would be stoned; and if she were to do it, the Penalty (Hadd) would be staved off from herself, then she would not be Permissible for him up to the Day of Judgement’.

citation.arabic_text: سُئِلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ قَوْلِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ وَ الَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ أَزْواجَهُمْ وَ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُمْ شُهَداءُ إِلَّا أَنْفُسُهُمْ قَالَ هُوَ الَّذِي يَقْذِفُ امْرَأَتَهُ فَإِذَا قَذَفَهَا ثُمَّ أَقَرَّ بِأَنَّهُ كَذَبَ عَلَيْهَا جُلِدَ الْحَدَّ وَ رُدَّتْ إِلَيْهِ امْرَأَتُهُ وَ إِنْ أَبَى إِلَّا أَنْ يَمْضِيَ فَشَهِدَ عَلَيْهَا أَرْبَعَ شَهَادَاتٍ بِاللَّهِ إِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ وَ الْخَامِسَةُ يَلْعَنُ فِيهَا نَفْسَهُ إِنْ كَانَ مِنَ الْكَاذِبِينَ وَ إِنْ أَرَادَتْ أَنْ تَدْرَأَ عَنْ نَفْسِهَا الْعَذَابَ وَ الْعَذَابُ هُوَ الرَّجْمُ شَهِدَتْ أَرْبَعَ شَهَادَاتٍ بِاللَّهِ إِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الْكَاذِبِينَ وَ الْخَامِسَةُ أَنَّ غَضَبَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا إِنْ كَانَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ وَ إِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ رُجِمَتْ فَإِنْ فَعَلَتْ دَرَأَتْ عَنْ نَفْسِهَا الْحَدَّ ثُمَّ لَا تَحِلُّ لَهُ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:29
citation.arabic_text: رَجُلٍ قَالَ لِامْرَأَتِهِ لَمْ تَأْتِنِي عَذْرَاءَ قَالَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْ‏ءٌ لِأَنَّ الْعُذْرَةَ تَذْهَبُ بِغَيْرِ جِمَاعٍ .
citation.translation: Yunus, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who says to his wife, ‘You did not come to me as a virgin’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is nothing upon him because the virginity can go away without copulation’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a man who accused his son with the adultery. Heasws said: ‘Had he (father) killed him, he would not be killed due to it, and if he has accused him, he would not be whipped for it’. I said, ‘So if his father accused his mother?’ So heasws said: ‘If he had accused her and negates himself from her child, then there is cursing, and that child which he had negated from would not be necessitated upon him, and there would be separation between the two, and she would not be Permissible for him, ever. Heasws said: ‘And if he had said to his son and his mother was alive, ‘O son of the adulteress’, and does not negated from her child, he would be whipped the Penalty (Hadd) for her, and there would not be separation between the two. citation.translation: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr,f rom Jameel Bin Darraj, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from one of the two<sup>asws</sup> (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘When the man accepts upon himself with the murder, he would be killed if there do not happent to be witnessed. text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, form Ibn Raib, from Zureys, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The slave, when he accepts once upon himself in the present of the Imam<sup>asws</sup> that he has stolen, he would be cut, and the slave girl, when she accepts upon herself with the theft, would be cut’.

citation.arabic_text: الْعَبْدُ إِذَا أَقَرَّ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ عِنْدَ الْإِمَامِ مَرَّةً أَنَّهُ قَدْ سَرَقَ قَطَعَهُ وَ الْأَمَةُ إِذَا أَقَرَّتْ عَلَى نَفْسِهَا بِالسَّرِقَةِ قَطَعَهَا .

citation.arabic_text: السَّارِقُ إِذَا جَاءَ مِنْ قِبَلِ نَفْسِهِ تَائِباً إِلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ وَ رَدَّ سَرِقَتَهُ عَلَى صَاحِبِهَا فَلَا قَطْعَ عَلَيْهِ .

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ مَنْ أَقَرَّ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ عِنْدَ الْإِمَامِ بِحَقِّ أَحَدٍ مِنْ حُقُوقِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَلَيْسَ عَلَى الْإِمَامِ أَنْ يُقِيمَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَدَّ الَّذِي أَقَرَّ بِهِ عِنْدَهُ حَتَّى يَحْضُرَ صَاحِبُ حَقِّ الْحَدِّ أَوْ وَلِيُّهُ فَيَطْلُبَهُ بِحَقِّهِ .
citation.translation: Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Al Fuzayl Bin Yasaar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws: ‘The one who accepts upon himself in the presence of the Imamasws with a right of someone from the rights of the Muslims, so it is not upon the Imamasws that heasws should established the Penalty (Hadd) upon him, the one who accepted with it in hisasws presence, until the owner of the right is present, or his guardian, so he seeks his right’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus, from Sama’at Bin Mahran, Abu Abdullahasws has said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws used to cut regrding a ‘Bayza’. I said, ‘And what is a ‘Bayza’ (a helmet)?’ Heasws said: ‘A Bayza, its value is a quarter Dinaar’. And I said, ‘Is it the lowest (value) for a Penalty (Hadd) of a thief?’ So heasws was silent (in agreement)’.

citation.arabic_text: قَطَعَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) فِي بَيْضَةٍ قُلْتُ وَ مَا بَيْضَةٌ قَالَ بَيْضَةٌ قِيمَتُهَا رُبُعُ دِينَارٍ وَ قُلْتُ هُوَ أَدْنَى حَدِّ السَّارِقِ فَسَكَتَ .

text: From him, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The hand of the thief would not be cut regards to anything except if it reaches the value of a Mijanna, and it is a quarter of a Dinar’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:35
citation.arabic_text: لَا يُقْطَعُ يَدُ السَّارِقِ إِلَّا فِي شَيْ‏ءٍ تَبْلُغُ قِيمَتُهُ مِجَنّاً وَ هُوَ رُبُعُ دِينَارٍ .
citation.translation: From him, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The hand of the thief would not be cut regards to anything except if it reaches the value of a Mijanna, and it is a quarter of a Dinar’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The hand of the thief must not be cut until his theft reaches a quarter of a Dinar; and Ali<sup>asws</sup> had cut regarding an iron helment (Bayza)’. I said, ‘And how much is its price?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A quarter of a Dinar’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا يُقْطَعُ يَدُ السَّارِقِ حَتَّى تَبْلُغَ سَرِقَتُهُ رُبُعَ دِينَارٍ وَ قَدْ قَطَعَ عَلِيٌّ ( صلوات الله عليه ) فِي بَيْضَةِ حَدِيدٍ قَالَ عَلِيٌّ وَ قَالَ أَبُو بَصِيرٍ سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ أَدْنَى مَا يُقْطَعُ فِيهِ السَّارِقُ فَقَالَ فِي بَيْضَةِ حَدِيدٍ قُلْتُ وَ كَمْ ثَمَنُهَا قَالَ رُبُعُ دِينَارٍ .

text: Ali, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad Bin Humran, and from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, altogether from Muhammad Bin Muslim, Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The lowest of that with regards to which the hand of the thief would be cut, is five Dinars’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:35
citation.arabic_text: أَدْنَى مَا يُقْطَعُ فِيهِ يَدُ السَّارِقِ خُمُسُ دِينَارٍ .
citation.translation: Ali, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad Bin Humran, and from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, altogether from Muhammad Bin Muslim, Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The lowest of that with regards to which the hand of the thief would be cut, is five Dinars’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Aban Bin Usman, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The lowest of what with regards to which the man is cut, is five Dinars’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:35
citation.arabic_text: أَقَلُّ مَا يُقْطَعُ فِيهِ الرَّجُلُ خُمُسُ دِينَارٍ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Aban Bin Usman, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The lowest of what with regards to which the man is cut, is five Dinars’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Regarding how much would the thief’s (hand) be cut?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Regarding a quarter of a Dinaar’. I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Regarding to Dirhams?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Regarding a quarter of a Dinar, the (value of the) Dinar reaching what it reaches’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view of the one who steals less than a quarter of a Dinar when he steals, he would be named as a thief, and is he a thief in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> in that state?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Every one who steals anything from a Muslim, so he has taken it and kept it in his possession, so upon him would occur the name of the thief, and he would be a thief in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, but, his hand would not be cut except with regards to a quarter of a Dinar, or more. And if the hands of the thief were to be cut regarding what is less than a quarter of a Dinaar, you would find the generality of the people as being (hand) cut’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:35
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فِي كَمْ يُقْطَعُ السَّارِقُ فَقَالَ فِي رُبُعِ دِينَارٍ قَالَ قُلْتُ لَهُ فِي دِرْهَمَيْنِ فَقَالَ فِي رُبُعِ دِينَارٍ بَلَغَ الدِّينَارُ مَا بَلَغَ قَالَ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ أَ رَأَيْتَ مَنْ سَرَقَ أَقَلَّ مِنْ رُبُعِ دِينَارٍ هَلْ يَقَعُ عَلَيْهِ حِينَ سَرَقَ اسْمُ السَّارِقِ وَ هَلْ هُوَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ سَارِقٌ فِي تِلْكَ الْحَالِ فَقَالَ كُلُّ مَنْ سَرَقَ مِنْ مُسْلِمٍ شَيْئاً قَدْ حَوَاهُ وَ أَحْرَزَهُ فَهُوَ يَقَعُ عَلَيْهِ اسْمُ السَّارِقِ وَ هُوَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ سَارِقٌ وَ لَكِنْ لَا يُقْطَعُ إِلَّا فِي رُبُعِ دِينَارٍ أَوْ أَكْثَرَ وَ لَوْ قُطِعَتْ أَيْدِي السُّرَّاقِ فِيمَا هُوَ أَقَلُّ مِنْ رُبُعِ دِينَارٍ لَأَلْفَيْتَ عَامَّةَ النَّاسِ مُقَطَّعِينَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Regarding how much would the thief’s (hand) be cut?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Regarding a quarter of a Dinaar’. I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Regarding to Dirhams?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Regarding a quarter of a Dinar, the (value of the) Dinar reaching what it reaches’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view of the one who steals less than a quarter of a Dinar when he steals, he would be named as a thief, and is he a thief in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> in that state?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Every one who steals anything from a Muslim, so he has taken it and kept it in his possession, so upon him would occur the name of the thief, and he would be a thief in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, but, his hand would not be cut except with regards to a quarter of a Dinar, or more. And if the hands of the thief were to be cut regarding what is less than a quarter of a Dinaar, you would find the generality of the people as being (hand) cut’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘From where is the cutting (of the hand) Obligated?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> extended his fingers and said: ‘For over here, meaning from the hinge of the palm’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:36
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لَهُ مِنْ أَيْنَ يَجِبُ الْقَطْعُ فَبَسَطَ أَصَابِعَهُ وَ قَالَ مِنْ هَاهُنَا يَعْنِي مِنْ مَفْصِلِ الْكَفِّ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘From where is the cutting (of the hand) Obligated?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> extended his fingers and said: ‘For over here, meaning from the hinge of the palm’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The cutting (of the hand) is from the middle of the palm, and the thumb is not cut; and when the foot is cut, the heel is not cut’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:36
citation.arabic_text: الْقَطْعُ مِنْ وَسَطِ الْكَفِّ وَ لَا يُقْطَعُ الْإِبْهَامُ وَ إِذَا قُطِعَتِ الرِّجْلُ تُرِكَ الْعَقِبُ لَمْ يُقْطَعْ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The cutting (of the hand) is from the middle of the palm, and the thumb is not cut; and when the foot is cut, the heel is not cut’.

text: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban Bin Usman, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> did not increased upon cutting of the hand and the leg, and he<sup>asws</sup> was saying, I<sup>asws</sup> am embarassed from my<sup>asws</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> that I<sup>asws</sup> should leave him not having for him what he can wash himself with (from toilet), or clean himself with’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘If he were to steal after cutting of the hand and the leg?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> would leave him in the prison forever, and make the people to be free from his evil’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:36
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ عَلِيٌّ ( صلوات الله عليه ) لَا يَزِيدُ عَلَى قَطْعِ الْيَدِ وَ الرِّجْلِ وَ يَقُولُ إِنِّي لَأَسْتَحْيِي مِنْ رَبِّي أَنْ أَدَعَهُ لَيْسَ لَهُ مَا يَسْتَنْجِي بِهِ أَوْ يَتَطَهَّرُ بِهِ قَالَ وَ سَأَلْتُهُ إِنْ هُوَ سَرَقَ بَعْدَ قَطْعِ الْيَدِ وَ الرِّجْلِ فَقَالَ أَسْتَوْدِعُهُ السِّجْنَ أَبَداً وَ أُغْنِي عَنِ النَّاسِ شَرَّهُ .
citation.translation: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban Bin Usman, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> did not increased upon cutting of the hand and the leg, and he<sup>asws</sup> was saying, I<sup>asws</sup> am embarassed from my<sup>asws</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> that I<sup>asws</sup> should leave him not having for him what he can wash himself with (from toilet), or clean himself with’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘If he were to steal after cutting of the hand and the leg?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> would leave him in the prison forever, and make the people to be free from his evil’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, altogether from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding the thief: ‘When he steals, cut off his right hand, and when he steals again, cut off his left leg. Then if he were to steal again, imprison him and leave his right leg to walk upon it to the WC, and his left hand, he can eat with it, and wash himself (from the WC) with it’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> am embarassed from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> that I<sup>asws</sup> would leave him not being able to do anything, but I<sup>asws</sup> would imprison him until he dies in the prison’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> did not cut (anymore) from a thief after (having cut) his hand and his leg’.

citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man with a crippled right hand, or a crippled left hand, steals’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘His right hand would be cut upon every state’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah Bin Hilal, from his father, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Inform me about the thief, why is his right hand and his left leg cut, and his right hand and his right leg is not cut?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘How good is what you have asked. When his right hand and right leg is cut, he would fall upon his left side, and he would not be able to stand. So when his right hand and his left leg are cut, he would balance and be able to stand straight’. I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! And how can he stand and his leg has been cut?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The cutting is not from where you view as him being cut. But rather, the man would be cut from the lower part of the foot, and there would be left from his foot upon which he can stand to Pray and worship Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’. I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘From where would the hand be cut?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The four fingers would be cut, and the thumb would be left, so he can depend upon it during the Prayer, and he can wash his face with it for the Prayer’. I said, ‘So this is the cutting from the first one who was cut (in such a manner)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It was Usman Bin Affan who made that good for Muawiya’.

citation.arabic_text: لَيْسَ عَلَى الَّذِي يَسْتَلِبُ قَطْعٌ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَى الَّذِي يَطُرُّ الدَّرَاهِمَ مِنْ ثَوْبِ الرَّجُلِ قَطْعٌ .
citation.translation: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from a number of our companions, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdul Rahma Bin Abu Abdullah, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is no cutting upon the one who embezzles, and there is no cutting upon the one who displaces the Dirhams from a cloth of the man’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who steals with stealthy embezzlement, he would not be cut, but he would be whipped with an intense whipping’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:37
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ مَنْ سَرَقَ خُلْسَةً اخْتَلَسَهَا لَمْ يُقْطَعْ وَ لَكِنْ يُضْرَبُ ضَرْباً شَدِيداً .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who steals with stealthy embezzlement, he would not be cut, but he would be whipped with an intense whipping’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘They came with a pick-pocket who had picked some Dirhams from a man. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he has picked it from his outer shirt, I<sup>asws</sup> would not cut his (hand), but if he picked is from his inner shirt, I<sup>asws</sup> would cut his (hand)’.

citation.arabic_text: أُتِيَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) بِطَرَّارٍ قَدْ طَرَّ دَرَاهِمَ مِنْ كُمِّ رَجُلٍ قَالَ فَقَالَ إِنْ كَانَ قَدْ طَرَّ مِنْ قَمِيصِهِ الْأَعْلَى لَمْ أَقْطَعْهُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ طَرَّ مِنْ قَمِيصِهِ الدَّاخِلِ قَطَعْتُهُ .

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:37
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) أَرْبَعَةٌ لَا قَطْعَ عَلَيْهِمْ الْمُخْتَلِسُ وَ الْغُلُولُ وَ مَنْ سَرَقَ مِنَ الْغَنِيمَةِ وَ سَرِقَةُ الْأَجِيرِ فَإِنَّهَا خِيَانَةٌ .
citation.translation: Ali, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Four, there is no cutting upon them – the embezzler, and the unfaithful (of trust), and the one who steals from the war booty, and the employee thief, for these are treachery’.

text: And by this chain, that, ‘They came with a man to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> who had picked ear rings from the ears of a girl. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is open snatching’. So he<sup>asws</sup> whipped him and imprisoned him’.

citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘(There would be) no cutting-off (the hand) with regards to a feather, meaning the whole bird’.

text: And by this chain, He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> did not cut, upon the one who stole stones, meaning the marble and similar to that’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:42
citation.arabic_text: وَ بِهَذَا الْإِسْنَادِ قَالَ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لَا قَطْعَ عَلَى مَنْ سَرَقَ الْحِجَارَةَ يَعْنِي الرُّخَامَ وَ أَشْبَاهَ ذَلِكَ .
citation.translation: And by this chain, He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> did not cut, upon the one who stole stones, meaning the marble and similar to that’.

text: And by this chain, He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> judged regarding the one who stole the fruits being in their clusters. So whatever he ate from it, there was nothing upon him; and whatever he carried, so he was rebuked and made to compensate its price, twice (double)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:42
citation.arabic_text: وَ بِهَذَا الْإِسْنَادِ قَالَ قَضَى النَّبِيُّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فِيمَنْ سَرَقَ الثِّمَارَ فِي كُمِّهِ فَمَا أَكَلَ مِنْهُ فَلَا شَيْ‏ءَ عَلَيْهِ وَ مَا حَمَلَ فَيُعَزَّرُ وَ يُغَرَّمُ قِيمَتَهُ مَرَّتَيْنِ .
citation.translation: And by this chain, He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> judged regarding the one who stole the fruits being in their clusters. So whatever he ate from it, there was nothing upon him; and whatever he carried, so he was rebuked and made to compensate its price, twice (double)’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Yahya Al Khazzaz, from Gayas Bin Ibrahim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that Ali<sup>asws</sup>, they came to him<sup>asws</sup> with a man at Al-Kufa who had stolen a dove. So he<sup>asws</sup> did not cut him, and said: ‘There is no cutting (of the hand) regarding the bird’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:42
citation.arabic_text: لَا قَطْعَ فِي الطَّيْرِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Yahya Al Khazzaz, from Gayas Bin Ibrahim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that Ali<sup>asws</sup>, they came to him<sup>asws</sup> with a man at Al-Kufa who had stolen a dove. So he<sup>asws</sup> did not cut him, and said: ‘There is no cutting (of the hand) regarding the bird’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Every place which can be entered without permission of its owner, so a thief steals from it, so there would be no cutting upon him, meaning the (public) baths, and the hotels, and the resting places’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:42
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) كُلُّ مَدْخَلٍ يُدْخَلُ فِيهِ بِغَيْرِ إِذْنِ صَاحِبِهِ فَسَرَقَ مِنْهُ السَّارِقُ فَلَا قَطْعَ عَلَيْهِ يَعْنِي الْحَمَّامَاتِ وَ الْخَانَاتِ وَ الْأَرْحِيَةَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Every place which can be entered without permission of its owner, so a thief steals from it, so there would be no cutting upon him, meaning the (public) baths, and the hotels, and the resting places’.

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman Al Asamma, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Malik, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that they came to Ali<sup>asws</sup> with a man who had stolen from the public treasury, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would not be cut, for there is a share for him in it’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:42
citation.arabic_text: لَا يُقْطَعُ فَإِنَّ لَهُ فِيهِ نَصِيباً .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman Al Asamma, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Malik, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that they came to Ali<sup>asws</sup> with a man who had stolen from the public treasury, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would not be cut, for there is a share for him in it’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘There would be no cutting regarding a fruit, nor a Kasar, and the Kasar is a sap of the palm tree’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:42
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لَا قَطْعَ فِي ثَمَرٍ وَ لَا كَثَرٍ وَ الْكَثَرُ شَحْمُ النَّخْلِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘There would be no cutting regarding a fruit, nor a Kasar, and the Kasar is a sap of the palm tree’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, and someone else, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Ziyad Al Qindy, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The thief would not be cut during a year of drought with regards to everything he eats, like the bread, and the meat, and the likes of that’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:43
citation.arabic_text: لَا يُقْطَعُ السَّارِقُ فِي سَنَةِ الْمَحْلِ فِي كُلِّ شَيْ‏ءٍ يُؤْكَلُ مِثْلِ الْخُبْزِ وَ اللَّحْمِ وَ أَشْبَاهِ ذَلِكَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, and someone else, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Ziyad Al Qindy, from the one who mentioned it, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The thief would not be cut during a year of drought with regards to everything he eats, like the bread, and the meat, and the likes of that’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The thief would not be cut during a year of inactivity, meaning during a year of famine’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:43
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ لَا يُقْطَعُ السَّارِقُ فِي عَامِ سَنَةٍ يَعْنِي فِي عَامِ مَجَاعَةٍ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The thief would not be cut during a year of inactivity, meaning during a year of famine’.

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from the one who informed him, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> did not cut the thief during the days of famine’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:43
citation.arabic_text: كَانَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) لَا يَقْطَعُ السَّارِقَ فِي أَيَّامِ الْمَجَاعَةِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from the one who informed him, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> did not cut the thief during the days of famine’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the child who steals. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be excused from it once, and twice, and he would be rebuked during the third. So if he repeats, a bit of his finger would be cut. So if he repeats, lower than that would be cut’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:44
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الصَّبِيِّ يَسْرِقُ قَالَ يُعْفَى عَنْهُ مَرَّةً وَ مَرَّتَيْنِ وَ يُعَزَّرُ فِي الثَّالِثَةِ فَإِنْ عَادَ قُطِعَتْ أَطْرَافُ أَصَابِعِهِ فَإِنْ عَادَ قُطِعَ أَسْفَلُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ.
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the child who steals. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be excused from it once, and twice, and he would be rebuked during the third. So if he repeats, a bit of his finger would be cut. So if he repeats, lower than that would be cut’.

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the child who steals. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When he steals once and he is small, he would be excused from it. So if he repeats, he would be excused from it. So if he repeats, his fingertip would be cut. So if he repeats, he would be cut lower than that’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:44
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الصَّبِيِّ يَسْرِقُ قَالَ إِذَا سَرَقَ مَرَّةً وَ هُوَ صَغِيرٌ عُفِيَ عَنْهُ فَإِنْ عَادَ عُفِيَ عَنْهُ فَإِنْ عَادَ قُطِعَ بَنَانُهُ فَإِنْ عَادَ قُطِعَ أَسْفَلُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the child who steals. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When he steals once and he is small, he would be excused from it. So if he repeats, he would be excused from it. So if he repeats, his fingertip would be cut. So if he repeats, he would be cut lower than that’.

text: From him, from Safwan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, said, ‘I said to Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), ‘The children, when they came with them, Ali<sup>asws</sup> cut their fingertips from where did he<sup>asws</sup> cut?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘From the joints, the joints of the fingertips’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:44
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ ( عليه السلام ) الصِّبْيَانُ إِذَا أُتِيَ بِهِمْ عَلِيٌّ ( عليه السلام ) قَطَعَ أَنَامِلَهُمْ مِنْ أَيْنَ قَطَعَ فَقَالَ مِنَ الْمَفْصِلِ مَفْصِلِ الْأَنَامِلِ .
citation.translation: From him, from Safwan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, said, ‘I said to Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), ‘The children, when they came with them, Ali<sup>asws</sup> cut their fingertips from where did he<sup>asws</sup> cut?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘From the joints, the joints of the fingertips’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the child steals, he would be excused from it. So if he repeats, he is rebuked. So if he repeats, the ends of the fingers are cut. So if he repeats, he would be cut lower than that’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They came to Ali<sup>asws</sup> with a boy, there was doubt with regards to him having bed-wetted yet. So he<sup>asws</sup> cut the ends of the fingers’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:44
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا سَرَقَ الصَّبِيُّ عُفِيَ عَنْهُ فَإِنْ عَادَ عُزِّرَ فَإِنْ عَادَ قُطِعَ أَطْرَافُ الْأَصَابِعِ فَإِنْ عَادَ قُطِعَ أَسْفَلُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَ قَالَ أُتِيَ عَلِيٌّ بِغُلَامٍ يُشَكُّ فِي احْتِلَامِهِ فَقَطَعَ أَطْرَافَ الْأَصَابِعِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘When the child steals, he would be excused from it. So if he repeats, he is rebuked. So if he repeats, the ends of the fingers are cut. So if he repeats, he would be cut lower than that’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They came to Ali<sup>asws</sup> with a boy, there was doubt with regards to him having bed-wetted yet. So he<sup>asws</sup> cut the ends of the fingers’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘They came to Ali<sup>asws</sup> with an unmarried girl who had stolen. So he<sup>asws</sup> lashed her with a whip and did not cut her’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:44
citation.arabic_text: أُتِيَ عَلِيٌّ ( عليه السلام ) بِجَارِيَةٍ لَمْ تَحِضْ قَدْ سَرَقَتْ فَضَرَبَهَا أَسْوَاطاً وَ لَمْ يَقْطَعْهَا .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘They came to Ali<sup>asws</sup> with an unmarried girl who had stolen. So he<sup>asws</sup> lashed her with a whip and did not cut her’.

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the child who steals. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be excused from it once. So if he repeats, his fingertips would be cut, or they would be scratched until they bleed. So he if repeats, his fingers would be cut. So if he repeats, he would be cut lower than that’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:44
citation.arabic_text: الصَّبِيِّ يَسْرِقُ قَالَ يُعْفَى عَنْهُ مَرَّةً فَإِنْ عَادَ قُطِعَتْ أَنَامِلُهُ أَوْ حُكَّتْ حَتَّى تَدْمَى فَإِنْ عَادَ قُطِعَتْ أَصَابِعُهُ فَإِنْ عَادَ قُطِعَ أَسْفَلُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the child who steals. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be excused from it once. So if he repeats, his fingertips would be cut, or they would be scratched until they bleed. So he if repeats, his fingers would be cut. So if he repeats, he would be cut lower than that’.

text: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from someone else, from his companion, from Aban Bin Usman, from Zurara who said, ‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘They came to Ali<sup>asws</sup> with a boy who had stolen. So he<sup>asws</sup> scratched his fingers, then said: ‘But, if you were to repeat, I would cut these’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But it has not been done except by Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> and myself<sup>asws</sup>’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:44
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ أُتِيَ عَلِيٌّ ( عليه السلام ) بِغُلَامٍ قَدْ سَرَقَ فَطَرَّفَ أَصَابِعَهُ ثُمَّ قَالَ أَمَا لَئِنْ عُدْتَ لَأَقْطَعَنَّهَا ثُمَّ قَالَ أَمَا إِنَّهُ مَا عَمِلَهُ إِلَّا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) وَ أَنَا .
citation.translation: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from someone else, from his companion, from Aban Bin Usman, from Zurara who said, ‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘They came to Ali<sup>asws</sup> with a boy who had stolen. So he<sup>asws</sup> scratched his fingers, then said: ‘But, if you were to repeat, I would cut these’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But it has not been done except by Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> and myself<sup>asws</sup>’.

text: Aban, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘When the child steals and he has yet to bed-wet, the ends of his fingers would be cut’. And Ali<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It has not been done except by Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> and myself<sup>asws</sup>’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:44
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا سَرَقَ الصَّبِيُّ وَ لَمْ يَحْتَلِمْ قُطِعَتْ أَطْرَافُ أَصَابِعِهِ قَالَ وَ قَالَ [عَلِيٌّ ع] لَمْ يَصْنَعْهُ إِلَّا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) وَ أَنَا .
citation.translation: Aban, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘When the child steals and he has yet to bed-wet, the ends of his fingers would be cut’. And Ali<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It has not been done except by Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> and myself<sup>asws</sup>’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from one of his companions, from Al A’la Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the child who stole, so heasws said: ‘If he was nine years of age, his hand would be cut, and a Penalty (Hadd) from the Penalties of Allahazwj would not be wasted’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:44
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الصَّبِيِّ يَسْرِقُ فَقَالَ إِنْ كَانَ لَهُ تِسْعُ سِنِينَ قُطِعَتْ يَدُهُ وَ لَا يُضَيَّعُ حَدٌّ مِنْ حُدُودِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from one of his companions, from Al A’la Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the child who stole, so heasws said: ‘If he was nine years of age, his hand would be cut, and a Penalty (Hadd) from the Penalties of Allahazwj would not be wasted’.

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Aban, from Razeyn who said, ‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘They came to Ali<sup>asws</sup> with a boy who had stolen, so he<sup>asws</sup> scratched his fingers, then said: ‘But, if you were to repeat, I<sup>asws</sup> would cut these’. citation.arabic_text: قَضَى أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) فِي الْعَبِيدِ وَ الْإِمَاءِ إِذَا زَنَى أَحَدُهُمْ أَنْ يُجْلَدَ خَمْسِينَ جَلْدَةً إِنْ كَانَ مُسْلِماً أَوْ كَافِراً أَوْ نَصْرَانِيّاً وَ لَا يُرْجَمَ وَ لَا يُنْفَى .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws used to whip the free, and the slave, and the Jew, and the Christian, regarding the wine and the intoxicant Al-Nabeez, eighty (lashes). So it was said, ‘What is the matter (with whipping) the Jew and the Christian?’ Heasws said: ‘When they (openly) display that in a city from the cities, because it is not for them that they should be displaying (openly drinking)’[849]. Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ja’far Bin Rizqallah or a man from Ja’far Bin Rizqallah who said, ‘A Christian man who had been immoral with a Muslim woman, was brought before Al-Mutawakkal (the Caliph). So he wanted to establish the Penalty (Hadd) upon him, but he became a Muslim. So Yahya Bin Aksam said, ‘His belief (has now) demolished his Polytheism and his deed’. And some of them said, ‘Whip him with three Penalties’, and some of them said, ‘Do with him such and such’. So Al-Mutawakkal instructed for a letter (to be written to) Abu Al-Hassanasws the 3rd and ask himasws about that. So when heasws read the letter, heasws wrote: ‘Whip him until he dies’. But, Yahya Bin Aksam disagreed, and the jurists of Al-Askar disagreed with that, and they said, ‘O commander of the faithful! Ask about this, for it is a thing which the Book (Quran) does not Speak of and a Sunnah has not come with it’. So the jurists of the Muslims who had disagreed this wrote saying, ‘A Sunnah has not come with it, and the Book (Quran) does not speak of it. Therefore, explain for us why is the whipping until death Obligated upon him?’ So heasws wrote: ‘In the Name of Allahazwj the Beneficent, the Merciful. [40:84] But when they saw Our Punishment, they said: We believe in Allah alone and we deny what we used to associate with Him [40:85] But their belief was not going to profit them when they had seen Our Punishment; (this is) Allah’s Way, which has been excluded regarding His servants, and there the unbelievers are in loss’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So Al-Mutawakkil ordered by it, and he was whipped until he died’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) يَجْلِدُ الْحُرَّ وَ الْعَبْدَ وَ الْيَهُودِيَّ وَ النَّصْرَانِيَّ فِي الْخَمْرِ وَ مُسْكِرِ النَّبِيذِ ثَمَانِينَ فَقِيلَ مَا بَالُ الْيَهُودِيِّ وَ النَّصْرَانِيِّ قَالَ إِذَا أَظْهَرُوا ذَلِكَ فِي مِصْرٍ مِنَ الْأَمْصَارِ لِأَنَّهُمْ لَيْسَ لَهُمْ أَنْ يُظْهِرُوهُ . مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ رِزْقِ اللَّهِ أَوْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ رِزْقِ اللَّهِ قَالَ قُدِّمَ إِلَى الْمُتَوَكِّلِ رَجُلٌ نَصْرَانِيٌّ فَجَرَ بِامْرَأَةٍ مُسْلِمَةٍ فَأَرَادَ أَنْ يُقِيمَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَدَّ فَأَسْلَمَ فَقَالَ يَحْيَى بْنُ أَكْثَمَ قَدْ هَدَمَ إِيمَانُهُ شِرْكَهُ وَ فِعْلَهُ وَ قَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ يُضْرَبُ ثَلَاثَةَ حُدُودٍ وَ قَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ يُفْعَلُ بِهِ كَذَا وَ كَذَا فَأَمَرَ الْمُتَوَكِّلُ بِالْكِتَابِ إِلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الثَّالِثِ ( عليه السلام ) وَ سُؤَالِهِ عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَلَمَّا قَرَأَ الْكِتَابَ كَتَبَ يُضْرَبُ حَتَّى يَمُوتَ فَأَنْكَرَ يَحْيَى بْنُ أَكْثَمَ وَ أَنْكَرَ فُقَهَاءُ الْعَسْكَرِ ذَلِكَ وَ قَالُوا يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ سَلْ عَنْ هَذَا فَإِنَّهُ شَيْ‏ءٌ لَمْ يَنْطِقْ بِهِ كِتَابٌ وَ لَمْ تَجِئْ بِهِ سُنَّةٌ فَكَتَبَ إِلَيْهِ أَنَّ فُقَهَاءَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ قَدْ أَنْكَرُوا هَذَا وَ قَالُوا لَمْ يَجِئْ بِهِ سُنَّةٌ وَ لَمْ يَنْطِقْ بِهِ كِتَابٌ فَبَيِّنْ لَنَا لِمَ أَوْجَبْتَ عَلَيْهِ الضَّرْبَ حَتَّى يَمُوتَ فَكَتَبَ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ [فَلَمَّا أَحَسُّوا] فَلَمَّا رَأَوْا بَأْسَنا قالُوا آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَحْدَهُ وَ كَفَرْنا بِما كُنَّا بِهِ مُشْرِكِينَ فَلَمْ يَكُ يَنْفَعُهُمْ إِيمانُهُمْ لَمَّا رَأَوْا بَأْسَنا سُنَّتَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي قَدْ خَلَتْ فِي عِبادِهِ وَ خَسِرَ هُنالِكَ الْكافِرُونَ قَالَ فَأَمَرَ بِهِ الْمُتَوَكِّلُ فَضُرِبَ حَتَّى مَاتَ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said, ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws used to whip the free, and the slave, and the Jew, and the Christian, regarding the wine and the intoxicant Al-Nabeez, eighty (lashes). So it was said, ‘What is the matter (with whipping) the Jew and the Christian?’ Heasws said: ‘When they (openly) display that in a city from the cities, because it is not for them that they should be displaying (openly drinking)’[849]. Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ja’far Bin Rizqallah or a man from Ja’far Bin Rizqallah who said, ‘A Christian man who had been immoral with a Muslim woman, was brought before Al-Mutawakkal (the Caliph). So he wanted to establish the Penalty (Hadd) upon him, but he became a Muslim. So Yahya Bin Aksam said, ‘His belief (has now) demolished his Polytheism and his deed’. And some of them said, ‘Whip him with three Penalties’, and some of them said, ‘Do with him such and such’. So Al-Mutawakkal instructed for a letter (to be written to) Abu Al-Hassanasws the 3rd and ask himasws about that. So when heasws read the letter, heasws wrote: ‘Whip him until he dies’. But, Yahya Bin Aksam disagreed, and the jurists of Al-Askar disagreed with that, and they said, ‘O commander of the faithful! Ask about this, for it is a thing which the Book (Quran) does not Speak of and a Sunnah has not come with it’. So the jurists of the Muslims who had disagreed this wrote saying, ‘A Sunnah has not come with it, and the Book (Quran) does not speak of it. Therefore, explain for us why is the whipping until death Obligated upon him?’ So heasws wrote: ‘In the Name of Allahazwj the Beneficent, the Merciful. [40:84] But when they saw Our Punishment, they said: We believe in Allah alone and we deny what we used to associate with Him [40:85] But their belief was not going to profit them when they had seen Our Punishment; (this is) Allah’s Way, which has been excluded regarding His servants, and there the unbelievers are in loss’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So Al-Mutawakkil ordered by it, and he was whipped until he died’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Hanan Bin Sudeyr, (The narrator) says, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a Jew who had been immoral with a Muslim woman. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should be killed’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:46
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ يَهُودِيٍّ فَجَرَ بِمُسْلِمَةٍ قَالَ يُقْتَلُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Hanan Bin Sudeyr, (The narrator) says, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a Jew who had been immoral with a Muslim woman. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should be killed’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘Heasws said: ‘The Penalty of the Jew, and the Christian, and the owned (slaves) regarding the wine and the fabrication is the same. But rather, it is correct for the Ahl Al-Zimma (people under responsibility) that they can drink it in their houses’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ حَدُّ الْيَهُودِيِّ وَ النَّصْرَانِيِّ وَ الْمَمْلُوكِ فِي الْخَمْرِ وَ الْفِرْيَةِ سَوَاءٌ وَ إِنَّمَا صُولِحَ أَهْلُ الذِّمَّةِ عَلَى أَنْ يَشْرَبُوهَا فِي بُيُوتِهِمْ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘Heasws said: ‘The Penalty of the Jew, and the Christian, and the owned (slaves) regarding the wine and the fabrication is the same. text: Yunus, from Sama’at who said, I asked himasws about the Jew, and the Christian who slandered his companion of a same religion, and the Magian who slandered the Muslim. Heasws said: ‘He would be whipped the Penalty (Hadd)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:46
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الْيَهُودِيِّ وَ النَّصْرَانِيِّ يَقْذِفُ صَاحِبَهُ مِلَّةً عَلَى مِلَّةٍ وَ الْمَجُوسِيِّ يَقْذِفُ الْمُسْلِمَ قَالَ يُجْلَدُ الْحَدَّ.
citation.translation: Yunus, from Sama’at who said, I asked himasws about the Jew, and the Christian who slandered his companion of a same religion, and the Magian who slandered the Muslim. Heasws said: ‘He would be whipped the Penalty (Hadd)’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abbad Bin Suheyb who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about a Christian who had slandered a Muslim, so he said to him, ‘O adulterer!’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be whipped eighty lashes due to a right of the Muslim, and eighty lashes except for one due to the sanctity of Al-Islam, and his head would be shaved off, and he would be paraded with among the people of his religion as a lesson for others’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:46
citation.arabic_text: سُئِلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ نَصْرَانِيٍّ قَذَفَ مُسْلِماً فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا زَانِ فَقَالَ يُجْلَدُ ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً لِحَقِّ الْمُسْلِمِ وَ ثَمَانِينَ سَوْطاً إِلَّا سَوْطاً لِحُرْمَةِ الْإِسْلَامِ وَ يُحْلَقُ رَأْسُهُ وَ يُطَافُ بِهِ فِي أَهْلِ دِينِهِ لِكَيْ يُنَكَّلَ غَيْرُهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abbad Bin Suheyb who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about a Christian who had slandered a Muslim, so he said to him, ‘O adulterer!’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be whipped eighty lashes due to a right of the Muslim, and eighty lashes except for one due to the sanctity of Al-Islam, and his head would be shaved off, and he would be paraded with among the people of his religion as a lesson for others’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Al Washa, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws judged that the Jew, and the Christian would be whipped regarding the wine and Al-Nabeez the intoxicant (drink), eighty lashes, when they display drinking it in a city from the cities of the Muslims. And similar to that is the Magian; and they would not be treated harshly when they drink it in their houses and their churches, until they come to be in between the Muslims’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:46
citation.arabic_text: قَضَى أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) أَنْ يُجْلَدَ الْيَهُودِيُّ وَ النَّصْرَانِيُّ فِي الْخَمْرِ وَ النَّبِيذِ الْمُسْكِرِ ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً إِذَا أَظْهَرُوا شُرْبَهُ فِي مِصْرٍ مِنْ أَمْصَارِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَ كَذَلِكَ الْمَجُوسِيُّ وَ لَمْ يَعْرِضْ لَهُمْ إِذَا شَرِبُوهَا فِي مَنَازِلِهِمْ وَ كَنَائِسِهِمْ حَتَّى يَصِيرُوا بَيْنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Al Washa, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws judged that the Jew, and the Christian would be whipped regarding the wine and Al-Nabeez the intoxicant (drink), eighty lashes, when they display drinking it in a city from the cities of the Muslims. And similar to that is the Magian; and they would not be treated harshly when they drink it in their houses and their churches, until they come to be in between the Muslims’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> forbid from slandering one who is not upon Al-Islam except that he emerges upon that, from them’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The easiest of what could happen is that he would happen to have lied’.
