citation.arabic_text: أَيْسَرُ مَا يَكُونُ أَنْ يَكُونَ قَدْ كَذَبَ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> forbid from slandering one who is not upon Al-Islam except that he emerges upon that, from them’. text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> forbid from slandering one who was upon other than Al-Islam, except that he happened to have been notified upon that, from him’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:47
citation.arabic_text: أَنَّهُ نَهَى عَنْ قَذْفِ مَنْ كَانَ عَلَى غَيْرِ الْإِسْلَامِ إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ قَدِ اطَّلَعْتَ عَلَى ذَلِكَ مِنْهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> forbid from slandering one who was upon other than Al-Islam, except that he happened to have been notified upon that, from him’.

text: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Al Hassan Al Haza’a who said, ‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so a man said to me, ‘What did your creditor do?’ I said, ‘That one is a son of a ‘sexually active (immoral) woman’ . So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> looked at me with a harsh look. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! He is a Magian. His mother is his sister’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Or is that not (considered a valid) marriage in their religion?’

citation.arabic_text: كُنْتُ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) فَسَأَلَنِي رَجُلٌ مَا فَعَلَ غَرِيمُكَ قُلْتُ ذَاكَ ابْنُ الْفَاعِلَةِ فَنَظَرَ إِلَيَّ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) نَظَراً شَدِيداً قَالَ فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنَّهُ مَجُوسِيٌّ أُمُّهُ أُخْتُهُ فَقَالَ أَ وَ لَيْسَ ذَلِكَ فِي دِينِهِمْ نِكَاحاً .
citation.translation: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Al Hassan Al Haza’a who said, ‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so a man said to me, ‘What did your creditor do?’ I said, ‘That one is a son of a ‘sexually active (immoral) woman’ . So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> looked at me with a harsh look. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! He is a Magian. His mother is his sister’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Or is that not (considered a valid) marriage in their religion?’

text: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the reprimanding, how much is it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A part of (about) ten lashes, what is between the ten to the twenty’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ التَّعْزِيرِ كَمْ هُوَ قَالَ بِضْعَةَ عَشَرَ سَوْطاً مَا بَيْنَ الْعَشَرَةِ إِلَى الْعِشْرِينَ .
citation.translation: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the reprimanding, how much is it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A part of (about) ten lashes, what is between the ten to the twenty’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunush, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about two men, each one of the two fabricated upon his companion. So heasws said: ‘The Penalty (Hadd) would be staved off from them, and they would both be reprimanded’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ رَجُلَيْنِ افْتَرَى كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا عَلَى صَاحِبِهِ فَقَالَ يُدْرَأُ عَنْهُمَا الْحَدُّ وَ يُعَزَّرَانِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunush, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about two men, each one of the two fabricated upon his companion. text: From him, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah who, said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who insluted a man without slander, would he be treated harshly? Would he be whipped?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon him is a reprimand’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ رَجُلٍ سَبَّ رَجُلًا بِغَيْرِ قَذْفٍ يُعَرِّضُ بِهِ هَلْ يُجْلَدُ قَالَ عَلَيْهِ تَعْزِيرٌ .
citation.translation: From him, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah who, said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who insluted a man without slander, would he be treated harshly? Would he be whipped?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon him is a reprimand’.

text: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ja’far Bin Sama’at, from Aban Bin Usman, from Ismail Bin Al Fazl who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the fabrication upon the Ahl Al-Zimma (under the responsibility), and the people of the Book (Jews and Christians), would the Muslim be whipped the Penalty (Hadd) with regards to the fabrication against them?’ Heasws said: ‘No, but he would be reprimanded’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:48
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الِافْتِرَاءِ عَلَى أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ وَ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ هَلْ يُجْلَدُ الْمُسْلِمُ الْحَدَّ فِي الِافْتِرَاءِ عَلَيْهِمْ قَالَ لَا وَ لَكِنْ يُعَزَّرُ .
citation.translation: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ja’far Bin Sama’at, from Aban Bin Usman, from Ismail Bin Al Fazl who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the fabrication upon the Ahl Al-Zimma (under the responsibility), and the people of the Book (Jews and Christians), would the Muslim be whipped the Penalty (Hadd) with regards to the fabrication against them?’ Heasws said: ‘No, but he would be reprimanded’.

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al hassan Bin Ali, from Hammad Bin Usman who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘How much is the reprimand?’ So heasws said: ‘Less than the Penalty (Hadd)’. I said, ‘Less than eighty (lashes)?’ So heasws said: ‘No, but it is less than the forty (lashes), for it is a Penalty (Hadd) of the owned (slaves)’. I said, ‘And how much is that?’ Heasws said: ‘Upon the measurement of what the guardian sees fit from a sin of the man, and strength of his body’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) كَمِ التَّعْزِيرُ فَقَالَ دُونَ الْحَدِّ قَالَ قُلْتُ دُونَ ثَمَانِينَ قَالَ فَقَالَ لَا وَ لَكِنْ دُونَ الْأَرْبَعِينَ فَإِنَّهُ حَدُّ الْمَمْلُوكِ قَالَ قُلْتُ وَ كَمْ ذَلِكَ قَالَ قَالَ عَلَى قَدْرِ مَا يَرَى الْوَالِي مِنْ ذَنْبِ الرَّجُلِ وَ قُوَّةِ بَدَنِهِ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al hassan Bin Ali, from Hammad Bin Usman who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘How much is the reprimand?’ So heasws said: ‘Less than the Penalty (Hadd)’. I said, ‘Less than eighty (lashes)?’ So heasws said: ‘No, but it is less than the forty (lashes), for it is a Penalty (Hadd) of the owned (slaves)’. I said, ‘And how much is that?’ Heasws said: ‘Upon the measurement of what the guardian sees fit from a sin of the man, and strength of his body’.

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman, from Jarrah Al Madainy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘When the man says to the man, ‘You are filthy’, and ‘You are a pig’, so there is no Penalty (Hadd) with regards to it, but in it is advising, and part of the punishment’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:48
citation.arabic_text: إِذَا قَالَ الرَّجُلُ لِلرَّجُلِ أَنْتَ خَبِيثٌ وَ أَنْتَ خِنْزِيرٌ فَلَيْسَ فِيهِ حَدٌّ وَ لَكِنْ فِيهِ مَوْعِظَةٌ وَ بَعْضُ الْعُقُوبَةِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suleyman, from Jarrah Al Madainy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘When the man says to the man, ‘You are filthy’, and ‘You are a pig’, so there is no Penalty (Hadd) with regards to it, but in it is advising, and part of the punishment’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Zurara, from Sama’at who said, ‘I asked himasws about false testifiers’. So heasws said: ‘They would be whipped the Penalty (Hadd). And as for the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [24:4] and do not accept any testimony from them ever . . . . citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ شُهُودِ الزُّورِ قَالَ فَقَالَ يُجْلَدُونَ حَدّاً لَيْسَ لَهُ وَقْتٌ وَ ذَلِكَ إِلَى الْإِمَامِ وَ يُطَافُ بِهِمْ حَتَّى يَعْرِفَهُمُ النَّاسُ وَ أَمَّا قَوْلُ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ وَ لا تَقْبَلُوا لَهُمْ شَهادَةً أَبَداً... إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تابُوا قَالَ قُلْتُ كَيْفَ تُعْرَفُ تَوْبَتُهُ قَالَ يُكْذِبُ نَفْسَهُ عَلَى رُءُوسِ النَّاسِ حَتَّى يُضْرَبَ وَ يَسْتَغْفِرَ رَبَّهُ وَ إِذَا فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ فَقَدْ ظَهَرَتْ تَوْبَتُهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Zurara, from Sama’at who said, ‘I asked himasws about false testifiers’. So heasws said: ‘They would be whipped the Penalty (Hadd). There is not (fixed) time for it, and that is upon the Imamasws, and they would be paraded with until the the people recognise them’. And as for the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [24:4] and do not accept any testimony from them ever . . . . [24:5] Except those who repent, I said, ‘How is their repentance recognised?’ Heasws said: ‘He would belie himself (confess) to the chiefs of the people until he is whipped, and he would seek Forgiveness of his Lordazwj’. And when he does that, so his repentance would have been manifested’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih Bin Saeed, from one of his companions, from Mansour Bin Hazam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about a man who married a Zimmi woman (woman under the responsibility of the Islamic government) over a Muslim woman, (as a second wife) and did not have her instructions (permission). Heasws said: ‘And there would be separation between the two of them’. So I said, ‘So is there disciplining upon him?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, twelve lashes, and half of eighty being a Penalty (Hadd) of the adulterer, and he would be belittled’. I said, ‘So if the free Muslim woman were to be happy with his deed after what he had done?’ Heasws said: ‘He would not be whipped, nor would there be separation between the two. They would both remain upon the first marriage’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ تَزَوَّجَ ذِمِّيَّةً عَلَى مُسْلِمَةٍ وَ لَمْ يَسْتَأْمِرْهَا قَالَ وَ يُفَرَّقُ بَيْنَهُمَا قَالَ فَقُلْتُ فَعَلَيْهِ أَدَبٌ قَالَ نَعَمْ اثْنَا عَشَرَ سَوْطاً وَ نِصْفٌ ثُمُنُ حَدِّ الزَّانِي وَ هُوَ صَاغِرٌ قُلْتُ فَإِنْ رَضِيَتِ الْمَرْأَةُ الْحُرَّةُ الْمُسْلِمَةُ بِفِعْلِهِ بَعْدَ مَا كَانَ فَعَلَ قَالَ لَا يُضْرَبُ وَ لَا يُفَرَّقُ بَيْنَهُمَا يَبْقَيَانِ عَلَى النِّكَاحِ الْأَوَّلِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih Bin Saeed, from one of his companions, from Mansour Bin Hazam, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about a man who married a Zimmi woman (woman under the responsibility of the Islamic government) over a Muslim woman, (as a second wife) and did not have her instructions (permission). Heasws said: ‘And there would be separation between the two of them’. So I said, ‘So is there disciplining upon him?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, twelve lashes, and half of eighty being a Penalty (Hadd) of the adulterer, and he would be belittled’. I said, ‘So if the free Muslim woman were to be happy with his deed after what he had done?’ Heasws said: ‘He would not be whipped, nor would there be separation between the two. They would both remain upon the first marriage’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Yahya Bin Al Mubarak, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Abu Jameela, from Is’haq Bin Ammar and Sama’at, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘I said, ‘The consumer of the interest after the evidence (is clarified to him)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be disciplined. So if he repeats, he would be disiplined. So if he repeats, he would be killed’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:48
citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ آكِلُ الرِّبَا بَعْدَ الْبَيِّنَةِ قَالَ يُؤَدَّبُ فَإِنْ عَادَ أُدِّبَ فَإِنْ عَادَ قُتِلَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Yahya Bin Al Mubarak, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Abu Jameela, from Is’haq Bin Ammar and Sama’at, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘I said, ‘The consumer of the interest after the evidence (is clarified to him)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be disciplined. So if he repeats, he would be disiplined. So if he repeats, he would be killed’.

text: And by this chain, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The consumer of the dead (animals, fish etc.), and the blood, and the flesh of the swine, upon him is the disciplining. So if he repeats, he is disciplined. So if he repeats, he is disciplined, and there is no Penalty (Hadd) upon him’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:48
citation.arabic_text: آكِلُ الْمَيْتَةِ وَ الدَّمِ وَ لَحْمِ الْخِنْزِيرِ عَلَيْهِ أَدَبٌ فَإِنْ عَادَ أُدِّبَ فَإِنْ عَادَ أُدِّبَ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ حَدٌّ .
citation.translation: And by this chain, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The consumer of the dead (animals, fish etc.), and the blood, and the flesh of the swine, upon him is the disciplining. So if he repeats, he is disciplined. So if he repeats, he is disciplined, and there is no Penalty (Hadd) upon him’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Al Sindy, from Ja’far Bin Basheer, from Al Husayn Bin Abu Al A’la, from Abu Makhlad Al Sarraj, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding a man who called another, ‘Son of the insane’. So the other one said to him, ‘You are a son of the insane’. So he<sup>asws</sup> ordered that the first one (who was slandered) to whip his companion with twenty lashes, and said to him, ‘Know that he is also deserving the like of it, twenty’. So when he had whipped him, he<sup>asws</sup> gave the whip to the whipped one, so he whipped him, being a lesson to be learnt by both of them’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:48
citation.arabic_text: قَضَى أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) فِي رَجُلٍ دَعَا آخَرَ ابْنَ الْمَجْنُونِ فَقَالَ لَهُ الْآخَرُ أَنْتَ ابْنُ الْمَجْنُونِ فَأَمَرَ الْأَوَّلَ أَنْ يَجْلِدَ صَاحِبَهُ عِشْرِينَ جَلْدَةً وَ قَالَ لَهُ اعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ مُسْتَحِقٌّ مِثْلَهَا عِشْرِينَ فَلَمَّا جَلَدَهُ أَعْطَى الْمَجْلُودَ السَّوْطَ فَجَلَدَهُ نَكَالًا يُنَكِّلُ بِهِمَا .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Al Sindy, from Ja’far Bin Basheer, from Al Husayn Bin Abu Al A’la, from Abu Makhlad Al Sarraj, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding a man who called another, ‘Son of the insane’. So the other one said to him, ‘You are a son of the insane’. So he<sup>asws</sup> ordered that the first one (who was slandered) to whip his companion with twenty lashes, and said to him, ‘Know that he is also deserving the like of it, twenty’. So when he had whipped him, he<sup>asws</sup> gave the whip to the whipped one, so he whipped him, being a lesson to be learnt by both of them’.

text: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bandaar, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq Al Ahmar, from Abdullah Bin Hammad Al Ansary, from Mufazzal Bin Umar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding a man who came to his wife and she was Fasting, and he was Fasting’. Heasws said: ‘If she was forced, so upon him would be two expiations, and if she was not forced, so upon him is an expiation and upon her is an expiation, and if she had abhorred it, so upon him would be a whipping of fifty lashes, half the Penalty (Hadd), and if she had obeyed him, he would be whipped twenty five lashes, and she would be whipped fifty lashes’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:48
citation.arabic_text: رَجُلٍ أَتَى امْرَأَتَهُ وَ هِيَ صَائِمَةٌ وَ هُوَ صَائِمٌ قَالَ إِنْ كَانَ قَدِ اسْتَكْرَهَهَا فَعَلَيْهِ كَفَّارَتَانِ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَكْرِهْهَا فَعَلَيْهِ كَفَّارَةٌ وَ عَلَيْهَا كَفَّارَةٌ وَ إِنْ كَانَ أَكْرَهَهَا فَعَلَيْهِ ضَرْبُ خَمْسِينَ سَوْطاً نِصْفِ الْحَدِّ وَ إِنْ كَانَتْ طَاوَعَتْهُ ضُرِبَ خَمْسَةً وَ عِشْرِينَ سَوْطاً وَ ضُرِبَتْ خَمْسَةً وَ عِشْرِينَ سَوْطاً .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bandaar, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq Al Ahmar, from Abdullah Bin Hammad Al Ansary, from Mufazzal Bin Umar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding a man who came to his wife and she was Fasting, and he was Fasting’. Heasws said: ‘If she was forced, so upon him would be two expiations, and if she was not forced, so upon him is an expiation and upon her is an expiation, and if she had abhorred it, so upon him would be a whipping of fifty lashes, half the Penalty (Hadd), and if she had obeyed him, he would be whipped twenty five lashes, and she would be whipped fifty lashes’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih Bin Saeed, from Ismail Bin Al Fazl Al Hasimy who said, ‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about a man who came to his wife and she was in menstruation. Heasws said: ‘He should seek Forgiveness of Allahazwj, and should not repeat it’. I said, ‘So upon him would be the disciplining?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, twenty five lashes, being a quarter of the Penalty (Hadd) of the adulterer, and he would be belittled, because he came unlawfully’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:48
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَتَى أَهْلَهُ وَ هِيَ حَائِضٌ قَالَ يَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ وَ لَا يَعُودُ قُلْتُ فَعَلَيْهِ أَدَبٌ قَالَ نَعَمْ خَمْسَةً وَ عِشْرِينَ سَوْطاً رُبُعَ حَدِّ الزَّانِي وَ هُوَ صَاغِرٌ لِأَنَّهُ أَتَى سِفَاحاً .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih Bin Saeed, from Ismail Bin Al Fazl Al Hasimy who said, ‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about a man who came to his wife and she was in menstruation. Heasws said: ‘He should seek Forgiveness of Allahazwj, and should not repeat it’. I said, ‘So upon him would be the disciplining?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, twenty five lashes, being a quarter of the Penalty (Hadd) of the adulterer, and he would be belittled, because he came unlawfully’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad Al hannat who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying, ‘They came to Amir Al-Momineenasws with two men, each one of them had slandered his companion with the adultery in his body. So heasws staved off the Penalty (Hadd) from both of them, and reprimanded them both’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:48
citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ أُتِيَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) بِرَجُلَيْنِ قَدْ قَذَفَ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا صَاحِبَهُ بِالزِّنَى فِي بَدَنِهِ فَدَرَأَ عَنْهُمَا الْحَدَّ وَ عَزَّرَهُمَا .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad Al Miqary, from Al Noman Bin Abdul Salam, from Abu Haneefa who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a man who said to another, ‘O wicked!’ Heasws said: ‘There is no Penalty (Hadd) upon him, and he would be reprimanded’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:48
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ رَجُلٍ قَالَ لآِخَرَ يَا فَاسِقُ قَالَ لَا حَدَّ عَلَيْهِ وَ يُعَزَّرُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad Al Miqary, from Al Noman Bin Abdul Salam, from Abu Haneefa who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a man who said to another, ‘O wicked!’ Heasws said: ‘There is no Penalty (Hadd) upon him, and he would be reprimanded’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama’at who said, ‘The false testifiers would be whipped a Penalty (Hadd), there being no timing for it, that is up to the Imamasws, and they would be paraded with until they are recognised as such, so they would not repeat’. citation.arabic_text: شُهُودُ الزُّورِ يُجْلَدُونَ حَدّاً لَيْسَ لَهُ وَقْتٌ ذَلِكَ إِلَى الْإِمَامِ وَ يُطَافُ بِهِمْ حَتَّى يُعْرَفُوا فَلَا يَعُودُوا قُلْتُ لَهُ فَإِنْ تَابُوا وَ أَصْلَحُوا تُقْبَلُ شَهَادَتُهُمْ بَعْدُ قَالَ إِذَا تَابُوا تَابَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَ قُبِلَتْ شَهَادَتُهُمْ بَعْدُ .

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:48
citation.arabic_text: رَجُلٍ سَبَّ رَجُلًا بِغَيْرِ قَذْفٍ عَرَّضَ بِهِ هَلْ عَلَيْهِ حَدٌّ قَالَ عَلَيْهِ تَعْزِيرٌ .

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:48
citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَنِ الِافْتِرَاءِ عَلَى أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ هَلْ يُجْلَدُ الْمُسْلِمُ الْحَدَّ فِي الِافْتِرَاءِ عَلَيْهِمْ قَالَ لَا وَ لَكِنْ يُعَزَّرُ .

citation.arabic_text: أُتِيَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) بِرَجُلٍ أَصَابَ حَدّاً وَ بِهِ قُرُوحٌ فِي جَسَدِهِ كَثِيرَةٌ فَقَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) أَخِّرُوهُ حَتَّى يَبْرَأَ لَا تَنْكَئُوهَا عَلَيْهِ فَتَقْتُلُوهُ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abu Hammam, from Muhammad Bin Saeed, from Al Sakuny, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘They came to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> with a man who had numerous sores in his body. text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abu Al Abbas, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘They came to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> with a short, ugly man who had illness in his belly, and the veins of his belly had turned around. He had been immoral with a woman, so she said, ‘I did not know of him except that he entered into me’. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to him: ‘Did you commit adultery?’ So he said, ‘Yes’, and he was not married. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> raised his<sup>saww</sup> gaze and lowered it. Then he<sup>saww</sup> called for a palm branch, counted a hundred, then whipped him with its stalk’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:49
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أُتِيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) بِرَجُلٍ دَمِيمٍ قَصِيرٍ قَدْ سُقِيَ بَطْنُهُ وَ قَدْ دَرَّتْ عُرُوقُ بَطْنِهِ قَدْ فَجَرَ بِامْرَأَةٍ فَقَالَتِ الْمَرْأَةُ مَا عَلِمْتُ بِهِ إِلَّا وَ قَدْ دَخَلَ عَلَيَّ فَقَالَ لَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أَ زَنَيْتَ فَقَالَ نَعَمْ وَ لَمْ يَكُنْ أُحْصِنَ فَصَعَّدَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) بَصَرَهُ وَ خَفَضَهُ ثُمَّ دَعَا بِعِذْقٍ فَعَدَّهُ مِائَةً ثُمَّ ضَرَبَهُ بِشَمَارِيخِهِ .

Then he<sup>saww</sup> called for a palm branch, counted a hundred, then whipped him with its stalk’.

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman Al Assam, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Malik, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws that they came to Amir Al-Momineenasws with a man who was due a Penalty (Hadd), and with him were blisters and an illness, and such like that. So Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Delay it until he is cured. Do not peel off his blisters (by beating him), for he would die, but when he is cured, weasws shall Penalty (Hadd) him’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:49
citation.arabic_text: أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) أَخِّرُوهُ حَتَّى يَبْرَأَ لَا تُنْكَأْ قُرُوحُهُ عَلَيْهِ فَيَمُوتَ وَ لَكِنْ إِذَا بَرَأَ حَدَدْنَاهُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman Al Assam, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Malik, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws that they came to Amir Al-Momineenasws with a man who was due a Penalty (Hadd), and with him were blisters and an illness, and such like that. So Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Delay it until he is cured. Do not peel off his blisters (by beating him), for he would die, but when he is cured, weasws shall Penalty (Hadd) him’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam and Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from someone else from his companions, altogether from Aban Bin Usman, from Abu Salih, Abu Abdullahasws has said: ‘A group of sick people from the Clan of Zabbat came to Rasool-Allahsaww. So Rasool-Allahsaww said to them: ‘Stay with mesaww, so whenever you are cured, Isaww will send you with an escort, secretly. So they said, ‘Get us out from Al-Medina’. So hesaww sent them to the charity camels. They were drinking from their urine and eating from their milk. So when they were cured and became strong, they killed three people who were tending the camels. So (the news) reached Rasool-Allahsaww, so hesaww sent Aliasws to them, and they were in a valley and were confused (of their way) and did not have the ability to come out from it, near to the land of Al-Yemen. So heasws captured them and came with them to Rasool-Allahsaww. So this Verse was Revealed unto himsaww [5:33] But rather, the Recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Rasool and strive to make mischief in the land is only this, that they should be killed or crucified or their hands and their feet should be cut off on opposite sides or they should be exiled from the land. So Rasool-Allahsaww chose the cutting, so hesaww cut their hands, and their feet from opposite sides’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A group of people came to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>, so they said, ‘السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ يَا رَبَّنَا’ ‘Peace be upon you<sup>asws</sup>, O our Lord!’ So he<sup>asws</sup> told them to repent, but they did not repent. citation.arabic_text: أَتَى قَوْمٌ أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالُوا السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ يَا رَبَّنَا فَاسْتَتَابَهُمْ فَلَمْ يَتُوبُوا فَحَفَرَ لَهُمْ حَفِيرَةً وَ أَوْقَدَ فِيهَا نَاراً وَ حَفَرَ حَفِيرَةً أُخْرَى إِلَى جَانِبِهَا وَ أَفْضَى بَيْنَهُمَا فَلَمَّا لَمْ يَتُوبُوا أَلْقَاهُمْ فِي الْحَفِيرَةِ وَ أَوْقَدَ فِي الْحَفِيرَةِ الْأُخْرَى حَتَّى مَاتُوا .

citation.arabic_text: مَنْ أُخِذَ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ وَ قَدْ أَفْطَرَ فَرُفِعَ إِلَى الْإِمَامِ يُقْتَلُ فِي الثَّالِثَةِ .

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ بَزِيعاً يَزْعُمُ أَنَّهُ نَبِيٌّ فَقَالَ إِنْ سَمِعْتَهُ يَقُولُ ذَلِكَ فَاقْتُلْهُ قَالَ فَجَلَسْتُ لَهُ غَيْرَ مَرَّةٍ فَلَمْ يُمْكِنِّي ذَلِكَ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Ibn Abu Yafour who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that, Baziya alleges that he is a Prophet. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If you were to hear him saying that, you should kill him’. He said, ‘So I sat with (awaiting) for him many a time, but was not able over that’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abul Rahman Al Abzary Al Kunasy, from Al Haris Bin Al Mugheira who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view if a man came to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so he said, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I do not know whether you<sup>saww</sup> are a Prophet<sup>saww</sup> or not, would he<sup>saww</sup> have accepted from him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No! But, he<sup>saww</sup> would have killed him. If he<sup>saww</sup> had accepted from him, no hypocrite would ever become a Muslim’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) أَ رَأَيْتَ لَوْ أَنَّ رَجُلًا أَتَى النَّبِيَّ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَقَالَ وَ اللَّهِ مَا أَدْرِي أَ نَبِيٌّ أَنْتَ أَمْ لَا كَانَ يَقْبَلُ مِنْهُ قَالَ لَا وَ لَكِنْ كَانَ يَقْتُلُهُ إِنَّهُ لَوْ قَبِلَ ذَلِكَ مِنْهُ مَا أَسْلَمَ مُنَافِقٌ أَبَداً .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abul Rahman Al Abzary Al Kunasy, from Al Haris Bin Al Mugheira who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view if a man came to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so he said, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I do not know whether you<sup>saww</sup> are a Prophet<sup>saww</sup> or not, would he<sup>saww</sup> have accepted from him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No! But, he<sup>saww</sup> would have killed him. If he<sup>saww</sup> had accepted from him, no hypocrite would ever become a Muslim’.

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Mallik, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘They came to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> with an atheist, so he<sup>asws</sup> struck his neck. So it was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘He had a lot of wealth for him, so for whom would his wealth be for?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For his children, and for his inheritors, and for his wife’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:61
citation.arabic_text: أُتِيَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) بِزِنْدِيقٍ فَضَرَبَ عِلَاوَتَهُ فَقِيلَ لَهُ إِنَّ لَهُ مَالًا كَثِيراً فَلِمَنْ يُجْعَلُ مَالُهُ قَالَ لِوُلْدِهِ وَ لِوَرَثَتِهِ وَ لِزَوْجَتِهِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Mallik, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘They came to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> with an atheist, so he<sup>asws</sup> struck his neck. So it was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘He had a lot of wealth for him, so for whom would his wealth be for?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For his children, and for his inheritors, and for his wife’.

text: And by this chain, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> had judged regarding an atheist when two just, acceptable witnesses testify against him, they testify for him a thousand with the freeing him. He<sup>asws</sup> allowed the testimony of two men and invalidated the testimonies of a thousand because it is an undisclosed religion’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:61
citation.arabic_text: وَ بِهَذَا الْإِسْنَادِ أَنَّ أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( صلوات الله عليه ) كَانَ يَحْكُمُ فِي زِنْدِيقٍ إِذَا شَهِدَ عَلَيْهِ رَجُلَانِ عَدْلَانِ مَرْضِيَّانِ وَ شَهِدَ لَهُ أَلْفٌ بِالْبَرَاءَةِ جَازَتْ شَهَادَةُ الرَّجُلَيْنِ وَ أَبْطَلَ شَهَادَةَ الْأَلْفِ لِأَنَّهُ دِينٌ مَكْتُومٌ .
citation.translation: And by this chain, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> had judged regarding an atheist when two just, acceptable witnesses testify against him, they testify for him a thousand with the freeing him. He<sup>asws</sup> allowed the testimony of two men and invalidated the testimonies of a thousand because it is an undisclosed religion’.

text: And by this chain, said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘(As for the) apostate, his wife should isolate herself from him, and she should not eat meat slaughtered by him, and he would be given three days to repent, so if he does repent (fine), or else he would be killed on the fourth day’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:61
citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) الْمُرْتَدُّ تُعْزَلُ عَنْهُ امْرَأَتُهُ وَ لَا تُؤْكَلُ ذَبِيحَتُهُ وَ يُسْتَتَابُ ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ فَإِنْ تَابَ وَ إِلَّا قُتِلَ يَوْمَ الرَّابِعِ .
citation.translation: And by this chain, said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘(As for the) apostate, his wife should isolate herself from him, and she should not eat meat slaughtered by him, and he would be given three days to repent, so if he does repent (fine), or else he would be killed on the fourth day’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A group of people came to Amir Al-Momineen, so they said, ‘Peace be upon you<sup>asws</sup>, ‘السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ يَا رَبَّنَا’ O our Lord! So he told them to repent, but they did not repent. So he<sup>asws</sup> dug out a pit for them and ignited a fire in it, and dug out another pit to its side, and bore a hole between these two. So when they did not repent, he<sup>asws</sup> cast them into the pit, and ignited fire in the other pit, until they died’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:61
citation.arabic_text: أَتَى قَوْمٌ أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) فَقَالُوا السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ يَا رَبَّنَا فَاسْتَتَابَهُمْ فَلَمْ يَتُوبُوا فَحَفَرَ لَهُمْ حَفِيرَةً وَ أَوْقَدَ فِيهَا نَاراً وَ حَفَرَ حَفِيرَةً أُخْرَى إِلَى جَانِبِهَا وَ أَفْضَى مَا بَيْنَهُمَا فَلَمَّا لَمْ يَتُوبُوا أَلْقَاهُمْ فِي الْحَفِيرَةِ وَ أَوْقَدَ فِي الْحَفِيرَةِ الْأُخْرَى [نَاراً] حَتَّى مَاتُوا .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A group of people came to Amir Al-Momineen, so they said, ‘Peace be upon you<sup>asws</sup>, ‘السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ يَا رَبَّنَا’ O our Lord! So he told them to repent, but they did not repent. So he<sup>asws</sup> dug out a pit for them and ignited a fire in it, and dug out another pit to its side, and bore a hole between these two. So when they did not repent, he<sup>asws</sup> cast them into the pit, and ignited fire in the other pit, until they died’.

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubeyda, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The slave, when he is a fugitive from his master, then steals, he would not be cut, and he is a fugitive, because he is a renegade from Al-Islam, but he would be called to the return to his master, and the entry into the fold of Al-Islam. So if he were to refuse to return to his master, his hand would be cut due to the theft, then he would be killed; and the apostate, when he steals is at his status’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:61
citation.arabic_text: الْعَبْدُ إِذَا أَبَقَ مِنْ مَوَالِيهِ ثُمَّ سَرَقَ لَمْ يُقْطَعْ وَ هُوَ آبِقٌ لِأَنَّهُ مُرْتَدٌّ عَنِ الْإِسْلَامِ وَ لَكِنْ يُدْعَى إِلَى الرُّجُوعِ إِلَى مَوَالِيهِ وَ الدُّخُولِ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ فَإِنْ أَبَى أَنْ يَرْجِعَ إِلَى مَوَالِيهِ قُطِعَتْ يَدُهُ بِالسَّرِقَةِ ثُمَّ قُتِلَ وَ الْمُرْتَدُّ إِذَا سَرَقَ بِمَنْزِلَتِهِ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubeyda, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The slave, when he is a fugitive from his master, then steals, he would not be cut, and he is a fugitive, because he is a renegade from Al-Islam, but he would be called to the return to his master, and the entry into the fold of Al-Islam. So if he were to refuse to return to his master, his hand would be cut due to the theft, then he would be killed; and the apostate, when he steals is at his status’.

text: Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Bureyd Al Ajaly who said, ‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> was asked about a man against whom witnesses testified that he had broken a Fast from the Month of Ramazan for three days. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be asked, ‘Is there a sin upon you with regards to your breaking the Fast?’ So if he says, ‘No’, then it would be upon the Imam<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> should kill him; and if he were to say, ‘Yes’, so it would be upon the Imam<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> blights him with the whipping’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:61
citation.arabic_text: سُئِلَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ رَجُلٍ شَهِدَ عَلَيْهِ شُهُودٌ أَنَّهُ أَفْطَرَ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ فَقَالَ يُسْأَلُ هَلْ عَلَيْكَ فِي إِفْطَارِكَ إِثْمٌ فَإِنْ قَالَ لَا فَإِنَّ عَلَى الْإِمَامِ أَنْ يَقْتُلَهُ وَ إِنْ هُوَ قَالَ نَعَمْ فَإِنَّ عَلَى الْإِمَامِ أَنْ يَنْهَكَهُ ضَرْباً .
citation.translation: Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Bureyd Al Ajaly who said, ‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> was asked about a man against whom witnesses testified that he had broken a Fast from the Month of Ramazan for three days. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be asked, ‘Is there a sin upon you with regards to your breaking the Fast?’ So if he says, ‘No’, then it would be upon the Imam<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> should kill him; and if he were to say, ‘Yes’, so it would be upon the Imam<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> blights him with the whipping’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about the one who insults Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should be killed for the lowest (of insults), as a minimum, before he is brought to the Imam<sup>asws</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: يَقْتُلُهُ الْأَدْنَى فَالْأَدْنَى قَبْلَ أَنْ يَرْفَعَهُ إِلَى الْإِمَامِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about the one who insults Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should be killed for the lowest (of insults), as a minimum, before he is brought to the Imam<sup>asws</sup>’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Hammad Bin usman, from Ibn Abu Yafour who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that Bazi’a is claiming that he is a Prophet. citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) إِنَّ بَزِيعاً يَزْعُمُ أَنَّهُ نَبِيٌّ قَالَ فَإِنْ سَمِعْتَهُ يَقُولُ ذَلِكَ فَاقْتُلْهُ قَالَ فَجَلَسْتُ غَيْرَ مَرَّةٍ فَلَمْ يُمْكِنِّي ذَلِكَ .

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So if you were to hear him saying that, so kill him’. He (the narrator) said, ‘I sat awaiting more than once, but I was not able to do that’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Salih Bin Sahl, from Kirdayn, (It has been narrated) from a man from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said that when Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was free from the people of Al-Basra (Battle of the Camel), seventy men from Al-Zat came over. citation.arabic_text: إِنَّ أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) لَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْبَصْرَةِ أَتَاهُ سَبْعُونَ رَجُلًا مِنَ الزُّطِّ فَسَلَّمُوا عَلَيْهِ وَ كَلَّمُوهُ بِلِسَانِهِمْ فَرَدَّ عَلَيْهِمْ بِلِسَانِهِمْ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُمْ إِنِّي لَسْتُ كَمَا قُلْتُمْ أَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ مَخْلُوقٌ فَأَبَوْا عَلَيْهِ وَ قَالُوا أَنْتَ هُوَ فَقَالَ لَهُمْ لَئِنْ لَمْ تَنْتَهُوا وَ تَرْجِعُوا عَمَّا قُلْتُمْ فِيَّ وَ تَتُوبُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ لَأَقْتُلَنَّكُمْ فَأَبَوْا أَنْ يَرْجِعُوا وَ يَتُوبُوا فَأَمَرَ أَنْ تُحْفَرَ لَهُمْ آبَارٌ فَحُفِرَتْ ثُمَّ خَرَقَ بَعْضَهَا إِلَى بَعْضٍ ثُمَّ قَذَفَهُمْ فِيهَا ثُمَّ خَمَّرَ رُءُوسَهَا ثُمَّ أُلْهِبَتِ النَّارُ فِي بِئْرٍ مِنْهَا لَيْسَ فِيهَا أَحَدٌ مِنْهُمْ فَدَخَلَ الدُّخَانُ عَلَيْهِمْ فِيهَا فَمَاتُوا .

text: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al Mahmoudy, from his father, from Yunus, from Al Husayn Bin Khalid, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I heard himasws saying: ‘It is Obligatory upon the Imamasws when heasws finds a man committing adultery, or drinking the wine, that heasws should established the Penalty (Hadd) upon him, and heasws is not needy of any proof along with hisasws vision, because heasws is a Trustee of Allahazwj among Hisazwj creatures. And when heasws looks at a man who steals, so it is Obligatory upon himasws that heasws reprimands him, and forbids him, and goes and leaves him’. I said, ‘How can that be so?’ Heasws said: ‘Because the truth, if it was for the Sake of Allahazwj, so it is Obligatory upon the Imamasws to stand by it, and when it was for the people, so it is for the people (to stand by it)’.

citation.chapter: THE BOOK OF LEGAL PENALTIES (al-Kafi, vol 7), 3:63

citation.arabic_text: ثَلَاثٍ رَجُلٍ أَكَلَ مَالَ الْيَتِيمِ أَوْ غَصَبَهُ أَوْ رَجُلٍ اؤْتُمِنَ عَلَى أَمَانَةٍ فَذَهَبَ بِهَا .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘Sometimes I hit the slave regarding something which is Prohibited’. citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) إِذَا كَانَ الرَّجُلُ كَلَامُهُ كَلَامَ النِّسَاءِ وَ مِشْيَتُهُ مِشْيَةَ النِّسَاءِ وَ يُمَكِّنُ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ فَيُنْكَحُ كَمَا تُنْكَحُ الْمَرْأَةُ فَارْجُمُوهُ وَ لَا تَسْتَحْيُوهُ.

citation.arabic_text: وَ بِهَذَا الْإِسْنَادِ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) مَنْ بَلَغَ حَدّاً فِي غَيْرِ حَدٍّ فَهُوَ مِنَ الْمُعْتَدِينَ .

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws sent someone to Bishr Bin Utaradi Al-Tameemy regarding a speech which reached himasws. So the messenger of Amir Al-Momineenasws passed by him among the Clan of Asad and seized him. So Nuaym Bin Dajaja Al-Asady stood up to him and had him released. So Amir Al-Momineenasws sent someone to him, so he came up with him, and heasws ordered for him to be whipped. So Nuaym said to himasws, ‘But, by Allahazwj, the staying with youasws is a disgrace, and in separation from youasws is infidelity’. So when heasws heard that from him, heasws said to him: ‘O Nuaym! Weasws have excused you, for Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [23:96] Repel evil by what is best. As for your words that, ‘Staying with youasws is disgrace’, so it is an evil which you have attained; and as for your words, ‘In separation from youasws is infidelity’, so it is a good deed which you have attained. So this here (compensates) for this’. Then heasws ordered that he be released from it’.

text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Aban, from Ali Bin Ismail, from Amro Bin Abu Al Maqdam, from a man, from Razeyn who said, ‘I was performing ablution in the washing facilities of Al-Kufa, so there was a man who had come over. So he took-off his shoes, and placed his whip upon it. Then he approached me, so he performed ablution along with me. So I bumped him, and he fell upon his hands. So he arose and performed ablution. So when he was free, he struck my head with the whip, three times, then said: ‘Beware of bumping, so if you break (somebody’s bone), you will (have to pay) compensation’. So I said, ‘Who is this?’ So they (people) said, ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>’. So I went to offer my excuses, but he<sup>asws</sup> went and did not turn towards me’.

citation.arabic_text: كُنْتُ أَتَوَضَّأُ فِي مِيضَاةِ الْكُوفَةِ فَإِذَا رَجُلٌ قَدْ جَاءَ فَوَضَعَ نَعْلَيْهِ وَ وَضَعَ دِرَّتَهُ فَوْقَهَا ثُمَّ دَنَا فَتَوَضَّأَ مَعِي فَزَحَمْتُهُ فَوَقَعَ عَلَى يَدَيْهِ فَقَامَ فَتَوَضَّأَ فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ ضَرَبَ رَأْسِي بِالدِّرَّةِ ثَلَاثاً ثُمَّ قَالَ إِيَّاكَ أَنْ تَدْفَعَ فَتَكْسِرَ فَتُغَرَّمَ فَقُلْتُ مَنْ هَذَا فَقَالُوا أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ( عليه السلام ) فَذَهَبْتُ أَعْتَذِرُ إِلَيْهِ فَمَضَى وَ لَمْ يَلْتَفِتْ إِلَيَّ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Matar Bin Arqam who said, ‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying that Abul Aziz Bin Umar the governor sent an escort to me, so I<sup>asws</sup> went over to him, and in front of him were two men, one of them had grabbed his companions, so he scratched his face, and he (the governor) said, ‘What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying, O Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding these two men?’ I<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘And what did they both say?’ He said, ‘One of them said, ‘There is not merit for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> over anyone from the Clan of Umayya with regards to the nobility’, and the other one said to him, ‘He<sup>saww</sup> has the merit over the people, all of them, regarding every thing’, and the one who supported Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> got angered, so he did with his face what you<sup>asws</sup> see. So is there anything upon him?’ So I<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> think you have already asked the ones around you, so they have informed you’. So he said, ‘I swear to you<sup>asws</sup>, I have not said it’. So I<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It would be befitting for the one who alleges that anyone is similar to Rasool-Allah<sup>azwj</sup> with regards to the merits, that he should be killed, and not be left to live’. So he said, ‘Or is not the nobility of descent, one?’ So I<sup>asws</sup> said:’ The nobility is not the lineage. Do you not see, if I<sup>asws</sup> were to lodge a man from some of these races, your poor ones, so I said, ‘This is the nobility (that would be allowed)’. So he said, ‘Is not the lineage, one?’ I<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When it is gathered to Adam<sup>as</sup>, so the lineage is one, (except that) Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> did not mix with Polytheism, nor unchasteness’. So the governor ordered it, so he was killed’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ إِنَّ عَبْدَ الْعَزِيزِ بْنَ عُمَرَ الْوَالِيَ بَعَثَ إِلَيَّ فَأَتَيْتُهُ وَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ رَجُلَانِ قَدْ تَنَاوَلَ أَحَدُهُمَا صَاحِبَهُ فَمَرَشَ وَجْهَهُ وَ قَالَ مَا تَقُولُ يَا أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ فِي هَذَيْنِ الرَّجُلَيْنِ قُلْتُ وَ مَا قَالَا قَالَ قَالَ أَحَدُهُمَا لَيْسَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَضْلٌ عَلَى أَحَدٍ مِنْ بَنِي أُمَيَّةَ فِي الْحَسَبِ وَ قَالَ الْآخَرُ لَهُ الْفَضْلُ عَلَى النَّاسِ كُلِّهِمْ فِي كُلِّ حِينٍ وَ غَضِبَ الَّذِي نَصَرَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فَصَنَعَ بِوَجْهِهِ مَا تَرَى فَهَلْ عَلَيْهِ شَيْ‏ءٌ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ إِنِّي أَظُنُّكَ قَدْ سَأَلْتَ مَنْ حَوْلَكَ فَأَخْبَرُوكَ فَقَالَ أَقْسَمْتُ عَلَيْكَ لَمَّا قُلْتَ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ كَانَ يَنْبَغِي لِلَّذِي زَعَمَ أَنَّ أَحَداً مِثْلُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) فِي الْفَضْلِ أَنْ يُقْتَلَ وَ لَا يُسْتَحْيَا قَالَ فَقَالَ أَ وَ مَا الْحَسَبُ بِوَاحِدٍ فَقُلْتُ إِنَّ الْحَسَبَ لَيْسَ النَّسَبَ أَ لَا تَرَى لَوْ نَزَلْتَ بِرَجُلٍ مِنْ بَعْضِ هَذِهِ الْأَجْنَاسِ فَقَرَاكَ فَقُلْتَ إِنَّ هَذَا الْحَسَبُ [لَجَازَ ذَلِكَ] فَقَالَ أَ وَ مَا النَّسَبُ بِوَاحِدٍ قُلْتُ إِذَا اجْتَمَعَا إِلَى آدَمَ ( عليه السلام ) فَإِنَّ النَّسَبَ وَاحِدٌ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لَمْ يَخْلِطْهُ شِرْكٌ وَ لَا بَغْيٌ فَأَمَرَ بِهِ الْوَالِي فَقُتِلَ .

So I said, ‘So what are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding a man who is hurting us?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘With regards to what?’ I said, ‘He is hurting us regarding you<sup>asws</sup>, by mentioning you<sup>asws</sup> (in derogatory terms)?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Is there a share for him with regards to Ali<sup>asws</sup>?’ I said, ‘He is saying that and manifesting it’. text: Ali BIin Ibrahim narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Uqba, from Abu Khalid Al Qammat, from Humran who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘What is the Meaning of the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [5:32] For this reason did We Prescribe to the Children of Israel that whoever slays a soul, unless it be for manslaughter or for mischief in the land, it is as though he slew all the people. I said, ‘And how come it is as if he has killed all the people, for he has (only) killed one?’ So heasws said: ‘He would be placed in a place of Hell where the harshest of Punishments would end up to be upon its inhabitants, had he killed the people altogether. But rather, he would enter that place’. I said, ‘So if he were to kill another one?’ Heasws said: ‘It would be doubled upon him’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) مَا مَعْنَى قَوْلِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ مِنْ أَجْلِ ذلِكَ كَتَبْنا عَلى بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ أَنَّهُ مَنْ قَتَلَ نَفْساً بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ أَوْ فَسادٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَكَأَنَّما قَتَلَ النَّاسَ جَمِيعاً قَالَ قُلْتُ وَ كَيْفَ فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ النَّاسَ جَمِيعاً فَإِنَّمَا قَتَلَ وَاحِداً فَقَالَ يُوضَعُ فِي مَوْضِعٍ مِنْ جَهَنَّمَ إِلَيْهِ يَنْتَهِي شِدَّةُ عَذَابِ أَهْلِهَا لَوْ قَتَلَ النَّاسَ جَمِيعاً إِنَّمَا كَانَ يَدْخُلُ ذَلِكَ الْمَكَانَ قُلْتُ فَإِنَّهُ قَتَلَ آخَرَ قَالَ يُضَاعَفُ عَلَيْهِ.
citation.translation: Ali BIin Ibrahim narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Uqba, from Abu Khalid Al Qammat, from Humran who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘What is the Meaning of the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [5:32] For this reason did We Prescribe to the Children of Israel that whoever slays a soul, unless it be for manslaughter or for mischief in the land, it is as though he slew all the people. I said, ‘And how come it is as if he has killed all the people, for he has (only) killed one?’ So heasws said: ‘He would be placed in a place of Hell where the harshest of Punishments would end up to be upon its inhabitants, had he killed the people altogether. But rather, he would enter that place’. I said, ‘So if he were to kill another one?’ Heasws said: ‘It would be doubled upon him’.

text: Ali, from his father, from Amro Bin Usman, from Al Mufazzal Bin Salih, from Jabir Bin Yazeed, Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> has said that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The first of what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Judge on the Day of Judgement would be regarding the blood-shed. So He<sup>azwj</sup> would Pause the two sons of Adam<sup>as</sup>, so He<sup>azwj</sup> would Decide between the two of them. Then it would be those from the committers of the blood-shed who stained themselves by what they (the sons of Adam<sup>as</sup>) did, until there does not remain anyone from them. Then it would be the (other) people after that, to the extent that the murdered one would come with his murderer, so his face would be soaked in his blood, so he would be saying, ‘This one killed me’. So He<sup>azwj</sup> would be Saying: “Did you kill him?’ So he would not be able to conceal any statement from Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) أَوَّلُ مَا يَحْكُمُ اللَّهُ فِيهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ الدِّمَاءُ فَيُوقِفُ ابْنَيْ آدَمَ فَيَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمَا ثُمَّ الَّذِينَ يَلُونَهُمَا مِنْ أَصْحَابِ الدِّمَاءِ حَتَّى لَا يَبْقَى مِنْهُمْ أَحَدٌ ثُمَّ النَّاسَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ حَتَّى يَأْتِيَ الْمَقْتُولُ بِقَاتِلِهِ فَيَتَشَخَّبَ فِي دَمِهِ وَجْهُهُ فَيَقُولَ هَذَا قَتَلَنِي فَيَقُولُ أَنْتَ قَتَلْتَهُ فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ يَكْتُمَ اللَّهَ حَدِيثاً .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Abu Al Jaroud, Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘There is none from the killed soul, righteous or immoral, except that it would be Resurrected on the Day of Judgement holding on to his murderer by right hand, and his (own severed) head in his left hand and his veins streaming blood. He would be saying, ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! Ask this one, why did he kill me?’ So if it was such that his killing was in obedience of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, they would bring the killer to the Paradise and go with the killed one to the Fire; and if it was in obedience to so and so (other than Allah<sup>azwj</sup>), it would be said to him, ‘Kill him just as he had killed you’. Then Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Deal with the two of them afterwards as He<sup>azwj</sup> Wishes to’.

citation.arabic_text: مَا مِنْ نَفْسٍ تُقْتَلُ بَرَّةٍ وَ لَا فَاجِرَةٍ إِلَّا وَ هِيَ تُحْشَرُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ مُتَعَلِّقَةً بِقَاتِلِهِ بِيَدِهِ الْيُمْنَى وَ رَأْسُهُ بِيَدِهِ الْيُسْرَى وَ أَوْدَاجُهُ تَشْخُبُ دَماً يَقُولُ يَا رَبِّ سَلْ هَذَا فِيمَ قَتَلَنِي فَإِنْ كَانَ قَتَلَهُ فِي طَاعَةِ اللَّهِ أُثِيبَ الْقَاتِلُ الْجَنَّةَ وَ أُذْهِبَ بِالْمَقْتُولِ إِلَى النَّارِ وَ إِنْ قَالَ فِي طَاعَةِ فُلَانٍ قِيلَ لَهُ اقْتُلْهُ كَمَا قَتَلَكَ ثُمَّ يَفْعَلُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فِيهِمَا بَعْدُ مَشِيئَةً .

Then Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Deal with the two of them afterwards as He<sup>azwj</sup> Wishes to’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly, (It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Do not be deceived by the embrace of the two arms with the blood, for it, in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is a killer who does not die’. They said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! And what is the killer who does not die?’ So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The Fire (of Hell)’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لَا يَغُرَّنَّكُمْ رَحْبُ الذِّرَاعَيْنِ بِالدَّمِ فَإِنَّ لَهُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ قَاتِلًا لَا يَمُوتُ قَالُوا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَ مَا قَاتِلٌ لَا يَمُوتُ فَقَالَ النَّارُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly, (It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Do not be deceived by the embrace of the two arms with the blood, for it, in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is a killer who does not die’. They said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! And what is the killer who does not die?’ So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The Fire (of Hell)’.

text: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Abu Ubeyda, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Do not let the embrace of the two arms with the blood cause you to wonder, for it, in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, is a killer who does not die’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) لَا يُعْجِبُكَ رَحْبُ الذِّرَاعَيْنِ بِالدَّمِ فَإِنَّ لَهُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ قَاتِلًا لَا يَمُوتُ .
citation.translation: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Abu Ubeyda, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Do not let the embrace of the two arms with the blood cause you to wonder, for it, in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, is a killer who does not die’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabie Bin Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [5:32] whoever slays a soul, unless it be for manslaughter . . . it is as though he slew all the people. Heasws said: ‘For him is a seat in the Fire, had he killed the people altogether, he would not have been Returned, except to that (very) place’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ ( عليه السلام ) عَنْ قَوْلِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ مَنْ قَتَلَ نَفْساً بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ... فَكَأَنَّما قَتَلَ النَّاسَ جَمِيعاً قَالَ لَهُ فِي النَّارِ مَقْعَدٌ لَوْ قَتَلَ النَّاسَ جَمِيعاً لَمْ يَرِدْ إِلَّا إِلَى ذَلِكَ الْمَقْعَدِ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabie Bin Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, ‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [5:32] whoever slays a soul, unless it be for manslaughter . . . it is as though he slew all the people. text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The Believer does not cease to be in ample space (leeway) in his Religion for as long as he does not shed blood unlawfully’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The killer of the Believer deliberately, would not be given the opportunity for the repentance’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا يَزَالُ الْمُؤْمِنُ فِي فُسْحَةٍ مِنْ دِينِهِ مَا لَمْ يُصِبْ دَماً حَرَاماً وَ قَالَ لَا يُوَفَّقُ قَاتِلُ الْمُؤْمِنِ مُتَعَمِّداً لِلتَّوْبَةِ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The Believer does not cease to be in ample space (leeway) in his Religion for as long as he does not shed blood unlawfully’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The killer of the Believer deliberately, would not be given the opportunity for the repentance’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Abu Hamza, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘(Someone) came to Rasool-Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so he said to him<sup>saww</sup>: ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! He<sup>saww</sup> said, and the people heard him<sup>saww</sup>, so they came over, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Who had done that killing?’ They said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! We do not know’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It would be said to him: ‘Die whichever death you like – if you so like, as a Jew, and if you so like, as a Christian, and if you so like, as a Magian!’.

citation.arabic_text: رَجُلٍ قَتَلَ رَجُلًا مُؤْمِناً قَالَ يُقَالُ لَهُ مُتْ أَيَّ مِيتَةٍ شِئْتَ إِنْ شِئْتَ يَهُودِيّاً وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ نَصْرَانِيّاً وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ مَجُوسِيّاً .
citation.translation: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Saeed Al Arzaq, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who killed a Believing man. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It would be said to him: ‘Die whichever death you like – if you so like, as a Jew, and if you so like, as a Christian, and if you so like, as a Magian!’.

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said that the man would be brought on the Day of Judgement, and on him would be the (minimum amount of) blood - of the measurement of a cup, so he would be saying, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! text: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from a man, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘He would not be entering the Paradise, the one who shed the blood, nor the one who drank the wine, nor a slandering backbiter’.

citation.arabic_text: لَا يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ سَافِكُ الدَّمِ وَ لَا شَارِبُ الْخَمْرِ وَ لَا مَشَّاءٌ بِنَمِيمٍ .
citation.translation: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from a man, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘He would not be entering the Paradise, the one who shed the blood, nor the one who drank the wine, nor a slandering backbiter’.

text: Ali Bin IBrahi, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Asama Zayd Al Shaham, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> paused at Mina where he<sup>saww</sup> fulfilled his<sup>saww</sup> rituals during the Farewell Hajj. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O you people! Listen to what I<sup>saww</sup> am saying to you all, and understand from me<sup>saww</sup>, for I<sup>saww</sup> do not know, perhaps I<sup>saww</sup> would not meet you all again during this year of ours’. Then he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Which day is greatest in sanctity?’ They said, ‘This day!’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘So which month is greatest in sanctity?’ They said, ‘This month!’ He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘So which city is greatest in sanctity?’ They said, ‘This city!’ He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘So your blood, and your wealth are sacred upon you like the sacredness of this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this city of yours, up to the day you meet Him<sup>azwj</sup>, so He<sup>azwj</sup> would be Questioning you about your deeds. citation.arabic_text: وُجِدَ فِي ذُؤَابَةِ سَيْفِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) صَحِيفَةٌ مَكْتُوبٌ فِيهَا لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ وَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ عَلَى مَنْ أَحْدَثَ حَدَثاً أَوْ آوَى مُحْدِثاً وَ مَنِ ادَّعَى إِلَى غَيْرِ أَبِيهِ فَهُوَ كَافِرٌ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ وَ مَنِ ادَّعَى إِلَى غَيْرِ مَوَالِيهِ فَعَلَيْهِ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ .

text: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [4:93] And whoever kills a Believer deliberately, his Punishment is Hell; he shall abide in it eternally, said: ‘The one who kills a Believer upon his Religion, so that is the deliberation which Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Speaks of and Prepare for him a Painful Punishment’. I said, ‘So what happens if something takes place between two persons, so he strikes him with his sword, so he kills him?’ Heasws said: ‘That is not the deliberation (pre-meditated killer) whom Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Speaks of’.

citation.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ قَوْلِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ وَ مَنْ يَقْتُلْ مُؤْمِناً مُتَعَمِّداً فَجَزاؤُهُ جَهَنَّمُ [خالِداً فِيها] قَالَ مَنْ قَتَلَ مُؤْمِناً عَلَى دِينِهِ فَذَلِكَ الْمُتَعَمِّدُ الَّذِي قَالَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ وَ أَعَدَّ لَهُ عَذاباً عَظِيماً قُلْتُ فَالرَّجُلُ يَقَعُ بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَ الرَّجُلِ شَيْ‏ءٌ فَيَضْرِبُهُ بِسَيْفِهِ فَيَقْتُلُهُ قَالَ لَيْسَ ذَلِكَ الْمُتَعَمِّدَ الَّذِي قَالَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ .

citation.arabic_text: سُئِلَ عَنِ الْمُؤْمِنِ يَقْتُلُ الْمُؤْمِنَ مُتَعَمِّداً أَ لَهُ تَوْبَةٌ فَقَالَ إِنْ كَانَ قَتَلَهُ لِإِيمَانِهِ فَلَا تَوْبَةَ لَهُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ قَتَلَهُ لِغَضَبٍ أَوْ لِسَبَبِ شَيْ‏ءٍ مِنْ أَمْرِ الدُّنْيَا فَإِنَّ تَوْبَتَهُ أَنْ يُقَادَ مِنْهُ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ عُلِمَ بِهِ انْطَلَقَ إِلَى أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَقْتُولِ فَأَقَرَّ عِنْدَهُمْ بِقَتْلِ صَاحِبِهِمْ فَإِنْ عَفَوْا عَنْهُ فَلَمْ يَقْتُلُوهُ أَعْطَاهُمُ الدِّيَةَ وَ أَعْتَقَ نَسَمَةً وَ صَامَ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ وَ أَطْعَمَ سِتِّينَ مِسْكِيناً تَوْبَةً إِلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ .

citation.arabic_text: يُقَادُ بِهِ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يُعْلَمْ بِهِ انْطَلَقَ إِلَى أَوْلِيَائِهِ فَأَعْلَمَهُمْ أَنَّهُ قَتَلَهُ فَإِنْ عَفَوْا عَنْهُ أَعْطَاهُمُ الدِّيَةَ وَ أَعْتَقَ رَقَبَةً وَ صَامَ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ وَ تَصَدَّقَ عَلَى سِتِّينَ مِسْكِيناً .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Husayn Bin Ahmad Al Minqary, from Isa Al Zareyr who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man kills a man deliberately, what is his repentance?’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should make himself available (to the guardians of the killed one)’. I said, ‘He is afraid that they might kill him’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So let him give them the wergild’. I said, ‘He is afraid that they would come to know (it was him) due to that’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So let him be secretive with the wergild, so let him make it as small packages, then place it during the Prayer timings (in their homes), so they can be with the wergild’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) رَجُلٌ قَتَلَ رَجُلًا مُتَعَمِّداً مَا تَوْبَتُهُ قَالَ يُمَكِّنُ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ قُلْتُ يَخَافُ أَنْ يَقْتُلُوهُ قَالَ فَلْيُعْطِهِمُ الدِّيَةَ قُلْتُ يَخَافُ أَنْ يَعْلَمُوا بِذَلِكَ قَالَ فَلْيَنْظُرْ إِلَى الدِّيَةِ فَلْيَجْعَلْهَا صُرَراً ثُمَّ لْيَنْظُرْ مَوَاقِيتَ الصَّلَوَاتِ فَلْيُلْقِهَا فِي دَارِهِمْ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Hadeed and Ibn Abu Umeyr, altogether from Jameel Bin Darraj, from one of his companions, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘The deliberate killing is all of what the strike is deliberated with, so upon him is the retaliation, and rather, the erroneous (killing) is that he intends the thing, so he hits another (person)’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When he confesses upon himself with the killing, he would be killed, and even if there does not happen to be a proof against him’.

citation.arabic_text: قَتْلُ الْعَمْدِ كُلُّ مَا عَمَدَ بِهِ الضَّرْبَ فَعَلَيْهِ الْقَوَدُ وَ إِنَّمَا الْخَطَأُ أَنْ يُرِيدَ الشَّيْ‏ءَ فَيُصِيبَ غَيْرَهُ وَ قَالَ إِذَا أَقَرَّ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ بِالْقَتْلِ قُتِلَ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَيْهِ بَيِّنَةٌ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from Al Halby who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The deliberation is all of what something is anticipated, so he hits it with an iron, or with a rock, or with a stick, or with a nudge, so all of these are deliberate; and the error is from anticipating something, so he hits something else’.

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) الْعَمْدُ كُلُّ مَا اعْتَمَدَ شَيْئاً فَأَصَابَهُ بِحَدِيدَةٍ أَوْ بِحَجَرٍ أَوْ بِعَصاً أَوْ بِوَكْزَةٍ فَهَذَا كُلُّهُ عَمْدٌ وَ الْخَطَأُ مَنِ اعْتَمَدَ شَيْئاً فَأَصَابَ غَيْرَهُ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Safwan and Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, altogether fro, Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Does Yahya Bin Saeed oppose your judges?’ I said, ‘Yes’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Give me something from what he differed in’. I said, ‘Two boys fought each other in the open, so one of them bit his companions. So the bitten one deliberated to pick up a stone, so he struck by it the head of his companion who had bitten him. So it split (his head), and (the wound) exacerbated, so he died. So that was raised to Yahya Bin Saeed, so he judged for the retaliation (revenge). So that was grievous upon Ibn Abu Layli, and Ibn Shabrama (other judges), and they spoke a lot with regards to it, and they said, ‘But rather, this is an error’. So Isa Bin Ali paid him from his own wealth’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘From our<sup>asws</sup> (judgement), let there be retaliation for the (fatal) wounding. But rather, the error is when he intended with something, so he hit something else’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Mhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kanany, both together, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, both said, ‘We asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who struck a man with a stick. text: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu nasr, from Musa Bin Bakr, (It has been narrated) from Abd Salih<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), regarding a man who struck a man with a stick, so he did not raise the stick (stop) until he died. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be handed over to the guardian of the killed one, but he should not be left to enjoy the pleasure of it, but the sword should be allowed upon him’.

citation.arabic_text: رَجُلٍ ضَرَبَ رَجُلًا بِعَصاً فَلَمْ يَرْفَعِ الْعَصَا حَتَّى مَاتَ قَالَ يُدْفَعُ إِلَى أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَقْتُولِ وَ لَكِنْ لَا يُتْرَكُ يُتَلَذَّذُ بِهِ وَ لَكِنْ يُجَازُ عَلَيْهِ بِالسَّيْفِ .

citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) لَوْ أَنَّ رَجُلًا ضَرَبَ رَجُلًا بِخَزَفَةٍ أَوْ بِآجُرَّةٍ أَوْ بِعُودٍ فَمَاتَ كَانَ عَمْداً .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Al A’ala Bin Al Fuzayl, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The deliberation is in which he strikes with the sword, or the stick (and) does not stop from it until he kills; and the error is in which he does not anticipate it (the killing)’.

citation.arabic_text: الْعَمْدُ الَّذِي يَضْرِبُ بِالسِّلَاحِ أَوِ الْعَصَا لَا يَقْلَعُ عَنْهُ حَتَّى يُقْتَلَ وَ الْخَطَأُ الَّذِي لَا يَتَعَمَّدُهُ .
citation.translation: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Al A’ala Bin Al Fuzayl, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘The deliberation is in which he strikes with the sword, or the stick (and) does not stop from it until he kills; and the error is in which he does not anticipate it (the killing)’.

text: Yunus, from one of his companions, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘If a man strikes a man with a stick, or with a rock, so he dies from his one strike before he speaks, so it is somewhat deliberate, therefore the wergild is upon the killer; and if he pounces upon him and hits him incessantly (nonstop) with the stick, or with the rock until he kills him, so he was deliberately killed with; and if he were to strike him with one strike, so he speaks, then remains (alive) for a day or more from (that) day, then dies, so it is somewhat deliberate’.

citation.arabic_text: إِنْ ضَرَبَ رَجُلٌ رَجُلًا بِعَصاً أَوْ بِحَجَرٍ فَمَاتَ مِنْ ضَرْبَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَتَكَلَّمَ فَهُوَ شِبْهُ الْعَمْدِ فَالدِّيَةُ عَلَى الْقَاتِلِ وَ إِنْ عَلَاهُ وَ أَلَحَّ عَلَيْهِ بِالْعَصَا أَوْ بِالْحِجَارَةِ حَتَّى يَقْتُلَهُ فَهُوَ عَمْدٌ يُقْتَلُ بِهِ وَ إِنْ ضَرَبَهُ ضَرْبَةً وَاحِدَةً فَتَكَلَّمَ ثُمَّ مَكَثَ يَوْماً أَوْ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ يَوْمٍ ثُمَّ مَاتَ فَهُوَ شِبْهُ الْعَمْدِ .
citation.translation: Yunus, from one of his companions, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said: ‘If a man strikes a man with a stick, or with a rock, so he dies from his one strike before he speaks, so it is somewhat deliberate, therefore the wergild is upon the killer; and if he pounces upon him and hits him incessantly (nonstop) with the stick, or with the rock until he kills him, so he was deliberately killed with; and if he were to strike him with one strike, so he speaks, then remains (alive) for a day or more from (that) day, then dies, so it is somewhat deliberate’.

text: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, both together from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abu Al Abbas, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I threw something at a man, the likes of which does not kill (but he dies)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is erroneous (killing)’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> picked up a small pebble, so he threw it. I said, ‘I threw it at the sheep but it hit a man?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is the error in which there is no doubt, and the deliberate is that which he strikes with something, the likes of which could kill’.

citation.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لَهُ أَرْمِي الرَّجُلَ بِالشَّيْ‏ءِ الَّذِي لَا يَقْتُلُ مِثْلُهُ قَالَ هَذَا خَطَأٌ ثُمَّ أَخَذَ حَصَاةً صَغِيرَةً فَرَمَى بِهَا قُلْتُ أَرْمِي بِهَا الشَّاةَ فَأَصَابَتْ رَجُلًا قَالَ هَذَا الْخَطَأُ الَّذِي لَا شَكَّ فِيهِ وَ الْعَمْدُ الَّذِي يَضْرِبُ بِالشَّيْ‏ءِ الَّذِي يُقْتَلُ بِمِثْلِهِ .

Then he<sup>asws</sup> picked up a small pebble, so he threw it. I said, ‘I threw it at the sheep but it hit a man?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is the error in which there is no doubt, and the deliberate is that which he strikes with something, the likes of which could kill’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, both together from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said, ‘I heard Ibn Abu Layli saying, ‘The wergild during the Pre-Islamic period was a hundred camels. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> accepted it. Then he<sup>asws</sup> necessitated upon the owner of the cows, (wergild of) two hundred cows, and upon the owners of the sheep (wergild of) a thousand sheep (or) male goats; and upon the owners of the gold (wergild of) a thousand Dinars; and upon owners of the currency, (a wergild) of ten thousand Dirhams; and upon the clothes merchants of Al-Yemen, a hundred garments’. Abdul Rahman Bin Al-Hajjaj (the narrator) said, ‘So I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about what Ibn Abu Layli is reporting, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘The wergild is a thousand Dinars, and the value of the Dinar is ten Dirhams, and a thousand Dirhams being for the people of the city, and upon the people of the valleys is the wergild of one hundred camels, and for the vast majority of the people (wergild of) two hundred cows, or a thousand sheep’.

citation.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ ابْنَ أَبِي لَيْلَى يَقُولُ كَانَتِ الدِّيَةُ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ مِائَةً مِنَ الْإِبِلِ فَأَقَرَّهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ( صلى الله عليه وآله ) ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ فَرَضَ عَلَى أَهْلِ الْبَقَرِ مِائَتَيْ بَقَرَةٍ وَ فَرَضَ عَلَى أَهْلِ الشَّاةِ أَلْفَ شَاةٍ ثَنِيَّةٍ وَ عَلَى أَهْلِ الذَّهَبِ أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ وَ عَلَى أَهْلِ الْوَرِقِ عَشَرَةَ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ وَ عَلَى أَهْلِ الْيَمَنِ الْحُلَلَ مِائَةَ حُلَّةٍ قَالَ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ الْحَجَّاجِ فَسَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) عَمَّا رَوَى ابْنُ أَبِي لَيْلَى فَقَالَ كَانَ عَلِيٌّ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ الدِّيَةُ أَلْفُ دِينَارٍ وَ قِيمَةُ الدِّينَارِ عَشَرَةُ دَرَاهِمَ وَ عَشَرَةُ آلَافِ [دِرْهَمٍ] لِأَهْلِ الْأَمْصَارِ وَ عَلَى أَهْلِ الْبَوَادِي الدِّيَةُ مِائَةٌ مِنَ الْإِبِلِ وَ لِأَهْلِ السَّوَادِ مِائَتَا بَقَرَةٍ أَوْ أَلْفُ شَاةٍ .

So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> accepted it. text: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Wergild of the erroneous (killing) when the man did not intend, is one hundred from the camels, or ten thousand (Dirhams) from the (owners of) the foliage, or a thousand from the sheep’. citation.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ( عليه السلام ) دِيَةُ الْخَطَإِ إِذَا لَمْ يُرِدِ الرَّجُلَ مِائَةٌ مِنَ الْإِبِلِ أَوْ عَشَرَةُ آلَافٍ مِنَ الْوَرِقِ أَوْ أَلْفٌ مِنَ الشَّاةِ وَ قَالَ دِيَةُ الْمُغَلَّظَةِ الَّتِي تُشْبِهُ الْعَمْدَ وَ لَيْسَ بِعَمْدٍ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ دِيَةِ الْخَطَإِ بِأَسْنَانِ الْإِبِلِ ثَلَاثٌ وَ ثَلَاثُونَ حِقَّةً وَ ثَلَاثٌ وَ ثَلَاثُونَ جَذَعَةً وَ أَرْبَعٌ وَ ثَلَاثُونَ ثَنِيَّةً كُلُّهَا طَرُوقَةُ الْفَحْلِ قَالَ وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الدِّيَةِ فَقَالَ دِيَةُ الْمُسْلِمِ عَشَرَةُ آلَافٍ مِنَ الْفِضَّةِ أَوْ أَلْفُ مِثْقَالٍ مِنَ الذَّهَبِ أَوْ أَلْفٌ مِنَ الشَّاةِ عَلَى أَسْنَانِهَا أَثْلَاثاً وَ مِنَ الْإِبِلِ مِائَةٌ عَلَى أَسْنَانِهَا وَ مِنَ الْبَقَرِ مِائَتَانِ .

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Al A’la Bin Al Fuzayl, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘With regards to the erroneous killing, it (wergild) is a hundred from the camels, or a thousand from the sheep, or ten thousand Dirhams, or a thousand Dinars. So if it was the camels, so twenty-five should be Ibnat Makhaz (two year old females), and twenty five Ibnat Laboun (three year old females), and twenty five Hiqqa (four year old females), and twenty five Jaz’a (five year old females). And the harsh wergild regarding the erroneous (killing) is that which resembles the deliberate which he struck with the rock, or with the stick, the single strike or two strikes not intending to kill him, so it is a third being thirty-three (four year old females), and thirty-three (five year old females), and thirty-four Saniyya (six year old females), all of these being capable of bearing the stallion (mount); and if it was from the sheep, so it is a thousand rams. And (as for) the deliberate (killing), it is the retaliation or (as per) the pleasure of the guardian of the killed one’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from one of our companions, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The one who kills a Believer deliberately, so he would be retaliated with (the same), except if the guardians of the killed one happy with accepting the wergild, or if he makes them to be pleased with more than the wergild, or less than the wergild. So if he were to do that between them, it is allowed, and if they were to retract (from accepting the wergild), it would be retaliation’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The wergild is ten thousand Dirhams, or a thousand Dinars, or one hundred from the camels’.

citation.arabic_text: مَنْ قَتَلَ مُؤْمِناً مُتَعَمِّداً فَإِنَّهُ يُقَادُ بِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ يَرْضَى أَوْلِيَاءُ الْمَقْتُولِ أَنْ يَقْبَلُوا الدِّيَةَ أَوْ يَتَرَاضَوْا بِأَكْثَرَ مِنَ الدِّيَةِ أَوْ أَقَلَّ مِنَ الدِّيَةِ فَإِنْ فَعَلُوا ذَلِكَ بَيْنَهُمْ جَازَ وَ إِنْ تَرَاجَعُوا أُقِيدُوا وَ قَالَ الدِّيَةُ عَشَرَةُ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ أَوْ أَلْفُ دِينَارٍ أَوْ مِائَةٌ مِنَ الْإِبِلِ .

text: Muhammad Bin Yahya from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim from his father, both together from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘You have to pay the wergild of the erroneous (killing) within three years, and you have to pay the wergild of the deliberate (killing) within one year’.

citation.arabic_text: كَانَ عَلِيٌّ ( عليه السلام ) يَقُولُ تُسْتَأْدَى دِيَةُ الْخَطَإِ فِي ثَلَاثِ سِنِينَ وَ تُسْتَأْدَى دِيَةُ الْعَمْدِ فِي سَنَةٍ .
citation.translation: Muhammad Bin Yahya from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim from his father, both together from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘You have to pay the wergild of the erroneous (killing) within three years, and you have to pay the wergild of the deliberate (killing) within one year’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad Bin Yahya from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, both together from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding ten (people) who participated in killing a man. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The family of the killed one can choose whichever one they so desire (from the ones who) killed, and his guardians has recourse to the remaining ones for nine-tenths of the wergild’.

citation.arabic_text: عَشَرَةٍ اشْتَرَكُوا فِي قَتْلِ رَجُلٍ قَالَ يُخَيَّرُ أَهْلُ الْمَقْتُولِ فَأَيَّهُمْ شَاءُوا قَتَلُوا وَ يَرْجِعُ أَوْلِيَاؤُهُ عَلَى الْبَاقِينَ بِتِسْعَةِ أَعْشَارِ الدِّيَةِ .

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The family of the killed one can choose whichever one they so desire (from the ones who) killed, and his guardians has recourse to the remaining ones for nine-tenths of the wergild’.

text: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding two men who both killed one man. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the guardians of the killed one intend to kill both of them, or they have to pay the complete wergild (of one person), and kill them both, and the wergild would happen to be between the guardians of the two who are executed. So if they were to intend to execute one of the two, so they can kill him and the remaining one has to pay half the wergild to the family of the executed one; and if they do not want the payment of the wergild of one of the two and they do not kill any one of the two, the guardian of the killed (one) can accept the (half) wergild from each of the two’.

citation.arabic_text: رَجُلَيْنِ قَتَلَا رَجُلًا قَالَ إِنْ أَرَادَ أَوْلِيَاءُ الْمَقْتُولِ قَتْلَهُمَا أَدَّوْا دِيَةً كَامِلَةً وَ قَتَلُوهُمَا وَ تَكُونُ الدِّيَةُ بَيْنَ أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَقْتُولَيْنِ فَإِنْ أَرَادُوا قَتْلَ أَحَدِهِمَا فَقَتَلُوهُ أَدَّى الْمَتْرُوكُ نِصْفَ الدِّيَةِ إِلَى أَهْلِ الْمَقْتُولِ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يُؤَدِّ دِيَةَ أَحَدِهِمَا وَ لَمْ يَقْتُلْ أَحَدَهُمَا قَبِلَ الدِّيَةَ صَاحِبُهُ مِنْ كِلَيْهِمَا .
